title.en: Volume 71 Biographies 59: The Sui Imperial Family
title.raw: 卷七十一 列傳第五十九: 隋宗室諸王 Volume 71 Biographies 59: The Sui Imperial Family

sentences.zh: 隋宗室諸王

translations.literal: Princes of the Sui Imperial Clan
translations.idiomatic: The Sui Imperial Clan Princes

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十九隋宗室諸王

translations.literal: Biography 59: Princes of the Sui Imperial Clan
translations.idiomatic: Biography 59 — The Sui Imperial Clan Princes

sentences.zh: 蔡景王整滕穆王瓚道宣王嵩衛昭王爽河間王弘義城公處綱離石太守子崇文帝四王煬帝三子

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Cai Zheng, Prince Mu of Teng Zan, Prince Xuan of Dao Song, Prince Zhao of Wei Shuang, Prince of Hejian Hong, Duke of Yicheng Chugang, Zichong Administrator of Lishi, four princes of Emperor Wen, three sons of Emperor Yang
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing of Cai, Zheng; Prince Mu of Teng, Zan; Prince Xuan of Dao, Song; Prince Zhao of Wei, Shuang; Prince of Hejian, Hong; Duke of Yicheng, Chugang; Zichong, Administrator of Lishi; the four princes of Emperor Wen; and the three sons of Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 蔡景王整，隋文帝之次弟也。

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Cai, Zheng, was the second younger brother of Emperor Wen of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing of Cai, Zheng, was Emperor Wen of Sui's next younger brother.

sentences.zh: 文帝四弟，唯整及滕穆王瓚與帝同生，次道宣王嵩，次衛昭王爽並異母。

translations.literal: Among the four younger brothers of Emperor Wen, only Zheng and Prince Mu of Teng, Zan, were born of the same mother as the Emperor; next came Prince Xuan of Dao, Song, and next Prince Zhao of Wei, Shuang — all by different mothers.
translations.idiomatic: Of Emperor Wen's four younger brothers, only Zheng and Prince Mu of Teng, Zan shared his mother; Prince Xuan of Dao, Song, and Prince Zhao of Wei, Shuang followed, each born to a different mother.

sentences.zh: 整，周明帝時以武元軍功，賜爵陳留郡公。

translations.literal: Zheng, during the reign of Emperor Ming of Zhou, for the military merit of Empress Dowager Wu, was granted the title Duke of Chenliu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Ming of Northern Zhou, Zheng was ennobled as Duke of Chenliu Commandery for service linked to Empress Dowager Wu's faction.

sentences.zh: 位開府、車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: He held the offices of Defender-in-Chief and General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Defender-in-Chief and General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu in the conquest of Qi.

sentences.zh: 力戰而死。

translations.literal: He fought fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought to the end and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 文帝初居武元之憂，率諸弟負土為墳，人植一栢，四根鬱茂，西北一根整栽者獨黃。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was first in mourning for Empress Dowager Wu, he led his brothers in carrying earth to build the tomb; each man planted one cypress, and the four roots grew lush together, but the northwestern tree that Zheng had planted alone turned yellow.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wen was still in mourning for Empress Dowager Wu, he and his brothers carried earth to raise her tomb, each planting a cypress. All four trees flourished, yet the one Zheng had set in the northwest alone turned yellow.

sentences.zh: 後因大風雨，並根失之，果終不吉。

translations.literal: Later, in a great wind and rain, all the roots were lost, and in the end the omen indeed proved ill.
translations.idiomatic: Later a violent storm uprooted them all — an omen that, as it turned out, foretold ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 文帝作相，贈柱國、大司徒、八州剌史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen became Chancellor, [Zheng] was posthumously honored as Pillar of State, Grand Minister of Education, and Inspector of eight provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen became regent, Zheng was posthumously honored as Pillar of State, Grand Minister of Education, and inspector over eight provinces.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，追封諡焉。

translations.literal: When [Wen] received the abdication, he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed and given his temple name and title.

sentences.zh: 子智積襲。

translations.literal: His son Zhiji succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhiji inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 又封其弟智明為高陽郡公，智才開封縣公。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Zhiming and Zhicai were also enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyang Commandery and Duke of Kaifeng County respectively.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Zhiming and Zhicai were enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyang Commandery and Duke of Kaifeng County.

sentences.zh: 尋拜智積開府儀同三司，授同州刺史，儀衛資送甚盛。

translations.literal: Soon Zhiji was appointed Defender-in-Chief with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes and made Governor of Tong Province, with very lavish guard and supplies sent with him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhiji was made Defender-in-Chief with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes and appointed governor of Tong Province, with an unusually grand escort and provision.

sentences.zh: 整娶同郡尉遲綱女，生智積。

translations.literal: Zheng married a daughter of Yuchi Gang of the same commandery, who bore Zhiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng married a daughter of Yuchi Gang of the same commandery; she bore Zhiji.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，有司奏智積將葬尉太妃，帝曰：「昔幾殺我。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era, the authorities reported that Zhiji was about to bury Grand Consort Wei of the Yuchi clan. The Emperor said: "She nearly killed me once.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang reign, officials reported that Zhiji was preparing to bury Grand Consort Wei of the Yuchi clan. The Emperor said, "She once came close to killing me.

sentences.zh: 我有同生二弟，並倚婦家勢，常憎疾我。

translations.literal: I had two younger brothers of the same mother who both relied on their wives' families' power and always resented me.
translations.idiomatic: I had two full brothers who leaned on their wives' families and always bore me ill will.

sentences.zh: 我向之笑云：'爾既嗔我，不可與爾角嗔。

translations.literal: I once said to them with a laugh: 'Since you are angry with me, I cannot compete with you in anger.
translations.idiomatic: I told them with a laugh, 'Since you resent me, I will not quarrel with you on your terms.

sentences.zh: '並云：'阿兄止倚頭額。

translations.literal: ' They both said: 'Elder brother only relies on his forehead.'
translations.idiomatic: ' They answered, 'Our elder brother has nothing but his brow to boast of.'

sentences.zh: '時有醫師邊隱逐勢，言我後百日當病癲。

translations.literal: ' At the time a physician named Bian Yin, courting their favor, said I would fall ill with madness within a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: ' A physician named Bian Yin, currying favor with them, declared that within a hundred days I would go mad.

sentences.zh: 二弟私喜。

translations.literal: The two brothers rejoiced in private.
translations.idiomatic: My two brothers rejoiced in secret.

sentences.zh: 以告父母。

translations.literal: They told our parents.
translations.idiomatic: They told our parents.

sentences.zh: 父母泣謂我曰：'爾二弟大劇，不能愛兄。

translations.literal: Our parents wept and said to me: 'Your two brothers are too harsh and cannot love their elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Our parents wept and said to me, 'Your two brothers are cruel beyond measure; they cannot love their elder brother.

sentences.zh: '我因言：'一日有天下，當改其姓。

translations.literal: ' I then said: 'If one day I possess the realm, I shall change their surname.
translations.idiomatic: ' I replied, 'If I ever win the realm, I shall change their surname.

sentences.zh: 夫不受其親而愛他人者，謂之悖德，當改之為悖。

translations.literal: One who does not accept his kin yet loves others is called perverse in virtue; their name should be changed to Bei [Perversity].
translations.idiomatic: Those who reject their own kin to favor outsiders are called perverse in virtue — I would change their name to Bei, "perversity."

sentences.zh: '父母許我此言。

translations.literal: ' Our parents granted me this saying.
translations.idiomatic: ' Our parents assented.

sentences.zh: 父母亡後，二弟及婦又讒我，言于晉公。

translations.literal: After our parents died, the two brothers and their wives slandered me again, speaking to the Duke of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: After our parents died, my brothers and their wives slandered me again, reporting to the Duke of Jin.

sentences.zh: 于時每還，欲入門，常不喜，如見獄門。

translations.literal: Whenever I returned then and was about to enter the gate, I was never pleased — it was like seeing the gate of a prison.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I came home then, I dreaded crossing the threshold; it felt like entering a jail.

sentences.zh: 托以患氣，常鎖閤靜坐，唯食至時暫開閤。

translations.literal: Pleading illness of the vital breath, I constantly locked my doors and sat in stillness, opening them only briefly at mealtimes.
translations.idiomatic: I pleaded ill health, kept my doors bolted, and sat in seclusion, opening them only when food was brought.

sentences.zh: 每飛言入耳，竊雲'復未邪？

translations.literal: Whenever slander reached my ears, I would mutter to myself, 'Not yet again?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever fresh slander reached me, I would mutter, 'Again? Not yet done?

sentences.zh: '當時實不可耐，羨人無兄弟。

translations.literal: ' At the time it was truly unbearable; I envied those without brothers.
translations.idiomatic: ' It was truly unbearable; I envied men who had no brothers.

sentences.zh: 世間貧家兄弟多相愛，由相假藉；

translations.literal: In the world, brothers in poor families often love one another, because they rely on each other;
translations.idiomatic: Poor brothers often love one another, because they must lean on each other;

sentences.zh: 達官兄弟多相憎，爭名利故也。」

translations.literal: brothers among high officials often hate one another, because they contend for fame and profit."
translations.idiomatic: while brothers among the great often hate one another, because they compete for fame and gain."

sentences.zh: 智積在同州，未嘗嬉戲遊獵，聽政之暇，端坐讀書。

translations.literal: Zhiji, in Tong Province, never played games or went hunting; in the intervals of hearing cases, he sat upright reading books.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Province Zhiji never idled in sport or the hunt; between sessions of government he sat upright with his books.

sentences.zh: 門無私謁。

translations.literal: At his gate there were no private callers.
translations.idiomatic: No private petitioners came to his gate.

sentences.zh: 有侍讀公孫尚義，山東儒士，府佐楊君英、蕭德言，並有文學，時延於坐。

translations.literal: He had a lecturing attendant, Gongsun Shangyi, a Confucian scholar of Shandong, and staff members Yang Junying and Xiao Deyan, all men of literary accomplishment, whom he would invite to his seat from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: His lecturing attendant Gongsun Shangyi was a Shandong scholar; his aides Yang Junying and Xiao Deyan were also learned men, and he would invite them to sit with him.

sentences.zh: 所設唯餅果，酒才三酌。

translations.literal: What he set out was only cakes and fruit; wine amounted to only three rounds.
translations.idiomatic: He served only cakes and fruit, and wine no more than three rounds.

sentences.zh: 家有女妓，唯年節嘉慶奏於太妃前。

translations.literal: He had female entertainers in the household, but they performed only at New Year and festive occasions before the Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Though he kept female musicians, they performed only at holidays and celebrations, and only before the Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 始，文帝龍潛時，與景王不睦，太妃尉氏又與獨孤皇后不相諧，以是智積常懷危懼，每自貶損。

translations.literal: From the beginning, when Emperor Wen was still in obscurity, he was not on good terms with Prince Jing, and Grand Consort Wei of the Yuchi clan was also at odds with Empress Dugu; for this reason Zhiji constantly harbored fear and always humbled himself.
translations.idiomatic: From the days when Emperor Wen was still only heir apparent, he had been at odds with Prince Jing, and Grand Consort Wei of the Yuchi clan had quarreled with Empress Dugu; Zhiji therefore lived in constant fear and kept himself abased.

sentences.zh: 帝亦以是哀憐之。

translations.literal: The Emperor also pitied him for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pitied him for the same reason.

sentences.zh: 人或勸智積為產業，智積曰：「昔平原露朽財帛，苦其多也。

translations.literal: Some urged Zhiji to build up estates. Zhiji said: "In former times the plains exposed rotting wealth in silk and coin, and suffered because there was too much.
translations.idiomatic: When others urged Zhiji to amass property, he said, "Long ago on the plains wealth lay rotting in the open — men suffered because they had too much.

sentences.zh: 吾幸無可露，何更營乎！

translations.literal: I am fortunate to have nothing to expose to the open — why should I scheme further!
translations.idiomatic: I am fortunate to have nothing worth exposing — why should I scheme for more?

sentences.zh: 」有五男，止教讀《論語》、《孝經》而已，亦不令交通賓客。

translations.literal: " He had five sons and taught them only to read the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety; he also did not allow them to associate with guests.
translations.idiomatic: " He had five sons and taught them only the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety, and would not let them cultivate ties with guests.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，智積曰：「恐兒子有才能以致禍也。

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Zhiji said: "I fear that if my sons have talent, it will bring disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Zhiji said, "I fear that if my sons show talent, it will bring disaster upon them.

sentences.zh: 」開皇二十年，徵還京，無他職任，闔門自守，非朝覲不出。

translations.literal: " In the twentieth year of Kaihuang he was summoned back to the capital, given no other office, and kept his household to itself, not going out except for court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twentieth year of Kaihuang he was recalled to the capital, given no further appointment, and kept his household shut in, leaving home only for court audiences.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，滕王綸、衛王集並以讒構得罪，高陽公智明亦以交通奪爵，智積愈懼。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Prince of Teng Lun and Prince of Wei Ji both suffered punishment through slander and intrigue, and Duke of Gaoyang Zhiming also lost his title for illicit associations; Zhiji grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Prince of Teng Lun and Prince of Wei Ji were ruined by slander, and Duke of Gaoyang Zhiming lost his title for illicit associations; Zhiji's fear deepened.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，授弘農太守，委政僚佐，清靜自居。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye he was appointed Administrator of Hongnong, entrusted government to his staff, and dwelt in quietude.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye he was made administrator of Hongnong, left affairs to his staff, and lived in quiet seclusion.

sentences.zh: 及楊玄感作逆，自東都引軍而西，智積謂官屬曰：「玄感欲西圖關中，若成其計，則根本固矣。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled and led his army west from the Eastern Capital, Zhiji said to his officials: "Xuangan wishes to march west and seize Guanzhong; if he carries out this plan, his foundation will be secure.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled and marched west from the Eastern Capital, Zhiji told his staff, "Xuangan means to strike west for Guanzhong; if he succeeds, his base will be secure.

sentences.zh: 當以計縻之，使不得進。

translations.literal: We should use a stratagem to tie him down so that he cannot advance.
translations.idiomatic: We must use a stratagem to hold him here and keep him from advancing.

sentences.zh: 不出一旬，自可禽耳。

translations.literal: Within ten days he can naturally be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he can be taken without fail.

sentences.zh: '及玄感軍至城下，智積登陴詈辱之，玄感怒甚，留攻之。

translations.literal: ' When Xuangan's army reached the foot of the wall, Zhiji mounted the ramparts and reviled him; Xuangan was greatly enraged and remained to attack.
translations.idiomatic: ' When Xuangan's army reached the walls, Zhiji mounted the battlements and hurled abuse at him; enraged, Xuangan halted to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 城門為賊所燒，智積乃更益火，賊不得入。

translations.literal: The city gate was burned by the rebels; Zhiji then added more fire, and the rebels could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels burned the gate, Zhiji fed the flames until the breach could not be crossed.

sentences.zh: 數日，宇文述等軍至，合擊破之。

translations.literal: After several days the armies of Yuwen Shu and others arrived and together struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the armies of Yuwen Shu and others arrived and destroyed the rebels in a joint attack.

sentences.zh: 尋拜宗正卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從駕江都，寢疾。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed the imperial progress to Jiangdu and fell ill in bed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he accompanied the court to Jiangdu and fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 帝時疏薄骨肉，智積每不自安，及遇患，不呼醫。

translations.literal: The Emperor at that time was cold toward his kin, and Zhiji was never at ease; when he fell ill, he did not summon physicians.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had grown cold toward his kin, and Zhiji was never at ease; when illness came, he refused to call a physician.

sentences.zh: 臨終，謂所親曰：「吾今日始知得保首領沒于地矣！

translations.literal: At the end he said to those close to him: "Only today do I know that I have been able to keep my head and die in the earth!
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told those near him, "Only today do I know I have kept my head and may die in peace upon the earth!

sentences.zh: 」時人哀之。

translations.literal: " People of the time pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: " Men of the time mourned him.

sentences.zh: 有子道玄。

translations.literal: He had a son Daoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son, Daoxuan.

sentences.zh: 宣帝崩，文帝入禁中，將總朝政，令廢太子勇召之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Emperor Wen entered the inner palace and was about to take overall control of court affairs; he ordered that the deposed Crown Prince Yong be summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou died, Emperor Wen entered the inner palace to seize control of government and ordered the deposed Crown Prince Yong summoned.

sentences.zh: 瓚素與帝不協，不從，曰：「作隋國公恐不能保，何乃更為族滅事邪！

translations.literal: Zan had long been at odds with the Emperor and would not obey, saying: "As Duke of Sui one probably cannot even preserve oneself — why undertake a matter that will exterminate the clan!
translations.idiomatic: Zan, who had long been at odds with his brother, refused, saying, "As Duke of Sui you can scarcely save yourself — why court extermination for the whole clan?

sentences.zh: 」文帝作相，拜大宗伯，典修禮律，進位上柱國、邵國公。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Wen became Chancellor, [Zan] was appointed Grand Director of Ceremonies, put in charge of revising ritual and law, and advanced to Upper Pillar of State and Duke of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: " When Wen became regent, Zan was made Grand Director of Ceremonies, charged with ritual and penal codes, and promoted to Upper Pillar of State and Duke of Shao.

sentences.zh: 瓚見帝執政，恐為家禍，陰有圖帝計，帝每優容之。

translations.literal: Zan saw the Emperor wield power and feared calamity for the family; secretly he had designs against the Emperor, but the Emperor always treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his brother in power, Zan feared disaster for the house and secretly plotted against him, yet the Emperor always treated him with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，立為滕王，拜雍州牧。

translations.literal: When [Wen] received the abdication, [Zan] was established as Prince of Teng and appointed Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen took the throne, Zan was created Prince of Teng and made governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 帝數與同坐，呼為阿三。

translations.literal: The Emperor often sat with him together and called him "Little Third."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often sat with him and called him "Little Third."

sentences.zh: 後坐事去牧，以王就第。

translations.literal: Later, because of an offense, he was removed from the governorship and lived at his princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after an offense, he was removed from office and retired to his princely mansion.

sentences.zh: 瓚妃宇文氏，素與獨孤皇后不平，至是鬱鬱不得志，陰有咒詛。

translations.literal: Zan's consort, of the Yuwen clan, had long been at odds with Empress Dugu; by this time she was depressed and unfulfilled and secretly practiced curses.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's consort of the Yuwen clan had long quarreled with Empress Dugu; now bitter and thwarted, she secretly practiced curses.

sentences.zh: 帝命瓚出之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Zan to send her away.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Zan to divorce her.

sentences.zh: 瓚不忍離絕，固請。

translations.literal: Zan could not bear to part from her and firmly pleaded.
translations.idiomatic: Zan could not bear to cast her off and pleaded stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，從之，宇文氏竟除屬籍。

translations.literal: The Emperor, having no choice, consented, but the Yuwen lady was ultimately struck from the clan registers.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor reluctantly yielded, yet the Yuwen lady was ultimately struck from the clan registers.

sentences.zh: 由是恩禮更薄。

translations.literal: From this his favor and ceremonial treatment grew still thinner.
translations.idiomatic: From then on imperial favor toward him grew still colder.

sentences.zh: 開皇十一年，從幸栗園，坐樹下，方飲酒，鼻忽流血，暴薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kaihuang, while accompanying the Emperor to Liyuan Garden, he sat under a tree drinking wine when blood suddenly flowed from his nose and he died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Kaihuang, while accompanying the Emperor to Chestnut Garden, he sat drinking under a tree when blood suddenly poured from his nose and he died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 時年四十四。

translations.literal: He was forty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-four.

sentences.zh: 人皆以為遇鳩。

translations.literal: People all believed he had met with poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone believed he had been poisoned.

sentences.zh: 子綸嗣。

translations.literal: His son Lun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 綸字斌褵，性弘厚，美姿容，頗知鐘律。

translations.literal: Lun, style name Binli, was by nature magnanimous and generous, handsome in appearance, and fairly versed in bells and pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Lun, courtesy name Binli, was open-hearted and handsome, with a fair knowledge of music and pitch.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，封邵國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, [Lun] was enfeoffed as Duke of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Lun was enfeoffed as Duke of Shao.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜邵州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Governor of Shao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed governor of Shao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣納妃于梁，詔綸致禮，甚為梁人所敬。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin Guang took a consort in Liang, an edict ordered Lun to present the ceremonial gifts; he was greatly respected by the people of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jin Guang took a bride from Liang, Lun was ordered to convey the betrothal gifts and won great respect among the Liang court.

sentences.zh: 綸以穆王故，當文帝世，每不自安。

translations.literal: Because of Prince Mu, during the reign of Emperor Wen Lun was never at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his father Prince Mu's fate, Lun never felt secure under Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，尤被猜忌。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was especially suspected.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang he was watched with especial suspicion.

sentences.zh: 綸憂懼，呼術者王琛問之。

translations.literal: Lun, anxious and afraid, summoned the diviner Wang Chen and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful, Lun summoned the diviner Wang Chen.

sentences.zh: 琛答曰：「王相祿不凡。

translations.literal: Chen replied: "Your princely physiognomy and emolument are not ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Chen answered, "Your princely countenance and fortune are no common lot.

sentences.zh: 滕即騰也，此字足為善應。

translations.literal: Teng [Ascent] is the same as teng [soaring]; this character is quite sufficient as a good omen."
translations.idiomatic: Teng, 'Ascent,' is the same word as teng, 'to soar' — the name itself is an excellent omen."

sentences.zh: 」有沙門惠恩、崛多等，頗解占候，綸每與交通，嘗令些三人為厭勝法。

translations.literal: " There were monks Huian, Jueduo, and others fairly skilled in divination and portents. Lun frequently associated with them and once had these three men perform rites of occult suppression.
translations.idiomatic: There were monks Huian, Jueduo, and others skilled in divination. Lun frequently associated with them and once had three of them perform rites of occult counter-magic.

sentences.zh: 有人告綸怨望呪詛，帝令黃門侍郎王弘窮驗之。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Lun harbored resentment and practiced curses; the Emperor ordered Yellow Gate Attendant Wang Hong to investigate thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: When someone accused Lun of resentment and curses, the Emperor ordered Yellow Gate Attendant Wang Hong to investigate.

sentences.zh: 弘希旨奏綸厭蠱惡逆，坐當死。

translations.literal: Hong, reading the Emperor's intent, memorialized that Lun had practiced occult suppression and sorcery constituting wicked rebellion, the crime for which he deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, reading the Emperor's wish, reported that Lun had practiced sorcery and treason, crimes warranting death.

sentences.zh: 帝令卿議之，司徒楊素等曰：「綸懷惡之由，積自家世。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the ministers to deliberate. Minister of Education Yang Su and others said: "The source of Lun's harbored evil lies accumulated from his own family for generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the high ministers to deliberate. Minister of Education Yang Su and others said, "The roots of Lun's malice lie in generations of his house.

sentences.zh: 惟皇運之始，四海同心，在於孔懷，彌須協力。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the imperial fortune, when the four seas were of one mind, among those of the same womb one must all the more join in effort.
translations.idiomatic: At the dawn of the dynasty, when the realm was united, those of the same womb ought all the more to stand together.

sentences.zh: 其先乃離阻大謀，棄同即異。

translations.literal: His forebears turned away from the great plan, abandoned kinship and took the alien side.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears turned from the great design, forsaking kin for the alien cause.

sentences.zh: 父悖于前，子逆於後，為惡有將，其罪莫大。

translations.literal: The father was perverse before, the son rebellious after; when evil has its harbinger, the crime is greatest.
translations.idiomatic: The father was perverse before him, the son rebellious after — evil that runs in a line merits the gravest penalty.

sentences.zh: 請依前科。

translations.literal: We request application of the former statute.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the statute be applied as before.

sentences.zh: 」帝以皇族不忍，除名徙邊郡。

translations.literal: " The Emperor, unable to bear it as one of the imperial clan, struck his name [from the registers] and banished him to a frontier commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor, unwilling to shed imperial blood, struck his name from the registers and banished him to a frontier commandery.

sentences.zh: 大業七年，帝征遼東，綸欲上表，請從軍自效，為郡司所遏。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daye the Emperor campaigned against Liaodong; Lun wished to submit a memorial asking to follow the army and offer his service, but was blocked by the commandery officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daye, when the Emperor campaigned against Liaodong, Lun tried to memorialize offering to serve in the army, but local officials stopped him.

sentences.zh: 示幾，徙珠崖。

translations.literal: As a warning, he was relocated to Zhuya.
translations.idiomatic: As a warning, he was exiled to Zhuya.

sentences.zh: 及天下大亂，為賊林仕弘逼，攜妻子竄儋耳。

translations.literal: When the realm fell into great disorder, he was pressed by the bandit Lin Shihong and fled with wife and children to Dan'er.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire collapsed into chaos, the rebel Lin Shihong pressed him, and he fled with his family to Dan'er.

sentences.zh: 後歸國，封懷化縣公。

translations.literal: Later he returned to the state and was enfeoffed as Duke of Huaihua County.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned to court and was enfeoffed as Duke of Huaihua County.

sentences.zh: 尋病卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 綸弟坦，字文褵，初封竟陵郡公，坐綸徙長沙。

translations.literal: Lun's younger brother Tan, style name Wenli, was at first enfeoffed as Duke of Jingling Commandery; because of [association with] Lun he was relocated to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's younger brother Tan, styled Wenli, was initially made Duke of Jingling Commandery, but was exiled to Changsha on account of Lun's crime.

sentences.zh: 坦弟猛，字武褵，徙衡山。

translations.literal: Tan's younger brother Meng, style name Wuli, was relocated to Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's younger brother Meng, styled Wuli, was exiled to Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 猛弟溫，字明褵，初徙零陵。

translations.literal: Meng's younger brother Wen, style name Mingli, was at first relocated to Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Meng's younger brother Wen, styled Mingli, was first sent into exile at Lingling.

sentences.zh: 溫好學，解屬文，既而作《零陵賦》以自寄，其詞哀思。

translations.literal: Wen loved learning and was skilled at literary composition; afterward he wrote "Rhapsody on Lingling" to express himself, its language full of sorrowful thought.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was studious and skilled in writing. He later composed the "Rhapsody on Lingling" to give voice to his feelings; its language was deeply mournful.

sentences.zh: 帝見而怒之，轉徙南海。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw it and was angered, and had him further relocated to Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor read it he was enraged and had Wen banished further to Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 溫弟詵，字弘褵，前亦徙零陵。

translations.literal: Wen's younger brother Shen, style name Hongli, had earlier also been relocated to Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's younger brother Shen, styled Hongli, had earlier been exiled to Lingling as well.

sentences.zh: 帝以其修謹，襲封滕王，以奉穆王嗣。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because of his cultivated prudence, enfeoffed him as Prince of Teng to continue Prince Mu's line.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his refined and careful conduct, the Emperor made him Prince of Teng to maintain Prince Mu's succession.

sentences.zh: 大業末，于江都為宇文化及所害。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, at Jiangdu he was killed by Yuwen Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Daye he was killed by Yuwen Huaji at Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 道宣王嵩，在周以武元軍功，賜爵興城公。

translations.literal: Prince Daoxuan Song, in Zhou for military merit under Emperor Wu, was granted the title Duke of Xingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daoxuan Song earned military distinction under Emperor Wu of Zhou and was granted the title Duke of Xingcheng.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，追封諡焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 以滕穆王瓚子靜襲。

translations.literal: Prince Jing, son of Prince Mu of Teng Zan, succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing, son of Prince Mu of Teng Zan, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰悼。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous name was Dao.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was given the posthumous name Dao.

sentences.zh: 無子，以蔡王智積子世澄襲。

translations.literal: Having no son, Shicheng, son of Prince of Cai Zhiji, succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son, so Shicheng, son of Prince of Cai Zhiji, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 衛昭王爽，字師仁，小字明達。

translations.literal: Prince Zhaohui of Wei Shuang, style name Shiren, courtesy name Mingda.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhaohui of Wei, Shuang, styled Shiren and known familiarly as Mingda.

sentences.zh: 在周以武元軍功，于繈褓中封同安郡公。

translations.literal: In Zhou, for military merit under Emperor Wu, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Tong'an Commandery while still in swaddling clothes.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou he was made Duke of Tong'an Commandery in infancy for his father's service under Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 六歲而武元崩，為獻皇后所養，由是寵愛特異諸弟。

translations.literal: At six years of age Emperor Wu died; he was raised by Empress Xian, and because of this received favor and love exceeding his [other] brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When he was six, Emperor Wu died. Empress Xian raised him, and from then on he was favored above his brothers.

sentences.zh: 年十七，為內史上大夫。

translations.literal: At age seventeen he became Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文帝執政，授蒲州刺史、柱國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen held power, he was appointed Governor of Puzhou and Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wen directed affairs of state, Shuang was made Governor of Puzhou and Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，立為衛王，所生李氏為太妃。

translations.literal: When [the Emperor] received the abdication, [Shuang] was established as Prince of Wei, and his birth mother Lady Li was made Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne passed to Emperor Wen, Shuang was made Prince of Wei and his birth mother Lady Li was made Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 爽位雍州牧、右領軍大將軍、權領并州總管、上柱國、涼州總管。

translations.literal: Shuang held the posts of Governor of Yongzhou, Great General of the Right Palace Guard, provisional Commander-in-Chief of Bingzhou, Senior Pillar of State, and Commander-in-Chief of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang served as Governor of Yongzhou, Great General of the Right Palace Guard, acting Commander-in-Chief of Bingzhou, Senior Pillar of State, and Commander-in-Chief of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 爽美風儀，有器局，政甚有聲。

translations.literal: Shuang had handsome bearing and breadth of mind; his governance was highly regarded.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was imposing in appearance and broad-minded; his administration won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 大軍北伐，河間王弘、豆盧勣、竇榮定、高熲、虞慶則等分道而進，以爽為元帥，俱受爽節度。

translations.literal: When the great army marched north, Prince of Hejian Hong, Doulu Ji, Dou Rongding, Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, and others advanced by separate routes; Shuang was made supreme commander, and all received Shuang's regulation.
translations.idiomatic: On the great northern campaign, Prince of Hejian Hong, Doulu Ji, Dou Rongding, Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, and others marched on separate routes with Shuang as supreme commander, all under his command.

sentences.zh: 親率李充等四將出朔州，遇沙缽略可汗于白道，接戰，大破之，沙缽略中重瘡而遁。

translations.literal: Personally leading four generals including Li Chong out from Shuozhou, he encountered Shabolüe Qaghan at Baidao, joined battle, and routed him; Shabolüe was struck by a grievous wound and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Leading four generals including Li Chong from Shuozhou, he met Shabolüe Qaghan at Baidao, engaged him in battle, and inflicted a crushing defeat; Shabolüe suffered a serious wound and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜爽真食梁安縣千戶。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and granted Shuang permanent fief income from one thousand households of Liang'an County.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted and granted Shuang a permanent income from one thousand households in Liang'an County.

sentences.zh: 六年，復為元帥，步騎十五萬出合川，突厥遁逃。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again served as supreme commander; with one hundred fifty thousand infantry and cavalry he marched out from Hechuan, and the Turks fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he again served as supreme commander, leading one hundred fifty thousand foot and horse soldiers out of Hechuan; the Turks fled without fighting.

sentences.zh: 徵為納言。

translations.literal: He was summoned [to court] and made Chief Talker.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court and appointed Chief Talker.

sentences.zh: 帝甚重之。

translations.literal: The Emperor valued him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 未幾，爽疾，帝使薛榮宗視之，雲眾鬼為厲。

translations.literal: Before long Shuang fell ill; the Emperor sent Xue Rongzong to visit him, who reported that many ghosts were afflicting him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shuang fell ill. The Emperor sent Xue Rongzong to see him; Rongzong reported that a host of ghosts were tormenting him.

sentences.zh: 爽令左右驅逐之。

translations.literal: Shuang ordered his attendants to drive them away.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang ordered his attendants to drive the spirits away.

sentences.zh: 居數日，有鬼物來擊榮宗，走下階而斃。

translations.literal: After several days ghostly things came and struck Rongzong; he went down the steps and died.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later ghostly beings attacked Rongzong; he fled down the steps and collapsed dead.

sentences.zh: 其夜爽薨，年二十五。

translations.literal: That same night Shuang died; he was twenty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: That same night Shuang died at the age of twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Commandant and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 子集嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ji succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 河間王弘，字辟惡，文帝從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Hong, style name Pie'e, was a younger cousin of Emperor Wen on the paternal side.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hejian Hong, styled Pie'e, was Emperor Wen's younger paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 祖愛敬，早卒。

translations.literal: His grandfather Aijing died early.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Aijing died young.

sentences.zh: 父元孫，少孤，隨母郭氏養于舅族。

translations.literal: His father Yuansun, orphaned young, was raised among his maternal uncle's clan following his mother Lady Guo.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuansun lost his father early and was brought up in his maternal uncle's household with his mother Lady Guo.

sentences.zh: 及武元帝與周文建義關中，元孫時在鄴，懼為齊人所誅，因假外家姓為郭氏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu and Zhou Wen raised righteous rebellion in Guanzhong, Yuansun was then in Ye; fearing execution by the people of Qi, he therefore adopted his maternal clan's surname and became Guo.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu and Zhou Wen raised their rebellion in Guanzhong, Yuansun was in Ye. Fearing death at the hands of the Qi, he took his maternal family's surname, Guo.

sentences.zh: 元孫死，齊為周滅，弘始入關。

translations.literal: Yuansun died; when Qi was destroyed by Zhou, Hong first entered the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuansun died and Qi fell to Zhou, Hong entered Guanzhong for the first time.

sentences.zh: 與文帝相得，帝哀之，為買田宅。

translations.literal: He and Emperor Wen got along well; the Emperor pitied him and bought fields and a residence for him.
translations.idiomatic: He and Emperor Wen became close; the Emperor took pity on him and bought him fields and a house.

sentences.zh: 慶傾曲善候時變。

translations.literal: Qing was ingratiating and servile, skilled at watching for changes in the times.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was supple and obsequious, adept at reading the shifting times.

sentences.zh: 帝猜忌骨肉，滕王綸等皆被廢放，唯慶獲全。

translations.literal: The Emperor was suspicious of his kinsmen; Prince of Teng Lun and others were all deposed and banished, but only Qing escaped intact.
translations.idiomatic: As the Emperor grew suspicious of his own kin, Prince of Teng Lun and others were all deposed and exiled, yet Qing alone was spared.

sentences.zh: 累遷滎陽太守，頗有政績。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Prefect of Xingyang and had considerable administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Rising through the ranks to Prefect of Xingyang, he compiled a solid record of governance.

sentences.zh: 及李密據洛口倉。

translations.literal: When Li Mi seized Luokou Granary.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi took control of the Luokou Granary.

sentences.zh: 滎陽諸縣多應密。

translations.literal: Many counties of Xingyang largely responded to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Most counties in Xingyang went over to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 慶勒兵拒守。

translations.literal: Qing deployed troops to resist and hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Qing mustered troops to hold out in defense.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，城中糧盡，兵勢日蹙。

translations.literal: After more than a year, provisions in the city were exhausted and the military situation grew daily tighter.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the city's grain ran out and its position grew steadily worse.

sentences.zh: 密遺慶書曰：「王之先世，家住山東，本姓郭氏，乃非楊族。

translations.literal: Mi sent Qing a letter saying: "Your lordship's forebears, their home was in Shandong; their original surname was Guo — they were not of the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi sent Qing a letter: "Your ancestors came from Shandong; their original surname was Guo — you are not truly of the Yang line.

sentences.zh: 婁敬之于漢高，殊非血胤；

translations.literal: Lou Jing's relation to Emperor Gaozu of Han was by no means a blood line;
translations.idiomatic: Lou Jing's tie to Emperor Gaozu of Han was no blood kinship;

sentences.zh: 呂布之于董卓，良異天親。

translations.literal: Lü Bu's relation to Dong Zhuo was truly different from heaven-appointed kin.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu's bond with Dong Zhuo was anything but natural kinship.

sentences.zh: 芝焚蕙歎，事不同此。

translations.literal: When the iris is burned the orchid sighs — this affair is not the same.
translations.idiomatic: When one companion plant is destroyed the other mourns — but your situation is not like that.

sentences.zh: 江都荒湎，流宕忘歸，骨肉崩離，人神怨憤。

translations.literal: At Jiangdu [the Emperor] indulged in wasteful debauchery, drifted about and forgot to return; bone and flesh were torn apart, and men and spirits alike resented and raged.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangdu the Emperor drowned in debauchery and forgot to return; families were torn apart and both men and gods burned with outrage.

sentences.zh: 舉烽火于驪山，諸侯莫至；

translations.literal: He raised beacon fires at Mount Li, yet no feudal lords came;
translations.idiomatic: He lit the beacon fires at Mount Li, yet no allies answered;

sentences.zh: 浮膠船于漢水，還日未期。

translations.literal: He floated boats with glue on the Han River; the day of return was not yet fixed.
translations.idiomatic: He floated glue-bound boats on the Han River with no set date for return.

sentences.zh: 王獨守孤城，援絕千里，糧餱支計，僅有月餘，弊卒之多，才盈數百。

translations.literal: Your lordship alone holds an isolated city; relief is cut off for a thousand li; dry provisions to sustain you amount to barely more than a month; your worn-out soldiers at most number only several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: You hold a lone city with aid cut off a thousand li away; dried rations will last barely a month, and your exhausted troops number only a few hundred.

sentences.zh: 有何恃賴，欲相抗拒？

translations.literal: On what do you rely that you wish to resist us?
translations.idiomatic: What do you have to rely on in choosing to resist?

sentences.zh: 求枯魚於市肆，既事非虛；

translations.literal: To seek dried fish in the marketplace — the affair is indeed not empty [i.e., it is futile];
translations.idiomatic: To ask for dried fish at the market — that errand is no idle one;

sentences.zh: 因歸雁以運糧，竟知何日！

translations.literal: To rely on returning wild geese to transport grain — who knows what day that would be!
translations.idiomatic: To hope wild geese will bring you grain — who knows when that would be!

sentences.zh: 止恐禍生匕首，釁發蕭牆，空以七尺之軀，懸賞千金之購，可為酸鼻者也。

translations.literal: I only fear disaster born of a dagger, trouble erupting within the palace walls — in vain with a seven-foot body to hang a thousand-gold bounty upon it; it is enough to make one weep.
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that a dagger will strike within your own walls, that for nothing your seven-foot frame will fetch a thousand-gold price on your head — the thought is heartbreaking.

sentences.zh: 幸能三思，自求多福。

translations.literal: I hope you can think thrice and seek abundant blessings for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Think carefully and choose what is best for yourself.

sentences.zh: 」于時江都敗問亦至，慶得書，遂降於密，改姓為郭氏。

translations.literal: " At that time news of disaster at Jiangdu also arrived; Qing received the letter and thereupon surrendered to Mi, changing his surname to Guo.
translations.idiomatic: " About then news of the catastrophe at Jiangdu arrived as well. Qing read the letter and surrendered to Li Mi, taking the surname Guo.

sentences.zh: 密破，歸東都，又為楊氏，越王侗不之責也。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, [Qing] returned to the Eastern Capital and again became Yang; Prince of Yue Yang Tong did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Mi's defeat Qing returned to the Eastern Capital and resumed the Yang surname; Prince of Yue Yang Tong did not hold it against him.

sentences.zh: 及侗稱制，拜宗正卿。

translations.literal: When Tong assumed the regency, [Qing] was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Tong assumed imperial authority, Qing was made Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 世充既僭偽號，降爵為郇國公，復為郭氏。

translations.literal: Once Wang Shichong usurped a false title, [Qing's] rank was reduced to Duke of the State of Xun, and he again became Guo.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Shichong seized a spurious throne, Qing was demoted to Duke of the State of Xun and again took the surname Guo.

sentences.zh: 世充以兄女妻之，署滎州刺史。

translations.literal: Shichong gave him his elder brother's daughter in marriage and appointed him Governor of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong married him to his brother's daughter and made him Governor of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 及世充將敗，慶欲將妻同歸長安，其妻曰：「國家以妾奉箕帚於公者，欲以申厚意，結公心耳。

translations.literal: When Shichong was about to be defeated, Qing wished to take his wife back with him to Chang'an; his wife said: "The state gave me in marriage to your lordship with broom and dustpan in order to express deep goodwill and win your lordship's heart.
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Shichong's cause neared collapse, Qing wanted to take his wife with him to Chang'an. His wife said, "The court gave me to you in marriage to show its goodwill and win your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今父叔窮迫，家國阽危，而不顧婚姻，孤負付屬，為全身之計，非妾所能責公也。

translations.literal: Now when father and uncle are cornered and the house and state stand on the brink, yet you heed not the marriage bond, betray the trust placed in you, and plan only to save yourself — it is not for me to reproach your lordship.
translations.idiomatic: Now that your in-laws are desperate and the realm is in peril, you would abandon our marriage and betray the trust placed in you to save yourself — I cannot blame you for that.

sentences.zh: 妾若至長安，公家一婢耳，何用妾為！

translations.literal: If I were to reach Chang'an, I would be but one maid in your house — of what use would I be!
translations.idiomatic: If I went to Chang'an I would be nothing but a servant in your household — what good would I be to you!

sentences.zh: 顧送還東都，君之惠也。

translations.literal: Only send me back to the Eastern Capital — that would be your lordship's kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Please send me back to the Eastern Capital — that would be your kindness to me.

sentences.zh: 」慶不許。

translations.literal: " Qing did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " Qing refused.

sentences.zh: 其妻遂沐浴靚莊。

translations.literal: His wife thereupon bathed and adorned herself beautifully.
translations.idiomatic: His wife bathed, dressed herself finely, and prepared herself.

sentences.zh: 仰藥而死。

translations.literal: She swallowed poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: She took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 慶遂歸國，為宜州刺史、郇國公，復姓楊氏。

translations.literal: Qing thereupon returned to the state, was made Governor of Yizhou and Duke of the State of Xun, and again took the surname Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Qing then returned to the Tang court, was made Governor of Yizhou and Duke of the State of Xun, and resumed the Yang surname.

sentences.zh: 其嫡母元太妃，年老，兩目喪明，世充斬之。

translations.literal: His father's principal wife Grand Consort Yuan, old in years, had lost sight in both eyes; Shichong had her beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother Grand Consort Yuan was elderly and blind; Wang Shichong had her executed.

sentences.zh: 義城公處綱，文帝族父也。

translations.literal: Duke of Yicheng Chugang was a paternal uncle of Emperor Wen in the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Yicheng Chugang was a clan elder kinsman of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 生長北邊，少習騎射。

translations.literal: He grew up on the northern frontier and from youth practiced riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Raised on the northern frontier, he learned riding and archery from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 在周，以軍功拜上儀同。

translations.literal: In Zhou, for military merit he was appointed Senior Regiment Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou he was made Senior Regiment Commander for military service.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，贈其父鐘葵柱國、尚書令、義城縣公，以處綱襲焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, he posthumously granted his father Zhongkui the titles Pillar of State, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Duke of Yicheng County; Chugang succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne he posthumously made Chugang's father Zhongkui Pillar of State, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Duke of Yicheng County, which Chugang inherited.

sentences.zh: 累遷右領軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General of the Right Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of the Right Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 綱雖無才藝，而性質直，在官強濟，亦為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Chugang though lacking talent and arts, by nature was upright; in office he was forceful and effective, and was also praised by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Chugang had no literary gifts, but possessed an upright character and governed forcefully and effectively — enough to win praise in his day.

sentences.zh: 拜蒲州刺史，吏人悅之。

translations.literal: Appointed Governor of Puzhou, officials and people were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: As Governor of Puzhou he won the goodwill of officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 卒于秦州總管，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died while Commander-in-Chief of Qinzhou; his posthumous name was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Commander-in-Chief of Qinzhou and was posthumously named Gong.

sentences.zh: 弟處樂，官至洛州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chule reached the office of Governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chule rose to Governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒反，朝廷以為二心，廢錮不齒。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, the court considered him of two minds; he was deposed, imprisoned, and not counted among [normal] people.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, the court judged Chule disloyal; he was stripped of rank, imprisoned, and cast out from society.

sentences.zh: 離石太守子崇，武元帝族弟也。

translations.literal: Zichong, Prefect of Lishi, was a younger clan cousin of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zichong, Prefect of Lishi, was a younger kinsman of Emperor Wu in the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 父盆生，贈荊刺史。

translations.literal: His father Pensheng was posthumously granted Governor of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pensheng was posthumously made Governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 子崇少好學，涉獵書記，有風儀，愛賢好士。

translations.literal: Zichong from youth loved learning, broadly read books and records, had fine bearing, and loved the worthy and honored gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Zichong was an avid student from youth, widely read in books and records, carried himself well, and loved worthy men.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜儀同，以車騎將軍恆典宿衛，後為司門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed Regiment Commander; with General of Chariots and Cavalry Heng in charge of palace guard duty, and later [Zichong] became Vice Director of the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era he was made Regiment Commander and served in the palace guard under General of Chariots and Cavalry Heng; he later became Vice Director of the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，累遷候衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, [Zichong] was repeatedly promoted to General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang he rose to General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復檢校將軍事。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed provisional military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again given provisional command of troops.

sentences.zh: 從帝幸汾陽宮，子崇知突厥必為寇，屢請早還京師，不納。

translations.literal: Following the Emperor on a visit to Fenyang Palace, Zichong knew the Turks would surely raid; he repeatedly asked to return early to the capital, but [the request] was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: On the Emperor's visit to Fenyang Palace, Zichong foresaw a Turkish invasion and repeatedly urged an early return to the capital, but the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 尋有雁門之圍。

translations.literal: Before long came the siege at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward came the siege of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 及賊退，帝怒之曰：「子崇怯懦，妄有陳請，驚動我眾心，不可居爪牙寄。

translations.literal: When the enemy withdrew, the Emperor angrily said: "Zichong is cowardly and timid; he rashly made memorials, disturbing the morale of my host — he cannot hold a post as my trusted aide.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew, the Emperor raged: "Zichong is a coward who disturbed my troops with reckless petitions — he is unfit to serve at my side.

sentences.zh: 」出為離石郡太守，有能名。

translations.literal: " He was sent out as Prefect of Lishi Commandery and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: " He was banished to serve as Prefect of Lishi Commandery, where he earned a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 自是突屢寇邊塞，胡賊劉六兒復擁眾劫掠郡境，子崇表請兵鎮遏。

translations.literal: From then on the Turks repeatedly raided the frontier; the barbarian bandit Liu Liu'er again gathered a host to plunder the commandery borders; Zichong memorialized requesting troops to suppress and contain them.
translations.idiomatic: Turks then raided the frontier repeatedly, and the rebel Liu Liu'er again led bands to pillage the prefecture. Zichong memorialized requesting troops to hold them in check.

sentences.zh: 帝復大怒，令子崇行長城。

translations.literal: The Emperor again grew greatly angry and ordered Zichong to patrol the Great Wall.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage again and ordered Zichong to inspect the Great Wall.

sentences.zh: 子崇行百餘里，四面路絕，不得進而歸。

translations.literal: Zichong traveled more than a hundred li; roads were cut off on all four sides, and he could not advance and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zichong marched more than a hundred li but found every route blocked and had to turn back.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，朔方梁師都、馬邑劉武周等各作亂，郡中諸胡復反。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Liang Shidu of Shuofang, Liu Wuzhou of Mayi, and others each raised rebellion; the various Hu in the commandery again revolted.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Liang Shidu in Shuofang, Liu Wuzhou in Mayi, and others rebelled, and the Xianbei and other peoples in the commandery rose again.

sentences.zh: 子崇患之，言欲朝集，遂與心腹數百人自孟門關將還京師。

translations.literal: Zichong was distressed by this; saying he wished to attend court assembly, he then with several hundred trusted followers from Mengmen Pass was about to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Zichong announced that he intended to go to court, then set out from Mengmen Pass with several hundred trusted men to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 遇道路隔絕，退歸離石。

translations.literal: Encountering roads cut off and isolated, he withdrew and returned to Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked by severed roads, he fell back to Lishi.

sentences.zh: 左右聞太原兵起，不復入城，各叛去。

translations.literal: His attendants, hearing that troops had risen at Taiyuan, no longer entered the city and each deserted and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When his followers heard that rebels had risen at Taiyuan, they refused to enter the city and scattered in desertion.

sentences.zh: 子崇悉收叛者父兄斬之。

translations.literal: Zichong completely gathered the fathers and elder brothers of the deserters and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Zichong rounded up the fathers and elder brothers of every deserter and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 後數日，義兵至，城中應之。

translations.literal: Several days later righteous troops arrived, and those inside the city responded to them.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later rebel armies arrived, and the city rose to join them.

sentences.zh: 城陷，為讎家所殺。

translations.literal: The city fell, and he was killed by the families of his victims.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the families of those he had killed put him to death.

sentences.zh: 文帝五男，皆文獻皇后所生。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen had five sons; all were born of Empress Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had five sons, all born to Empress Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 長曰房陵王勇，次煬帝，次秦孝王俊，次庶人秀，次庶人諒。

translations.literal: The eldest was Prince Yong of Fangling; next the future Emperor Yang; next Prince Jun of Qin; next the commoner Xiu; next the commoner Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest was Prince Yong of Fangling; next came the future Emperor Yang; then Prince Jun of Qin; then Xiu, later stripped of rank; and lastly Liang, also reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 房陵王勇，小名睍地伐。

translations.literal: Prince Yong of Fangling had the childhood name Mandifa.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Fangling's childhood name was Mandifa.

sentences.zh: 周世以武元軍功，封博平縣侯。

translations.literal: In the Zhou era, on account of Empress Wu Yuan's military merit, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Boling County.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Zhou, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Boling for Empress Wu Yuan's military service.

sentences.zh: 及文帝輔政，立為世子，拜大將軍、左司衛，封長寧郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen became regent, Yong was established as heir and appointed Grand General and Left Director of the Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Changning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen assumed the regency, Yong was named heir, appointed Grand General and Director of the Left Guard, and enfeoffed as Duke of Changning.

sentences.zh: 出為洛州總管、東京少塚宰，總統舊齊之地。

translations.literal: He went out as Commander-in-Chief of Luozhou and Junior Steward of the Eastern Capital, overall commander of the former Qi territory.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as commander of Luozhou and junior steward of the Eastern Capital, with authority over the former Qi lands.

sentences.zh: 後徵還京師，進上柱國、大司馬，領內史禦正，諸禁衛皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Later summoned back to the capital, he was promoted to Pillar of State and Grand Marshal, and concurrently held Director of the Palace Secretariat and Censor-in-Chief; all the palace guards were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he was promoted to Pillar of State and Grand Marshal, put in charge of the Secretariat and the office of palace censors, with all imperial guards under his command.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，立為皇太子，軍國政事及尚書奏死罪已下，皆令勇參決。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen accepted the abdication and ascended the throne, Yong was established as Crown Prince; military and state affairs and memorials to the Ministry of Justice from death sentences downward were all ordered to be decided with Yong's participation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Yong was installed as crown prince. Military and civil affairs, and criminal cases up to but not including capital offenses referred by the Ministry of Justice, were all submitted for his review.

sentences.zh: 帝以山東人多流冗，遣使案檢，又欲徙人北實邊塞。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because many people in Shandong were vagrants and refugees, dispatched envoys to investigate, and also wished to relocate people north to populate the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Noting the large numbers of displaced people in the east, the Emperor sent investigators and planned to resettle population northward to strengthen the frontier.

sentences.zh: 勇上書諫，以為「戀土懷舊，人之本情，波迸流離，蓋不獲已。

translations.literal: Yong submitted a memorial remonstrating, stating that "attachment to one's land and homesickness are humanity's fundamental feelings; scattering in flight and drifting in exile are surely what one cannot but do when compelled."
translations.idiomatic: Yong memorialized in protest, arguing that "love of home is human nature, and flight into exile is only what people do when they have no choice."

sentences.zh: 有齊之末，主暗時昏，周平東夏，繼以威虐，人不堪命，致有逃亡，非厭家鄉，原為羈旅。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi the ruler was benighted and the times dark; Zhou pacified the eastern regions, then followed with brutal oppression; people could not bear their fate, leading to flight—not because they loathed their native places, but because they were forced into wandering exile.
translations.idiomatic: "Under the last rulers of Qi, the court was corrupt and the age benighted. When Zhou conquered the east, harsh rule followed until life was unbearable and people fled—not because they hated their homes, but because they were driven into rootless wandering."

sentences.zh: 若假以數歲，沐浴皇風，逃竄之徒，自然歸本。

translations.literal: If granted several years, bathed in the imperial benevolence, those who had fled would naturally return to their origins.
translations.idiomatic: "Given a few years under the emperor's benevolent rule, those who fled would naturally come home."

sentences.zh: 雖北夷犯邊，令所在嚴固，何待遷配，以致勞擾？

translations.literal: Even if northern barbarians violated the frontier, one might order each place to strengthen its defenses—why wait for relocation and assignment, thereby causing toil and disturbance?
translations.idiomatic: "Even if northern tribes raid the border, local defenses can be strengthened—why resort to forced relocation and cause such upheaval?"

sentences.zh: 」上覽而嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor read it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the memorial and commended it.

sentences.zh: 時晉王廣亦表言不可，帝遂止。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Jin, Guang, also submitted a memorial saying it should not be done, and the Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, Guang, also memorialized against the plan, and the Emperor abandoned it.

sentences.zh: 是後時政不便，多所損益，帝每納之。

translations.literal: After this, whenever current policy was unsuitable, Yong made many additions and deletions, and the Emperor each time accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever Yong pointed out flaws in policy and proposed changes, the Emperor adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 帝常從容謂群臣曰：「前世皇王，溺於嬖幸，廢立之所由生。

translations.literal: The Emperor often calmly said to the assembled ministers: "Emperors and kings of former ages, drowning in favorites—from this arose the reasons for deposing and establishing heirs."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often told his ministers at leisure, "Past emperors drowned in favorites—and that is how heirs were deposed or raised."

sentences.zh: 朕傍無姬侍，五子同母，可謂真兄弟也。

translations.literal: By my side there are no concubine attendants; my five sons share one mother—they may be called true brothers.
translations.idiomatic: "I keep no concubines at court. My five sons share one mother—they are true brothers."

sentences.zh: 豈若前代，多諸內寵，孽子忿爭，為亡國之道邪！」

translations.literal: How could it be like previous generations, with many inner favorites, illegitimate sons raging in rivalry—the way to lose a state!"
translations.idiomatic: "How unlike earlier dynasties, where harem intrigues drove bastard sons to fight one another—the road to ruin!"

sentences.zh: 勇頗好學，解屬詞賦，性寬仁和厚，率意任情，無矯飾之行。

translations.literal: Yong was quite fond of learning, skilled at composing regulated prose and fu; by nature magnanimous, benevolent, and generous, he followed his inclinations and gave free rein to his feelings, with no artificial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yong loved learning and wrote polished prose and fu. Open-hearted, kindly, and generous, he acted on his nature without pretense.

sentences.zh: 引明克讓、姚察、陸開明等為之賓友。

translations.literal: He invited Ming Kerang, Yao Cha, Lu Kaiming, and others to serve as his guest-friends.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered Ming Kerang, Yao Cha, Lu Kaiming, and others as companions and advisors.

sentences.zh: 勇嘗文飾蜀鎧，帝見而不悅，恐致奢侈之漸，因誡之曰：「我曆觀前代帝王，未有奢華而能長久者。

translations.literal: Yong once had his Shu armor ornamented with decoration; the Emperor saw it and was displeased, fearing it would lead to gradual luxury, and therefore admonished him, saying: "I have reviewed emperors of all former ages—none who were luxurious were able to endure long."
translations.idiomatic: Yong once had ornamental designs added to his Shu-style armor. The Emperor disapproved, fearing the first step toward extravagance, and warned him: "In every dynasty I have studied, no indulgent ruler lasted long."

sentences.zh: 汝當儲後，若不上稱帝心，下合人意，何以承宗廟之重，居兆人之上？

translations.literal: You are to be the stored heir; if you do not match the Emperor's heart above and accord with people's wishes below, how can you bear the weight of the ancestral temple and sit above the myriad people?
translations.idiomatic: "You are the heir. If you fail to win my approval or the people's trust, how will you bear the ancestral rites or rule over the multitude?"

sentences.zh: 吾昔衣服，各留一物，時復看以自警戒。

translations.literal: From my former garments I have kept one item each; from time to time I look at them to warn myself.
translations.idiomatic: "I kept one item from each set of clothes I once wore, and look at them from time to time to keep myself humble."

sentences.zh: 又擬分賜汝兄弟。

translations.literal: I also plan to divide and bestow them upon you brothers.
translations.idiomatic: "I mean to share them among you and your brothers."

sentences.zh: 恐汝以今日皇太子之心，忘昔時之事，故令高熲賜汝我舊所帶刀子一枚，並菹醬一合，汝昔作上士時所常食如此。

translations.literal: Fearing that with today's crown prince's heart you would forget matters of former times, I therefore ordered Gao Jiong to bestow upon you one knife I formerly carried at my belt, together with one box of pickled sauces—such as you regularly ate when you were a senior officer.
translations.idiomatic: "Lest the crown prince forget his past, I had Gao Jiong send you the knife I once wore at my belt and a jar of pickled sauce—the plain fare you ate as a junior officer."

sentences.zh: 若存憶前事，應知我心。」

translations.literal: If you preserve memory of former matters, you should know my heart."
translations.idiomatic: "If you remember where you came from, you will understand what I mean."

sentences.zh: 後經冬至，百官朝勇，勇張樂受賀。

translations.literal: Later, when the winter solstice passed, the hundred officials attended court upon Yong; Yong set out music and received congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the winter solstice, officials flocked to the Eastern Palace to congratulate Yong, who held a banquet with music.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，問朝臣：「近聞至節，內外百官相率朝東宮，是何禮也？

translations.literal: The Emperor learned of it and asked the court ministers: "I have recently heard that at the solstice, inner and outer officials successively attended court at the Eastern Palace—what ritual is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, the Emperor asked his ministers, "I hear that at the solstice, officials inside and outside the palace all went to the Eastern Palace in procession. What custom is that?"

sentences.zh: 」太常少卿辛亶對曰：「于東宮是賀，不得言朝。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Xin Dan replied: "At the Eastern Palace it is congratulations—one may not call it a court audience."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices Xin Dan answered, "They were offering congratulations, not performing a formal court audience."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「改節稱賀，正可三數十人，逐情各去，何因有司徵召，一朝普集，太子法服設樂以待之？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "At the change of season one may offer congratulations—properly only thirty or forty people, each departing as inclination leads. Why did the responsible offices summon and convene them all at once in a morning assembly, with the crown prince in formal robes setting out music to await them?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Seasonal greetings might involve a few dozen people who come and go as they please. Why did the authorities summon everyone at once, with the crown prince in full regalia and music waiting to receive them?"

sentences.zh: 東宮如此，殊乖禮制。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace behaving thus greatly deviates from ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: "Such conduct at the Eastern Palace is a serious breach of protocol."

sentences.zh: 」乃下詔曰：「皇太子雖居上嗣，義兼臣子，而諸方嶽牧正冬朝賀，任土作貢，別上東宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict saying: "Although the crown prince occupies the position of supreme successor, in principle he is also a subject; yet the governors of the regions at the winter solstice court audience and tribute according to their lands separately presented themselves at the Eastern Palace."
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict: "Though the crown prince is heir, he remains a subject in duty. Yet regional governors, after paying winter tribute at court, were also presenting themselves separately at the Eastern Palace."

sentences.zh: 事非典則，宜悉停斷。」

translations.literal: Such matters are not canonical precedent and should all be stopped and discontinued."
translations.idiomatic: "This has no precedent in ritual law and must cease entirely."

sentences.zh: 自此恩寵始衰，漸生凝阻。

translations.literal: From this point favor and indulgence began to decline, and gradual coldness and obstruction arose.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Emperor's affection waned, and estrangement began to grow.

sentences.zh: 時帝令選強宗入上臺宿衛，高熲奏：「若盡取強者，恐東宮宿衛太劣。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor ordered selection of men from powerful clans to enter the upper platform as palace guards; Gao Jiong memorialized: "If all the strongest are taken, I fear the Eastern Palace guard will be too weak."
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor ordered strong clansmen recruited for palace guard duty, Gao Jiong warned, "If we take all the ablest men, the Eastern Palace guard will be left too weak."

sentences.zh: 」帝作色曰：「我有時行動，宿衛須得雄毅。

translations.literal: The Emperor changed color and said: "When I sometimes go out, the guard must obtain bold and resolute men."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's face darkened. "When I travel, my guard must be bold and tough."

sentences.zh: 太子毓德東宮，左右何須強武？

translations.literal: The crown prince cultivates virtue in the Eastern Palace—what need have his attendants for great martial strength?
translations.idiomatic: "The crown prince is cultivating virtue—why do his attendants need to be fierce warriors?"

sentences.zh: 如我商量，恆於交番之日，分向東宮上下，團伍不別，豈非好事邪？

translations.literal: As I have considered it, always on the days of rotating shifts, divide them between the Eastern Palace above and below, companies undifferentiated—would this not be a good arrangement?"
translations.idiomatic: "My plan is to rotate guard units between us on each shift change, with no distinction between companies—is that not better?"

sentences.zh: 我熟見前代，公不須仍踵舊風！

translations.literal: I have thoroughly seen former generations—you, sir, need not still follow the old ways!"
translations.idiomatic: "I know only too well what happened in past dynasties—you need not cling to old habits!"

sentences.zh: 」蓋疑熲男尚勇女，形於此言，以防之。

translations.literal: This was probably because he suspected Gao Jiong's son was betrothed to Yong's daughter—made manifest in these words, as a precaution against him.
translations.idiomatic: The remark betrayed his suspicion that Gao Jiong's son was betrothed to Yong's daughter—a veiled warning.

sentences.zh: 勇多內寵，昭訓雲氏嬖幸，禮匹於嫡。

translations.literal: Yong had many inner favorites; the Cloud clan lady of Zhaoxun rank was doted upon, her ritual status equal to the principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: Yong kept many concubines, but Lady Yun of Zhaoxun rank was his favorite, treated with the honors due a principal consort.

sentences.zh: 而妃元氏無寵，嘗遇心疾，二日而薨。

translations.literal: Yet his consort of the Yuan clan had no favor; once she suffered heart disease and died after two days.
translations.idiomatic: His principal consort, Lady Yuan, had fallen from favor. She suffered a sudden heart ailment and died within two days.

sentences.zh: 獻皇后意有他故，甚責望勇。

translations.literal: Empress Wenxian believed there was another cause, and greatly blamed and reproached Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wenxian suspected foul play and reproached Yong bitterly.

sentences.zh: 又自妃薨，雲昭訓專擅內政，後彌不平，頗求勇罪過。

translations.literal: Moreover, from the consort's death, Lady Yun of Zhaoxun monopolized inner household affairs; the Empress grew ever more resentful and sought Yong's faults with some diligence.
translations.idiomatic: After Lady Yuan's death, Lady Yun dominated the inner quarters, and the Empress, increasingly aggrieved, began hunting for Yong's misdeeds.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣知之，彌自矯飾，姬妾恆備員數，唯與蕭妃居處。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin, Guang, knowing this, all the more artificially adorned himself; his concubines were always kept at full quota, yet he only lived together with Consort Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, Guang, seized the opportunity to curate his image: though his concubine roster was full, he lived alone with Lady Xiao.

sentences.zh: 皇后由是薄勇，愈稱晉王德行，後晉王來朝，車馬侍從，皆為儉素，接朝臣，禮極卑屈，聲名籍甚，冠于諸王。

translations.literal: The Empress therefore slighted Yong and praised the Prince of Jin's conduct all the more; later when the Prince of Jin came to court, carriage, horses, and attendants were all simple and plain; receiving court ministers, his courtesy was extremely humble—his reputation was greatly famed, surpassing all the princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress turned against Yong and praised the Prince of Jin's virtue ever more loudly. When he came to court, his escort was plain, his manner toward officials humbly deferential—his reputation soon eclipsed every other prince.

sentences.zh: 臨還揚州，入內辭皇后，因哽咽流涕，伏不能興。

translations.literal: On the verge of returning to Yangzhou, he entered the inner quarters to take leave of the Empress; thereupon choking with sobs and shedding tears, he prostrated himself and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Before returning to Yangzhou, he went to bid the Empress farewell, broke into tears, and prostrated himself, unable to rise.

sentences.zh: 皇后泫然泣下，相對歔欷。

translations.literal: The Empress, tears streaming, wept; facing each other they sighed and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress wept as well, and mother and son wept together.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「臣性識愚下，常守平生昆弟之意，不知何罪，失愛東宮，恆蓄盛怒，欲加屠陷。

translations.literal: The Prince said: "Your subject's nature and understanding are stupid and low; I constantly keep the fraternal feeling of our lifelong brotherhood—I know not what crime, but losing favor with the Eastern Palace, he constantly harbors great anger and wishes to add slaughter and entrapment."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "I am dull by nature and mean only to honor our brotherhood. Yet for reasons I cannot fathom, the crown prince has turned against me and nurses such rage that he would destroy me."

sentences.zh: 每恐讒譖出於杼軸，鳩毒遇於杯杓。

translations.literal: Each day I fear slander emerging from the loom shuttle, or poisoned wine meeting the cup and ladle."
translations.idiomatic: "I live in fear of slander spun at the loom—or poison slipped into my cup."

sentences.zh: 」皇后忿然曰：「睍地伐漸不可耐，我為伊索得元家女，望隆基業，竟不聞作夫妻，專寵阿雲，有如許豚犬。

translations.literal: The Empress said angrily: "Mandifa is gradually unbearable! I sought out for him a daughter of the Yuan house, hoping for the flourishing of the imperial enterprise—yet I never hear of them as husband and wife; he dotes exclusively on Ayun—such a pig-dog!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress flared with anger. "Mandifa has become intolerable! I found him a Yuan bride to secure the succession, yet he pays her no mind and dotes on Ayun like some worthless cur!"

sentences.zh: 前新婦本無病痛，忽爾暴亡，遣人投藥，致此夭逝。

translations.literal: The former new bride originally had no illness or pain; suddenly she died violently—someone was sent to administer poison, causing this untimely death.
translations.idiomatic: "His wife was perfectly healthy, then suddenly died—someone had her poisoned."

sentences.zh: 事已如此，我亦不窮。

translations.literal: Since matters have already come to this, I also do not pursue it to the end.
translations.idiomatic: "Even knowing this, I let it pass."

sentences.zh: 何因復於汝處發如此意？

translations.literal: Why then again at your place give vent to such thoughts?
translations.idiomatic: "Why come to me with such fears?"

sentences.zh: 我在尚爾，我死後當魚肉汝乎？

translations.literal: While I am still alive it is still thus—after I die, will he not treat you like fish on the chopping block?"
translations.idiomatic: "If things are this bad while I live, what will he do to you after I am gone?"

sentences.zh: 每思東宮竟無正嫡，至尊千秋萬歲後，遣汝等兄弟向陽雲兒前再拜問訊，此是幾許大苦痛邪！

translations.literal: Each time I think that the Eastern Palace ultimately has no legitimate principal consort—after the Supreme One's thousands of autumns and myriad years, sending you brothers to bow twice before Yang Ayun'er and inquire after her—how great a bitterness is this!"
translations.idiomatic: "When I think that the Eastern Palace has no true principal consort, and that after the Emperor's death you brothers will have to bow before that Cloud woman—what agony is that!"

sentences.zh: 」晉王又拜，嗚咽不能止，皇后亦悲不自勝。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin again bowed, sobbing without cease; the Empress also grieved beyond self-control.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin bowed again, sobbing uncontrollably, until the Empress was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 此別之後，知皇后意移，始構奪宗之計。

translations.literal: After this parting, knowing the Empress's intent had shifted, he began to devise a plan to seize the succession.
translations.idiomatic: After this farewell, seeing that the Empress's favor had turned, he began plotting to supplant his brother.

sentences.zh: 因引張衡定策，遣褒公宇文述深交楊約，令喻旨於越公素，具言皇后此語。

translations.literal: He thereupon brought in Zhang Heng to fix the strategy, and dispatched Duke of Bao Yuwen Shu to become deeply friendly with Yang Yue, ordering him to convey the intent to Duke of Yue Yang Su, fully reporting these words of the Empress.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted Zhang Heng to shape the plan and sent Duke of Bao Yuwen Shu to win over Yang Yue, who was to relay the Empress's words to Duke of Yue Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 素瞿然曰：「但不知皇后如何？
