translations.literal: Yang Su started in alarm and said: "Only I do not know what the Empress thinks?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su started. "But what does the Empress truly think?"

sentences.zh: 但如所言，吾又何為者！

translations.literal: If it is just as described, what am I still doing!"
translations.idiomatic: "If what you say is true, what am I waiting for!"

sentences.zh: 」後數日，素入侍宴，微稱晉王孝悌恭儉有禮，用此揣皇后意，後泣曰：「公言是也。

translations.literal: Several days later Yang Su entered to attend a banquet, subtly praising the Prince of Jin's filial devotion, brotherly respect, reverence, frugality, and courtesy—using this to probe the Empress's mind; the Empress wept and said: "What you, sir, say is right."
translations.idiomatic: Days later, at a banquet, Yang Su gently praised the Prince of Jin's filial piety, modesty, and courtesy, testing the Empress's mood. She wept and said, "You speak the truth."

sentences.zh: 我兒大孝順，每聞至尊及我遣內使到，必迎於境首。

translations.literal: My son is greatly filial and obedient; each time he hears that the Supreme One and I have dispatched inner attendants, he invariably goes to welcome them at the border post.
translations.idiomatic: "My son is deeply filial. Whenever he learns that the Emperor or I have sent palace envoys, he rides out to the border to meet them."

sentences.zh: 又其新婦亦大可憐，我使婢去，常與同寢共食。

translations.literal: Moreover his new bride is also greatly pitiable—when I send maidservants, she always sleeps and eats together with them.
translations.idiomatic: "His wife is equally dear. When I send maids to visit, she shares bed and board with them."

sentences.zh: 豈如睍地伐共阿雲相對而坐，終日酣宴，昵近小人，疑阻骨肉！

translations.literal: How like Mandifa sitting face to face with Ayun, feasting drunkenly all day, intimate with petty men, suspicious and obstructing kinship!"
translations.idiomatic: "Unlike Mandifa, who sits drinking all day with Ayun, consorts with petty men, and drives wedges between his brothers!"

sentences.zh: 我所以益憐阿肼者，嘗恐暗地殺之。

translations.literal: The reason I pity A'pi all the more is that I constantly fear he will be secretly killed."
translations.idiomatic: "I favor A'pi all the more because I fear Mandifa will have him murdered in secret."

sentences.zh: 」素既知意，盛言太子不才。

translations.literal: Yang Su, now knowing her intent, greatly declared the crown prince lacking in talent.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Su understood her mind, he loudly declared the crown prince unfit.

sentences.zh: 皇后遂遺素金，始有廢立之意。

translations.literal: The Empress thereupon sent gold to Yang Su, and first had the intent to depose and establish.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress then sent Yang Su a gift of gold—the first open step toward deposing Yong and elevating Guang.

sentences.zh: 勇頗知其謀，憂懼，計無所出。

translations.literal: Yong quite knew their plot, and was anxious and fearful, with no plan to emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sensed the conspiracy and was stricken with fear, but could find no way out.

sentences.zh: 聞新豐人王輔賢能占候，召而問之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Wang Fuxian of Xinfeng could read divination and omens, he summoned and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Wang Fuxian of Xinfeng could read omens, he summoned him for counsel.

sentences.zh: 輔賢曰：「白虹貫東宮門，太白襲月，皇太子廢退象也。

translations.literal: Fuxian said: "A white rainbow pierces the Eastern Palace gate; Venus assaults the moon—these are signs of the crown prince's deposition and removal."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fuxian said, "A white rainbow spans the Eastern Palace gate, and Venus has struck the moon—both are omens of the crown prince's fall."

sentences.zh: 」以銅鐵五兵造諸厭勝。

translations.literal: With copper, iron, and the five weapons he made various counter-charms against evil.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had charms fashioned from copper, iron, and the five weapons to ward off ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 又于後園內作庶人村，屋宇卑陋，太子時于中寢息，布衣草褥，冀以當之。

translations.literal: Moreover in the rear garden he built a Commoner's Village; the buildings were low and shabby; the crown prince sometimes slept therein, with cloth robes and straw bedding, hoping thereby to substitute and counter the omen.
translations.idiomatic: In his rear garden he built a hamlet of hovels styled "Commoner's Village," where he sometimes slept on straw bedding in coarse clothes, hoping to avert the omen by symbolically accepting demotion.

sentences.zh: 帝知其不安，在仁壽宮，使楊素觀勇，素至東宮，偃息未入，勇束帶待之，故亦不進以怒勇，勇銜之，形於言色。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew he was unsettled; at Renshou Palace he sent Yang Su to observe Yong; Su arrived at the Eastern Palace and reclined to rest without entering; Yong girded his belt and waited for him, yet Su still did not enter in order to anger Yong; Yong harbored resentment, visible in speech and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, aware of Yong's anxiety, sent Yang Su from Renshou Palace to observe him. Su reached the Eastern Palace and lingered outside without entering. Yong belted himself and waited, but Su deliberately stayed away to provoke him. Yong's resentment showed plainly in face and voice.

sentences.zh: 素還，言勇怨望，恐有他變。

translations.literal: Su returned and reported that Yong was resentful and looked askance, fearing there might be other changes.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su reported that Yong was bitter and discontent and might resort to desperate measures.

sentences.zh: 帝甚疑之。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's suspicions deepened.

sentences.zh: 皇后又遣人伺覘東宮，纖介事皆聞奏，因加媒蘖，構成其罪。

translations.literal: The Empress also sent people to spy on the Eastern Palace; the slightest matters were all reported to her, and through added slander and fabrications his crimes were constructed.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress sent spies to the Eastern Palace and reported every trivial matter, embellishing slander until a case against Yong took shape.

sentences.zh: 帝惑之，遂疏忌勇。

translations.literal: The Emperor was bewildered by this and therefore grew distant and suspicious of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Bewildered, the Emperor turned cold toward Yong.

sentences.zh: 乃于玄武門達至德門量置人候，以伺動靜，皆隨事奏聞。

translations.literal: He then from Xuande Gate to Zhide Gate measured and placed watchers at intervals to observe movements, all reporting each matter as it arose.
translations.idiomatic: He posted observers from Xuande Gate to Zhide Gate to monitor every move at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 又東宮宿衛人，侍官已上，名籍悉令屬諸衛府，有健兒者咸屏去之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Eastern Palace guard personnel, attendants and above—their name registers were all ordered to belong to the various guard offices; those who were strong warriors were all removed and barred.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred all Eastern Palace guards above the rank of attendant to regular guard offices and stripped away every able fighter.

sentences.zh: 晉王又令段達私貨東宮幸臣姬威，令取太子消息，密告楊素。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin also had Duan Da secretly bribe Yong's favored attendant Ji Wei, ordering him to obtain the crown prince's intelligence and secretly report to Yang Su.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin had Duan Da bribe Ji Wei, a favorite of the Eastern Palace, to feed intelligence on the crown prince to Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 於是內外宣謗，過失日聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon inside and outside slander was spread, and faults were heard daily.
translations.idiomatic: Slander swelled inside and outside the palace, and fresh accusations against Yong surfaced daily.

sentences.zh: 段達脅姬威曰：「東宮罪過，主上皆已知之。

translations.literal: Duan Da coerced Ji Wei, saying: "The Eastern Palace's crimes—the lord above all already knows them."
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da threatened Ji Wei: "The Emperor already knows the crown prince's crimes."

sentences.zh: 已奉密詔，定當廢立。

translations.literal: A secret edict has already been received; deposition and establishment are certainly to be decided."
translations.idiomatic: "A secret edict has been issued—the succession will be changed."

sentences.zh: 君能告之，則大富貴。

translations.literal: If you, sir, can report them, then great wealth and honor will follow."
translations.idiomatic: "Inform on him, and great riches await you."

sentences.zh: 」威遂許諾。

translations.literal: Wei thereupon promised.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wei agreed.

sentences.zh: 開皇二十年，車駕至自仁壽宮，禦大興殿，謂侍臣曰：「我新還京師，應開懷歡樂，不知何意，翻悒然愁苦。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Kaihuang, the imperial carriage arrived from Renshou Palace; the Emperor attended at Daxing Hall and said to attendant ministers: "I have newly returned to the capital and ought to open my heart in joy—I know not why, instead I am gloomy and afflicted with sorrow."
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Kaihuang, the Emperor returned from Renshou Palace to Daxing Hall and told his ministers, "I have just come back to the capital and ought to be glad, yet for some reason I am sunk in gloom."

sentences.zh: 」吏部尚書牛弘對曰：「由臣等不稱職，故至尊憂勞。

translations.literal: Minister of Civil Appointments Niu Hong replied: "It is because we subjects are not fulfilling our duties, therefore the Supreme One is worried and toiling."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Civil Appointments Niu Hong answered, "Your ministers must be failing you, and that is why Your Majesty is troubled."

sentences.zh: 帝既數聞讒譖，疑朝臣具委，故有斯問，冀聞太子之愆。

translations.literal: The Emperor, having repeatedly heard slander, suspected the court ministers all knew in detail, and therefore had this question, hoping to hear of the crown prince's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Having heard so much slander, the Emperor suspected his ministers knew the full story and hoped this question would draw out accusations against the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 弘既此對，大乖本指。

translations.literal: Hong having replied thus, greatly missed the original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong's answer completely missed the point.

sentences.zh: 帝因作色謂東宮官屬曰：「仁壽宮去此不遠，令我每還京師，嚴備如入敵國。

translations.literal: The Emperor therefore changed color and said to the Eastern Palace officials: "Renshou Palace is not far from here—yet it makes me each time I return to the capital strictly prepare as if entering an enemy state."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's face darkened as he addressed the Eastern Palace staff: "Renshou Palace is close by, yet every return to the capital feels like entering enemy territory."

sentences.zh: 我為患利，不脫衣臥。

translations.literal: Because I suffer from bowel troubles, I do not remove my clothes to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: "Troubled by my bowels, I sleep without undressing."

sentences.zh: 夜欲得近廁，故在後房。

translations.literal: At night wishing to be near the privy, therefore I stay in the rear chamber.
translations.idiomatic: "At night I stay in the rear chamber to be near the privy."

sentences.zh: 恐有驚急，還就前殿。

translations.literal: Fearing sudden alarm, I still return to the front hall.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet fearing sudden danger, I still move back to the front hall."

sentences.zh: 豈非爾輩欲壞我家國邪！

translations.literal: Is it not that you people wish to ruin my house and state!
translations.idiomatic: "Is it not you who wish to ruin my house and state!"

sentences.zh: 」乃執唐令則等數人，付所司訊鞫。

translations.literal: " He then seized Tang Lingze and several others and handed them over to the appropriate offices for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: He then arrested Tang Lingze and several others and handed them over to the authorities for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 令楊素陳東宮事狀，以告近臣。

translations.literal: He ordered Yang Su to set forth the Eastern Palace situation and inform the close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yang Su to lay out the Eastern Palace affair and report it to his inner circle of ministers.

sentences.zh: 素顯言之曰：「奉敕向京，令皇太子檢校劉居士餘黨。

translations.literal: Su spoke openly, saying: "By imperial order I came to the capital, and was charged to have the crown prince investigate and purge the remaining faction of Liu Jushi.
translations.idiomatic: Su spoke plainly: "By imperial order I came to the capital to have the crown prince investigate and purge the remaining followers of Liu Jushi."

sentences.zh: 太子忿然作色，肉戰淚下，云：'居士党已盡，遣我何處窮討？

translations.literal: The crown prince flushed with anger, his flesh trembling and tears falling, saying: 'Jushi's faction is already exhausted—where do you send me to hunt them down to the end?
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince flushed with rage, trembling and in tears: "Jushi's faction is already wiped out—where do you send me to hunt them to the ends of the earth?"

sentences.zh: 爾作右僕射，受委自求，何關我事！

translations.literal: You serve as Right Vice Minister—you accepted the commission and sought it yourself; what has that to do with me!
translations.idiomatic: "You are Right Vice Minister—you took the assignment on your own; what has that to do with me!"

sentences.zh: '又云：' 昔大事不遂，我先被誅。

translations.literal: ' He also said: ' In the past when the great affair did not succeed, I was the first to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When the great affair failed in the past, I was the first who would have been executed."

sentences.zh: 今作天子，竟乃令我不如弟，一事已上，不得自由。

translations.literal: Now that he has become Son of Heaven, he actually makes me inferior to my younger brother—in any matter whatsoever I have no freedom.
translations.idiomatic: "Now that he is emperor, he makes me inferior even to my younger brother—not a single matter is left to my own choice."

sentences.zh: '因長歎回視云：'我大覺身妨！

translations.literal: ' Then he sighed long, turned and looked back, saying: 'I feel greatly that my person is a hindrance!
translations.idiomatic: He sighed deeply, looked back, and said: "I feel more and more that my very existence is in the way!"

sentences.zh: '又云：'諸王皆得奴，獨不與我！

translations.literal: ' He also said: 'All the princes get slaves—only I am not given any!
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "All the princes get servants—only I am given none!"

sentences.zh: '乃向西北奮頭，喃喃細語。

translations.literal: ' Then he turned his head vigorously toward the northwest and muttered in a low voice.
translations.idiomatic: Then he jerked his head toward the northwest and muttered under his breath.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此兒不堪妨承嗣久矣。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "This boy has long been unfit to obstruct the succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "This boy has long been unfit to inherit the throne."

sentences.zh: 皇后恆勸我廢，我以布素時生，復長子，望其漸改，隱忍至今。

translations.literal: The Empress constantly urged me to depose him. Because he was born when we wore plain cloth and is moreover my eldest son, I hoped he would gradually reform and forbear until now.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress has constantly urged me to depose him. He was born when we still wore plain cloth, and he is my eldest son; I hoped he would mend his ways and have borne with him until now.

sentences.zh: 勇昔從南兗州來，語衛王曰：'阿娘不與我一好婦女，亦是可恨。

translations.literal: When Yong once came from Southern Yanzhou, he said to the Prince of Wei: 'Mother won't give me a fine woman—that too is hateful.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong once returned from Southern Yanzhou, he told the Prince of Wei: "Mother won't give me a good wife—that alone is hateful enough."

sentences.zh: '因指皇后侍兒曰：'皆我物。

translations.literal: ' Then pointing at the Empress's attendants he said: 'They are all mine.
translations.idiomatic: Then, pointing at the Empress's attendants, he said: "They are all mine."

sentences.zh: '此言幾許異事！

translations.literal: ' What extraordinary words are these!
translations.idiomatic: What extraordinary words!

sentences.zh: 其婦初亡，即以鬥帳安余老嫗。

translations.literal: When his wife first died, he immediately installed a canopy tent for an old serving woman of mine.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife first died, he immediately set up a canopy tent for an old serving woman of mine.

sentences.zh: 新婦初亡，我深疑使馬嗣明藥殺。

translations.literal: When the new wife first died, I strongly suspected he had Ma Siming poison her with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When the new wife died, I strongly suspected he had Ma Siming kill her with poison.

sentences.zh: 我曾責之，便懟曰：'會當殺元孝矩。

translations.literal: When I once rebuked him, he retorted: 'I shall surely kill Yuan Xiaoju.
translations.idiomatic: When I rebuked him once, he snapped back: "I will kill Yuan Xiaoju."

sentences.zh: '此欲害我而遷怒耳。

translations.literal: ' This was intent to harm me expressed as displaced anger.
translations.idiomatic: That was rage meant for me, vented on someone else.

sentences.zh: 初，長寧誕育，朕與皇后共抱養之，自懷彼此，連遣來索。

translations.literal: At first, when Changning was born, the Empress and I together held and raised him; from natural affection he kept sending to claim him.
translations.idiomatic: When Changning was first born, the Empress and I together held and raised him; out of natural attachment he repeatedly sent to claim the child.

sentences.zh: 且雲定興女，在外私合而生，想此由來，何必是其體胤？

translations.literal: Moreover he said Dingxing's daughter had been conceived in an illicit union outside—considering this origin, why must she be his true issue?
translations.idiomatic: He also said Dingxing's daughter had been conceived in an illicit affair abroad—given such origins, why must the boy be his true heir?

sentences.zh: 昔晉太子取屠家女，其兒即好屠割。

translations.literal: Formerly the Jin crown prince took a butcher's daughter, and his son took pleasure in butchery.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago a Jin crown prince married a butcher's daughter, and his son delighted in slaughter.

sentences.zh: 今儻非類，便亂宗祐。

translations.literal: If now he should not be of the same kind, he would bring disorder to the ancestral blessing.
translations.idiomatic: If the child is not truly of our line, he will corrupt the ancestral succession.

sentences.zh: 又劉金驎，佞人也，呼定興作家翁。

translations.literal: Also Liu Jinlin, a flatterer, called Dingxing 'father-in-law.'
translations.idiomatic: Then there was Liu Jinlin, a sycophant, who called Dingxing "father-in-law."

sentences.zh: 定興愚人，受其此語。

translations.literal: Dingxing, a foolish man, believed this talk.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing, a fool, took such talk seriously.

sentences.zh: 我前解金驎者，為其此事。

translations.literal: The reason I earlier dismissed Jinlin was for this affair.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I dismissed Jinlin earlier was this very matter.

sentences.zh: 勇昔在宮，引曹妙達共定興女同宴，妙達在外雲'我今得勸妃酒。

translations.literal: Yong once in the palace invited Cao Miaoda to feast together with Dingxing's daughter; Miaoda outside said 'I now get to urge the consort to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Yong once had Cao Miaoda feast in the palace with Dingxing's daughter; outside, Miaoda boasted, "Now I get to urge the consort to drink."

sentences.zh: '直以其諸子偏庶，畏人不服，故逆縱之，欲收天下望耳。

translations.literal: ' Simply because his sons were mostly by concubines, fearing people would not submit, he therefore indulged them contrary to rule, wanting to gain the regard of the empire.
translations.idiomatic: He indulged them against all propriety only because most of his sons were by concubines and he feared men would not accept them—he wanted to win the empire's approval.

sentences.zh: 我雖德慚堯舜，終不以萬姓付不肖子。

translations.literal: Though my virtue falls short of Yao and Shun, in the end I will not entrust the myriad people to an unworthy son.
translations.idiomatic: However far my virtue falls short of Yao and Shun, I will never entrust the people to an unworthy son.

sentences.zh: 我恆畏其加害，加防大敵，令欲廢之，以安天下。

translations.literal: I constantly feared he would harm me, guarding against him as against a great enemy, and now wish to depose him to secure the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I have long feared he would do me harm and guarded against him as against a formidable foe; now I mean to depose him to secure the realm.

sentences.zh: 」左衛大將軍元旻諫曰：「廢立大事，天子無貳言，詔旨若行，後悔無及。

translations.literal: " Left Guardian General Yuan Min remonstrated, saying: "Deposition and installation is a great matter; the Son of Heaven has no second word—if the edict goes forth, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guardian General Yuan Min remonstrated: "Deposing and installing an heir is a grave matter. The Son of Heaven should not speak twice—once the edict goes out, regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 讒言罔極，惟陛下察之。

translations.literal: Slander has gone to extremes—may Your Majesty examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Slander has gone to extremes—may Your Majesty look into it carefully."

sentences.zh: 」辭直爭強，聲色俱厲，帝不答。

translations.literal: " His words were direct and forceful, his voice and bearing both fierce; the Emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: His words were blunt and forceful, his voice and manner fierce; the Emperor made no answer.

sentences.zh: 時姬威又表告太子非法，帝使威盡言。

translations.literal: At that time Ji Wei again memorialized reporting the crown prince's illegal conduct, and the Emperor had Wei speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ji Wei again submitted a memorial accusing the crown prince of misconduct, and the Emperor had him speak out fully.

sentences.zh: 威對曰：「皇太子由來共臣語，唯意在驕奢，欲得樊川以至散關，總規為苑。

translations.literal: Wei replied: "The crown prince in his talks with me has always had his mind set on proud extravagance, wishing to take Fan River through to Sanguan Pass and altogether plan it as a park.
translations.idiomatic: Wei replied: "In all his talks with me, the crown prince's mind has been set on proud extravagance—he wants to take the land from Fan River all the way to Sanguan Pass and turn it into a single park."

sentences.zh: 兼云：'昔漢武將起上林苑，東方朔諫，賜朔黃金百斤，幾許可笑！

translations.literal: He also said: 'Formerly when Emperor Wu of Han was about to build Shanglin Park, Dongfang Shuo remonstrated and was granted a hundred catties of gold by Shuo—how laughable!
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When Emperor Wu of Han was about to build Shanglin Park, Dongfang Shuo remonstrated and was rewarded with a hundred catties of gold—how ridiculous!"

sentences.zh: 我實無金輒賜此等。

translations.literal: I truly have no gold with which to reward such people.
translations.idiomatic: "I have no gold to reward people like that."

sentences.zh: 若有諫者，正當斬之，不過殺百許人，自然永息。

translations.literal: If there are remonstrators, they should simply be beheaded—it would be no more than killing a hundred or so people, and naturally it would cease forever.
translations.idiomatic: "If anyone remonstrates, behead him—kill a hundred or so and the trouble will stop for good."

sentences.zh: '前蘇孝慈解左衛率，皇太子奮髯揚肘曰：'大丈夫當有一日，終不忘之，決當快意。

translations.literal: ' Formerly when Su Xiaoci was dismissed from Left Guard Commandant, the crown prince bristled his beard and raised his elbow, saying: 'A true man ought one day—I'll never forget this; I'll surely have my satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Xiaoci was removed as Left Guard Commandant, the crown prince bristled his beard and threw back his elbow, saying: "A real man bides his time—I will never forget this; one day I will have my revenge."

sentences.zh: '又宮內所須，尚書多執法不與，便怒曰：'僕射已下五人，會展三人腳，便使知慢我之禍。

translations.literal: ' Also for what the palace needed, the Ministers of the Imperial Secretariat often held to law and would not grant them; he angrily said: 'Of the five men from the Vice Minister down, I would kill three—then they would know the calamity of slighting me.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace needed supplies, the Secretariat ministers often refused on legal grounds; he raged: "Of the five officials from the Vice Minister down, I would execute three of them—then they would learn what it costs to slight me."

sentences.zh: '又于苑內築一小城，春夏秋冬作役不輟，營起亭殿，朝造夕改。

translations.literal: ' Also within the park he built a small city; construction labor through spring, summer, autumn and winter never ceased, erecting pavilions and halls—built in the morning, altered by evening.
translations.idiomatic: Within the park he also built a small city. Labor went on without pause through all four seasons as pavilions and halls rose—built in the morning, torn down or altered by evening.

sentences.zh: 每云：'至尊嗔我多側庶，高緯、陳叔寶豈是孽子乎？

translations.literal: He often said: 'The Supreme One resents that I have many sons by concubines—were Gao Wei and Chen Shubao not sons of concubines?
translations.idiomatic: He often said: "Father resents that I have so many sons by concubines—but were Gao Wei and Chen Shubao not sons of concubines?"

sentences.zh: '嘗令師姥卜吉凶，語臣曰：'至尊忌在十八年，此期促矣。

translations.literal: ' He once had a divining nun cast omens and said to me: 'The Supreme One's doom falls in the eighteenth year—this deadline is near.
translations.idiomatic: He once had a divining nun cast omens and told me: "The Emperor's fatal year is the eighteenth— that deadline is close."

sentences.zh: '」帝泫然曰：「誰非父母生，乃至於此！

translations.literal: '" The Emperor said tearfully: "Who is not born of parents—yet it comes to this!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said through tears: "Who is not born of parents—yet it has come to this!"

sentences.zh: 我有舊使婦女，令看東宮。

translations.literal: I had a former serving woman look in on the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: I had a former serving woman of mine observe the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 奏云：'勿令廣平王至皇太子處。

translations.literal: She reported: 'Do not let the Prince of Guangping go to the crown prince's place.
translations.idiomatic: She reported: "Do not let the Prince of Guangping visit the crown prince."

sentences.zh: 東宮憎婦，亦廣平王教之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace detests women—it was also the Prince of Guangping who taught this.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace loathes women—and it was the Prince of Guangping who taught him that.

sentences.zh: '元贊亦知其陰惡，勸我于左藏東加置兩隊。

translations.literal: ' Yuan Zan also knew his secret wickedness and urged me to add two more guard companies east of the Left Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zan also knew his secret wickedness and urged me to station two more guard companies east of the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 初平陳後，宮人好者悉配春坊，如聞不知厭足，於外更有求訪。

translations.literal: After the initial pacification of Chen, all the comely palace women were assigned to the Spring Palace; I hear he was not satisfied but sought more outside as well.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was first pacified, all the finest palace women were assigned to the Spring Palace; I hear he was not satisfied and sought more beyond the palace as well.

sentences.zh: 朕近覽《齊書》，見高歡縱其兒子，不勝忿憤，安可效尤！

translations.literal: " I recently read the Book of Qi and saw how Gao Huan indulged his son—I could not restrain my rage; how could I follow that bad example!
translations.idiomatic: I recently read the Book of Qi and saw how Gao Huan indulged his son—I was furious; how could I follow so ruinous an example!"

sentences.zh: 」於是勇及諸子皆被禁錮，部分收其黨與。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yong and his sons were all placed under confinement, and in part his faction was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yong and his sons were all placed under confinement, and part of his faction was arrested.

sentences.zh: 楊素舞文鍛煉，以成其獄。

translations.literal: Yang Su twisted the written law and forged evidence to complete the case.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su twisted the law and fabricated evidence to complete the case.

sentences.zh: 勇由是遂敗。

translations.literal: Because of this Yong was at last ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this Yong was ruined at last.

sentences.zh: 居數日，有司承素意，奏「元旻身備宿衛，常曲事於勇，情有附托。

translations.literal: Several days later, the officials, carrying out Su's intent, memorialized: "Yuan Min, holding night guard duty, constantly curried favor with Yong; his feelings had attachment and reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later, the officials, acting on Su's wishes, memorialized: "Yuan Min, charged with night guard duty, constantly curried favor with Yong and was emotionally attached to him.

sentences.zh: 在仁壽宮，裴弘將勇書於朝堂與旻，題封雲，勿令人見。

translations.literal: At Renshou Palace, Pei Hong brought Yong's letter to the court hall and to Min; the superscription read: Do not let people see.
translations.idiomatic: At Renshou Palace, Pei Hong delivered Yong's letter to Min in the court hall; the cover bore the words: Do not let anyone see."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕在仁壽宮。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "I am at Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "I am at Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 有纖小事，東宮必知，疾于驛馬，懌之甚久，豈非此徒邪？

translations.literal: Even the slightest matter—the Eastern Palace always knows of it, faster than relay horses; I have nursed suspicion of this for a long time—is it not these fellows?
translations.idiomatic: Even the smallest matter—the Eastern Palace always knows of it, faster than relay horses. I have suspected this for a long time—is it not these men?"

sentences.zh: 」遣武士執旻及弘付法。

translations.literal: " He sent warriors to seize Min and Hong and deliver them to the law.
translations.idiomatic: He sent warriors to seize Min and Hong and hand them over for punishment.

sentences.zh: 先是，勇嘗于仁壽宮參起居還，途中見一枯槐樹，根幹蟠錯，大且五六圍，顧左右曰：「此堪作何器用？

translations.literal: Earlier, Yong once after attending to the Emperor's health at Renshou Palace on the way back saw a withered paulownia tree, its roots and trunk tangled and twisted, large enough for five or six arm-spans around, and turning to those beside him said: "What vessel could this serve as?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after attending to the Emperor at Renshou Palace, Yong on the way back saw a dead paulownia tree, its roots and trunk gnarled and twisted, five or six arm-spans around, and asked those with him: "What could this be made into?"

sentences.zh: 」或對曰：「古槐尤堪取火。

translations.literal: " Someone replied: "Ancient paulownia is especially fit for fire-starters.
translations.idiomatic: Someone answered: "Old paulownia is especially good for fire-strikers."

sentences.zh: 」于時衛士皆佩火燧，勇因令匠者造數千枚，欲以分賜左右。

translations.literal: " At that time the guards all wore fire-strikers on their belts; Yong therefore ordered craftsmen to make several thousand of them, intending to distribute them to those around him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the guards all carried fire-strikers on their belts; Yong therefore had craftsmen make several thousand, intending to distribute them to his attendants.

sentences.zh: 至是，獲於庫。

translations.literal: By this time they were seized in the storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: By then they were found in the storehouse.

sentences.zh: 又藥藏局貯艾數斛，亦搜得之。

translations.literal: Also the Medicine Store Bureau stored several hu of mugwort—they too were searched out and found.
translations.idiomatic: The Medicine Store Bureau also had several hu of mugwort in storage—and that too was discovered in the search.

sentences.zh: 大將為怪，以問姬威。

translations.literal: The generals thought it strange and questioned Ji Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The generals found this suspicious and questioned Ji Wei.

sentences.zh: 威曰：「太子此意別有所在。

translations.literal: Wei said: "The crown prince's intent in this must lie elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Wei said: "The crown prince's purpose here must lie elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 比令長寧王已下，詣仁壽宮還，每常急行，一宿便至。

translations.literal: Recently he had the Prince of Changning and those below go to Renshou Palace; on return they always travel at speed and reach [the capital] in one night's rest.
translations.idiomatic: Recently he had the Prince of Changning and the younger princes visit Renshou Palace; on the return journey they always rode at full speed and reached the capital after a single night's rest.

sentences.zh: 恆飼馬千匹，雲徑往捉城門，自然餓死。

translations.literal: He constantly keeps a thousand horses fed, saying they would go straight to seize the city gates—the horses inside would naturally starve to death.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly kept a thousand horses fed, saying they would ride straight to seize the city gates and that those inside would naturally starve.

sentences.zh: 」素以威言詰勇，勇不服曰：「竊聞公家馬數萬匹，勇忝備位太子，有馬千匹，乃是反乎？

translations.literal: " Su used Wei's words to interrogate Yong; Yong did not submit, saying: "I privately hear the state's horses number in the tens of thousands; Yong humbly holds the position of crown prince—if I have a thousand horses, is that rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Su used Wei's testimony to confront Yong. Yong refused to concede: "I hear the state keeps tens of thousands of horses. I am crown prince—if I have a thousand horses, is that rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 」素又發洩東宮服玩似加琱飾者，悉陳於庭，以示文帝群官，為太子罪。

translations.literal: " Su also brought out Eastern Palace clothing and playthings that seemed overly ornate, displayed them all in the courtyard to show Emperor Wen's group of officials, as the crown prince's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Su also produced Eastern Palace garments and playthings that seemed extravagantly ornamented, displayed them in the courtyard before Emperor Wen and the officials, and presented them as proof of the crown prince's guilt.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「前簿王世積，得婦女領巾，狀似槊幡，當時遍示百官，欲以為戒。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Formerly in Wang Shiji's record there was a woman's headscarf shaped like a spear-banner; at the time it was shown to all officials, intending it as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "In Wang Shiji's case there was once a woman's headscarf shaped like a spear-banner; it was shown to all the officials as a warning.

sentences.zh: 今我兒乃自為之。

translations.literal: Now my own son has made such things himself.
translations.idiomatic: Now my own son has made such things himself.

sentences.zh: 領巾為槊幡，此是服妖。

translations.literal: A headscarf as spear-banner—this is dress-omen.
translations.idiomatic: A headscarf made into a spear-banner—this is ominous dress."

sentences.zh: 」使將諸物示勇以詰之。

translations.literal: " He had the various items brought out and shown to Yong to question him.
translations.idiomatic: He had the items brought out and shown to Yong for questioning.

sentences.zh: 皇后又責之罪。

translations.literal: The Empress also blamed him for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress also rebuked him for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝使使問勇，勇不服。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys to question Yong; Yong would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent envoys to question Yong, but Yong would not concede.

sentences.zh: 太史令袁充進曰：「臣觀天文，皇太子當廢。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Yuan Chong advanced and said: "I observe the heavens—the crown prince ought to be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Yuan Chong stepped forward and said: "From the heavens I read that the crown prince should be deposed."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「玄象久見矣。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "The omen in the sky has long been visible.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "That celestial sign has long been visible.

sentences.zh: 」群臣無敢言者。

translations.literal: " Among the officials none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: None of the officials dared speak."

sentences.zh: 於是使人召勇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent men to summon Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sent men to summon Yong.

sentences.zh: 勇見使者，驚曰：「得無殺我邪？

translations.literal: Yong upon seeing the envoys cried in alarm: "You are not going to kill me, are you?
translations.idiomatic: When Yong saw the envoys he cried out in alarm: "You aren't here to kill me, are you?"

sentences.zh: 」帝戎服陳兵，禦武德殿，集百官立于東面，諸親立於西面，引勇及諸子烈於殿庭。

translations.literal: " The Emperor in martial dress arrayed troops, held audience at Wude Hall, gathered the hundred officials standing on the east, royal kin standing on the west, and led Yong and his sons Lie out into the hall courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, in martial dress with troops arrayed, held court at Wude Hall. The hundred officials stood on the east, the royal kin on the west, and Yong and his son Lie were brought out into the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 命薛道衡宣詔廢勇及其男女為王、公主者並為庶人。

translations.literal: He ordered Xue Daoheng to proclaim the edict deposing Yong and demoting his sons and daughters who were princes and princesses to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xue Daoheng to proclaim the edict deposing Yong and reducing his sons and daughters who had been princes and princesses to commoners.

sentences.zh: 命道衡謂勇曰：「爾之罪惡，人神所棄，欲求不廢，其可得邪！

translations.literal: He ordered Daoheng to say to Yong: "Your wickedness is abandoned by both men and gods—to seek not to be deposed, how could that be possible!
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Daoheng to tell Yong: "Your wickedness is rejected by both men and gods—to hope not to be deposed, how could that be possible!"

sentences.zh: 」勇再拜曰：「臣合屍之都市，為將來鑒誡。

translations.literal: " Yong bowed twice and said: "Your subject deserves to lie corpse in the marketplace as a warning for the future.
translations.idiomatic: Yong bowed twice and said: "Your subject deserves to be executed in the marketplace as a warning to posterity.

sentences.zh: 幸蒙哀憐，得全性命」。

translations.literal: Fortunately receiving pity, I preserve my life".
translations.idiomatic: By your mercy I am allowed to keep my life."

sentences.zh: 言畢，泣下流襟，既而舞蹈而去。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking, tears streamed down his collar; then he performed the dance of submission and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished, tears soaked his robe; then he performed the submission dance and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 左右莫不憫默。

translations.literal: Those nearby were all silent in compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Those present were all mute with pity.

sentences.zh: 又下詔：「左衛大將軍元旻，任掌禁兵，委以心膂，乃包藏奸伏，離間君親，崇長厲階，最為魁首。

translations.literal: An edict was also issued: "Left Guardian General Yuan Min, charged with holding the forbidden troops and entrusted as backbone support, yet harbored wickedness in secret, estranged ruler and kin, fomented and escalated the evil—foremost among the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was also issued: "Left Guardian General Yuan Min was charged with the forbidden troops and entrusted as the emperor's right hand, yet he harbored treachery, estranged ruler and kin, and fanned the evil—foremost among the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 太子左庶子唐令則，策名儲貳，位長宮僚，諂曲取容，音技自進，躬執樂器，親教內人，贊成驕侈，導引非法。

translations.literal: Left Household Subprefect of the Crown Prince Tang Lingze, by name a storehouse of the second rank, chief of palace staff, flattered and curried favor, advanced by musical skill, personally wielded instruments, personally teaching inner palace women, abetting proud extravagance, leading into unlawful ways.
translations.idiomatic: Left Household Subprefect of the Crown Prince Tang Lingze, registered in the heir's household and chief among palace staff, flattered his way forward, traded on musical skill, personally played instruments and taught palace women, abetted arrogance and excess, and led the crown prince into unlawful conduct.

sentences.zh: 太子家令鄒文騰，專行左道，偏被親昵，占問國家，希覬災禍。

translations.literal: Chief Steward of the Crown Prince Zou Wenteng, devoted exclusively to left paths, especially favored in intimacy, divining and questioning the state, hoping for calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Steward of the Crown Prince Zou Wenteng practiced heterodox arts alone, enjoyed special favor, divined about affairs of state, and hoped for disaster.

sentences.zh: 左衛率司馬夏侯福，內事諂諛，外作威勢，陵侮上下，褻濁宮闈。

translations.literal: Major of Left Guard Command Sima Xiahou Fu, inwardly serving with flattery, outwardly wielding power, insulting superiors and inferiors, polluting the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Major of Left Guard Command Sima Xiahou Fu flattered within and bullied without, insulted superiors and inferiors alike, and defiled the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 典膳監元淹，謬陳愛憎，開示怨隙，進引妖巫，營事厭禱。

translations.literal: Director of Imperial Provisions Yuan Yan, wrongly stating loves and hates, opening and revealing grievances, introducing and bringing in witch sorcerers, undertaking exorcism prayers.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Imperial Provisions Yuan Yan aired private likes and dislikes, opened old grievances, brought in witchcraft, and performed suppressive rites.

sentences.zh: 前吏部侍郎蕭子寶，往居省閣，舊非宮臣，進畫奸謀，要射榮利。

translations.literal: Former Vice Minister of the Ministry of Appointments Xiao Zibao, formerly dwelling in the ministry offices, originally not a palace official, advancing wicked plots, aiming to shoot at glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Former Vice Minister of the Ministry of Appointments Xiao Zibao, though once of the ministry and not originally a palace officer, advanced wicked plots and schemed for rank and profit.

sentences.zh: 前主璽下士何竦，假託玄象，妄說妖怪，志圖禍亂，心在速發；

translations.literal: Former Chief Clerk under the Imperial Seal He Song, falsely relying on dark omens, recklessly speaking of monsters and prodigies, intent on plotting turmoil and rebellion, heart set on swift outbreak;
translations.idiomatic: Former Chief Clerk under the Imperial Seal He Song invoked false celestial signs, spread talk of monsters and prodigies, plotted rebellion, and burned to act quickly;

sentences.zh: 兼諸奇服，皆竦規模，增長驕奢，糜費百姓。

translations.literal: Together with various strange garments, all modeled on Song's designs, increasing proud extravagance, wasting and spending the people's resources.
translations.idiomatic: together with various strange garments—all patterned after Song's designs—inflating arrogance and waste at the people's expense.

sentences.zh: 此之七人，為害斯甚，並處斬刑，妻妾子孫皆沒官。

translations.literal: These seven men—harmful beyond measure—all sentenced to execution by decapitation; wives, concubines, children and grandchildren all confiscated to official status.
translations.idiomatic: These seven men, harmful beyond measure, were all sentenced to decapitation; their wives, concubines, children, and grandchildren were all confiscated as government slaves.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍閻毗、東郡公崔君綽、游騎尉沈福寶、瀛州人章仇太翼等四人，所為之事，並是悖逆，論其狀跡，罪合極刑。

translations.literal: Cavalry General Yan Pi, Duke of Dongjun Cui Junchuo, Wandering Cavalry Commandant Shen Fubao, and Zhangchou Taiyi of Yingzhou—the four men's deeds were all in rebellion; judging their acts and traces, their crime merits extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry General Yan Pi, Duke of Dongjun Cui Junchuo, Wandering Cavalry Commandant Shen Fubao, and Zhangchou Taiyi of Yingzhou—the deeds of all four were rebellious; judged by their acts and evidence, their crimes merited the extreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 但未能盡戮，並特免死，各決杖一百，身及妻子資財田宅悉沒官。

translations.literal: But unable to execute all, all specially exempted from death; each given a hundred blows with the rod; person, wife and children, property and fields and houses all confiscated to official status.
translations.idiomatic: But unable to execute them all, all were specially spared death; each received a hundred blows with the rod; they themselves, their wives and children, and all their property, fields, and houses were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 副將作大匠高龍叉，預追番丁，輒配東宮使役，營造亭舍，進入春坊；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction Gao Longcha, who when pursuing corvée laborers arbitrarily assigned them to the Eastern Palace for service, building pavilions and lodges, entering the Spring Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction Gao Longcha, who when requisitioning corvée laborers arbitrarily assigned them to serve the Eastern Palace, building pavilions and lodges and entering the Spring Palace;

sentences.zh: 率更令晉文建、通直散騎侍郎判司農少卿事元衡，料度之外，私自出給，虛破丁功，擅割園地。

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia Jin Wenjian, and Attendant Palace Secretary on Direct Route concurrently administering affairs of Vice Minister of the Directorate of Agriculture Yuan Heng—beyond authorized estimates, privately issued supplies, falsely depleted corvée labor quotas, and arbitrarily seized parkland.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia Jin Wenjian, and Attendant Palace Secretary on Direct Route Yuan Heng, who concurrently administered the Directorate of Agriculture—beyond authorized estimates they privately issued supplies, falsely depleted corvée quotas, and arbitrarily seized parkland.

sentences.zh: 並處自盡，」於是集群官于廣陽門外，宣詔以戮之。

translations.literal: All were sentenced to take their own lives." Thereupon he gathered the officials outside Guangyang Gate and proclaimed the edict to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: All were sentenced to take their own lives." Thereupon the officials were gathered outside Guangyang Gate and the edict of execution was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 乃移勇於內史省，給五品料食。

translations.literal: Yong was then moved to the Palace Secretariat and given provisions for a fifth-rank official.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was then moved to the Palace Secretariat and given the provisions allowance of a fifth-rank official.

sentences.zh: 立晉王廣為皇太子，仍以勇付之，復囚於東宮。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin Guang was installed as crown prince; Yong was still handed over to him and again imprisoned in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin Guang was installed as crown prince; Yong was still placed in his charge and again imprisoned in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 賜楊素物三千段，元胄、楊約並千段，楊難敵五百段，皆鞫勇之功賞也。

translations.literal: Yang Su was granted three thousand bolts of goods, Yuan Zhou and Yang Yue a thousand each, and Yang Nandi five hundred—all rewards for their work in prosecuting Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su was granted three thousand bolts of goods, Yuan Zhou and Yang Yue a thousand each, and Yang Nandi five hundred—all rewards for prosecuting Yong.

sentences.zh: 時文林郎楊孝政上盡諫，言：「皇太子為小人所誤，不宜廢黜。

translations.literal: At that time Palace Secretary Yang Xiaozheng submitted a full remonstrance, saying: "The crown prince was misled by petty men and should not have been deposed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Palace Secretary Yang Xiaozheng submitted a full remonstrance, saying: "The crown prince was misled by petty men and should not have been deposed."

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，撻其胸。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was enraged and beat him on the chest.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged and beat him on the chest.

sentences.zh: 尋而貝州長史裴肅表稱：「庶人罪黜已久，當克已自新，請封一小國。

translations.literal: Soon after, Pei Su, Chief Administrator of Beizhou, memorialized: "The commoner has long borne punishment and dismissal; he should reform himself—please enfeoff him with a small state.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Pei Su, Chief Administrator of Beizhou, memorialized: "The commoner has long borne punishment and dismissal; he should reform himself—please enfeoff him with a small state."

sentences.zh: 」帝知勇黜不允天下情，乃徵肅入朝，具陳廢立意。

translations.literal: " The Emperor knew Yong's deposition did not accord with public sentiment; he therefore summoned Su to court and had him set forth in full the reasons for the deposition.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor knew Yong's deposition did not accord with public sentiment; he therefore summoned Su to court and had him set forth in full the reasons for the deposition.

sentences.zh: 時勇自以廢非其罪，頻請見上，面申冤屈。

translations.literal: At that time Yong, believing his deposition was not his fault, repeatedly requested audience with the Emperor to plead his innocence face to face.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yong, believing his deposition was unjust, repeatedly requested audience with the Emperor to plead his innocence in person.

sentences.zh: 皇太子遏不得聞。

translations.literal: The crown prince blocked the requests so they never reached the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince blocked the requests so they never reached the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 勇於是升樹叫，聞于帝，冀得引見。

translations.literal: Yong then climbed a tree and shouted, hoping the Emperor would hear and grant him an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yong then climbed a tree and shouted aloud, hoping the Emperor would hear and grant him an audience.

sentences.zh: 楊素因奏言：「勇情志昏亂，又癲鬼所著，不可復收。

translations.literal: Yang Su thereupon memorialized: "Yong's mind and emotions are deranged, and he is possessed by epileptic demons—he cannot be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su thereupon memorialized: "Yong's mind is deranged and he is possessed by demons—he cannot be restored."

sentences.zh: 」帝以為然，卒不得見。

translations.literal: " The Emperor agreed, and in the end Yong was never received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed, and in the end Yong was never received in audience.

sentences.zh: 帝遇疾于仁壽宮，皇太子入侍醫，奸亂事聞於帝。

translations.literal: When the Emperor fell ill at Renshou Palace, the crown prince entered to attend him medically, and news of his illicit conduct reached the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor fell ill at Renshou Palace, the crown prince entered to attend him, and news of his illicit conduct reached the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝抵床曰：「枉廢我兒！

translations.literal: The Emperor struck the bed and said: "I wrongly deposed my son!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor struck the bed and cried: "I wrongly deposed my son!"

sentences.zh: 」遣追勇。

translations.literal: " He sent to recall Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He sent to recall Yong.

sentences.zh: 未及發使而崩，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: Before the envoys could be dispatched he died; the death was kept secret and mourning not proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoys could be dispatched he died; the death was kept secret and mourning was not proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 遽收柳述、元岩，系大理獄，偽敕賜庶人死。

translations.literal: Liu Shu and Yuan Yan were quickly seized and imprisoned in the Court of Judicial Review; a forged edict ordered the commoner to die.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shu and Yuan Yan were quickly seized and imprisoned in the Court of Judicial Review; a forged edict ordered the commoner to die.

sentences.zh: 追封房陵王，不為立嗣。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Prince of Fangling, but no heir was established for him.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Prince of Fangling, but no heir was established for him.

sentences.zh: 勇有十男：雲昭訓生長寧王儼、平原王裕、安城王筠。

translations.literal: Yong had ten sons: Yun Zhaoxun bore Changning Wang Yan, Pingyuan Wang Yu, and Ancheng Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had ten sons: Yun Zhaoxun bore Changning Wang Yan, Pingyuan Wang Yu, and Ancheng Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 高良娣生安平王嶷、襄城王恪。

translations.literal: Concubine Gao bore Anping Wang Ni and Xiangcheng Wang Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Concubine Gao bore Anping Wang Ni and Xiangcheng Wang Ke.

sentences.zh: 王良媛生高陽王該、建安王韶。

translations.literal: Lady Wang bore Gaoyang Wang Gai and Jian'an Wang Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang bore Gaoyang Wang Gai and Jian'an Wang Shao.

sentences.zh: 成姬生潁川王煚。

translations.literal: Consort Cheng bore Yingchuan Wang Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Cheng bore Yingchuan Wang Jiong.

sentences.zh: 後宮生孝實、孝範。

translations.literal: Women of the inner palace bore Xiaoshi and Xiaofan.
translations.idiomatic: Women of the inner palace bore Xiaoshi and Xiaofan.

sentences.zh: 初，儼誕，帝聞之曰：「此乃皇太孫，何乃生不得地！

translations.literal: When Yan was first born, the Emperor heard of it and said: "This is the imperial grandson—why was he born in an ill-omened place!
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was first born, the Emperor heard of it and said: "This is the imperial grandson—why was he born in an ill-omened place!"

sentences.zh: 」雲定興奏曰：「天生龍種，所以因雲而出。

translations.literal: " Yun Dingxing replied: "Heaven-born is a dragon seed—therefore he emerged amid clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Dingxing replied: "Heaven-born is a dragon seed—therefore he emerged amid clouds."

sentences.zh: 」時人以為敏對。

translations.literal: " People at the time regarded this as a clever reply.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time regarded this as a clever reply.

sentences.zh: 六歲，封長寧郡王。

translations.literal: At six he was enfeoffed as Prince of Changning commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At six he was enfeoffed as Prince of Changning commandery.

sentences.zh: 勇敗，並坐廢。

translations.literal: When Yong was ruined, all were implicated and deposed together.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong was ruined, all were implicated and deposed together.

sentences.zh: 上表求宿衛，辭情哀切，帝覽之惻然。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting palace guard duty; the plea was piteous, and when the Emperor read it he was moved to pity.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial requesting palace guard duty; the plea was piteous, and when the Emperor read it he was moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 楊素進曰：「伏願聖心同於螫手，不宜留意。

translations.literal: Yang Su advanced and said: "I humbly wish that Your Majesty's heart be like one stung on the hand—do not take this to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su stepped forward and said: "I humbly wish Your Majesty's heart would be like one that cuts off a stung hand—do not take this to heart."

sentences.zh: 」煬帝踐祚，儼常從行，遇鴆卒。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Yang took the throne, Yan often accompanied him on journeys and died by poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Yan often accompanied him on journeys and died by poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 諸弟分徙嶺外，皆敕殺之。

translations.literal: His younger brothers were exiled separately beyond the mountain passes; all were ordered killed.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers were exiled separately beyond the mountain passes; all were ordered killed.

sentences.zh: 秦王俊，字阿祗。

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Jun, courtesy name Azhi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Jun, courtesy name Azhi.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，立為秦王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he was installed as Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he was installed as Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜上柱國、河南道行台尚書令、洛州刺史，時年十二。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Grand Preceptor, Chief Minister of the Henan Circuit Executive, and Prefect of Luozhou—at age twelve.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Grand Preceptor, Chief Minister of the Henan Circuit Executive, and Prefect of Luozhou—at age twelve.

sentences.zh: 加右武衛大將軍，領關東兵。

translations.literal: He was additionally made General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard and commanded the armies east of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard and commanded the armies east of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷秦州總管，隴右諸州盡隸焉。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to be Area Commander of Qinzhou, and all prefectures of Longyou were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Area Commander of Qinzhou, and all prefectures of Longyou were placed under him.

sentences.zh: 俊仁恕慈愛，崇敬佛道，請為沙門，不許。

translations.literal: Jun was kind, forgiving, and compassionate; he revered Buddhism and Daoism and requested to become a monk, but permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was kind, forgiving, and compassionate; he revered Buddhism and Daoism and requested to become a monk, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷山南道行台尚書令。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Chief Minister of the Southern Mountains Circuit Executive.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Chief Minister of the Southern Mountains Circuit Executive.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，為山南道行軍元帥，督三十總管，水陸十餘萬，屯漢口，為上流節度。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen he served as Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Mountains Circuit army, overseeing thirty area commanders and more than a hundred thousand men by land and water, encamped at Hankou as commander of the upper stream.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Chen he served as Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Mountains Circuit army, overseeing thirty area commanders and more than a hundred thousand men by land and water, encamped at Hankou as commander of the upper stream.

sentences.zh: 尋授揚州總管、四十四州諸軍事，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made Area Commander of Yangzhou with military authority over forty-four prefectures, stationed at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made Area Commander of Yangzhou with military authority over forty-four prefectures, stationed at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 轉并州總管、二十四州諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Area Commander of Bingzhou with military authority over twenty-four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Area Commander of Bingzhou with military authority over twenty-four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 初頗有令問，文帝聞而大悅。

translations.literal: At first he had quite a good reputation; Emperor Wen heard of it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At first he had quite a good reputation; Emperor Wen heard of it and was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 後漸奢侈，違犯制度，出錢求息。

translations.literal: Later he gradually grew extravagant, violated regulations, and lent money for interest.
translations.idiomatic: Later he gradually grew extravagant, violated regulations, and lent money for interest.

sentences.zh: 帝遣按其事，與相連坐者百餘人。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent to investigate; more than a hundred people were implicated with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent to investigate; more than a hundred people were implicated with him.

sentences.zh: 於是盛修宮室，窮極侈麗。

translations.literal: Thereupon he lavishly built palaces to the utmost of luxury.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he lavishly built palaces to the utmost of luxury.

sentences.zh: 俊有巧思，每親運斤斧，工巧之器，飾以珠玉。

translations.literal: Jun had ingenuity; he often personally wielded axe and adze, and his ingenious contrivances were adorned with pearls and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had ingenuity; he often personally wielded axe and adze, and his ingenious contrivances were adorned with pearls and jade.

sentences.zh: 為妃作七寶幕籬，重不可戴，以馬負之而行。

translations.literal: For his consort he made a seven-jewel canopy screen so heavy it could not be worn on the head—a horse had to carry it when they moved.
translations.idiomatic: For his consort he made a seven-jewel canopy screen so heavy it could not be worn on the head—a horse had to carry it when they moved.

sentences.zh: 徵役無已。

translations.literal: Corvée levies never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée levies never ceased.

sentences.zh: 置渾天儀、測景表。

translations.literal: He installed an armillary sphere and a gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: He installed an armillary sphere and a gnomon.

sentences.zh: 又為水殿，香塗粉壁，玉砌金堦，梁柱楣棟之間，周以明鏡，間以寶珠，極瑩飾之美。

translations.literal: He also built a water palace with perfumed plaster and whitewashed walls, jade steps and golden stairs; between columns, beams, lintels, and rafters he ringed the hall with bright mirrors interspersed with jewels, to the utmost of glittering ornament.
translations.idiomatic: He also built a water palace with perfumed plaster and whitewashed walls, jade steps and golden stairs; between columns, beams, lintels, and rafters he ringed the hall with bright mirrors interspersed with jewels, to the utmost of glittering ornament.

sentences.zh: 每與賓客伎女弦歌於上。

translations.literal: He often feasted with guests and singing girls, making music upon it.
translations.idiomatic: He often feasted with guests and singing girls, making music upon it.

sentences.zh: 俊頗好內，妃崔氏性妒，甚不平之，遂於瓜中進毒。

translations.literal: Jun was quite fond of women; his consort Lady Cui was jealous and greatly resentful, and so put poison in a melon.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was quite fond of women; his consort Lady Cui was jealous and greatly resentful, and so put poison in a melon.

sentences.zh: 俊由是遇疾，徵還京師。

translations.literal: Jun thereby fell ill and was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jun thereby fell ill and was summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 以俊奢縱，免官，以王就第。

translations.literal: Because of Jun's extravagant indulgence, he was dismissed from office and allowed to remain prince at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Jun's extravagant indulgence, he was dismissed from office and allowed to remain prince at his residence.

sentences.zh: 左武衛將軍劉升諫曰：「秦王非有他過，但費官物、營廨舍而已。

translations.literal: Left Martial Guard General Liu Sheng remonstrated: "The Prince of Qin has no other fault—he merely wasted official goods and built offices and lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Left Martial Guard General Liu Sheng remonstrated: "The Prince of Qin has no other fault—he merely wasted official goods and built offices and lodges."

sentences.zh: 臣謂可容。

translations.literal: Your subject believes this can be tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes this can be tolerated.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「法不可違。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "The law cannot be violated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "The law cannot be violated."

sentences.zh: 」升固諫，帝忿然作色，升乃止。

translations.literal: " Sheng pressed his remonstrance; the Emperor flushed with anger, and Sheng stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng pressed his remonstrance; the Emperor flushed with anger, and Sheng stopped.

sentences.zh: 楊素復進諫，以秦王過不應至此。

translations.literal: Yang Su again remonstrated, saying the Prince of Qin's fault did not merit punishment to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su again remonstrated, saying the Prince of Qin's fault did not merit punishment to this degree.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我是五兒之父，非兆人之父。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I am the father of five sons, not the father of the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "I am the father of five sons, not the father of the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 若如公意，何不別制天子兒律！

translations.literal: If it were as you suggest, why not make a separate law for the Son of Heaven's sons!
translations.idiomatic: If it were as you suggest, why not make a separate law for the Son of Heaven's sons!

sentences.zh: 以周公為人，尚誅管、蔡。

translations.literal: Even the Duke of Zhou, for all his virtue, still executed Guan and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Duke of Zhou, for all his virtue, still executed Guan and Cai.

sentences.zh: 我誠不及周公遠矣，安能虧法乎！

translations.literal: I truly fall far short of the Duke of Zhou—how could I bend the law!
translations.idiomatic: I truly fall far short of the Duke of Zhou—how could I bend the law!

sentences.zh: 」卒不許。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 湛驍果有膽烈。

translations.literal: Zhan was fierce and bold, with daring spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was fierce and bold, with daring spirit.

sentences.zh: 大業初，為滎陽太守，坐浩免，亦為化及所害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he served as Administrator of Xingyang; he was dismissed on account of Yang Hao and was also killed by Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye he served as Administrator of Xingyang; he was dismissed on account of Yang Hao and was also killed by Huaji.

sentences.zh: 庶人秀，開皇元年，立為越王。

translations.literal: The commoner Xiu, in the first year of Kaihuang, was installed as Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The commoner Xiu, in the first year of Kaihuang, was installed as Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徙封於蜀，拜柱國、益州總管、二十四州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred and enfeoffed in Shu, appointed Pillar of State, Area Commander of Yizhou, and military commander over twenty-four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred and enfeoffed in Shu, appointed Pillar of State, Area Commander of Yizhou, and military commander over twenty-four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二年，進上柱國、西南道行台尚書令，本官如故。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to Grand Preceptor and Chief Minister of the Southwest Circuit Executive, his other posts remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to Grand Preceptor and Chief Minister of the Southwest Circuit Executive, his other posts remaining as before.

sentences.zh: 歲餘而罷。

translations.literal: After a year or more he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After a year or more he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十二年，入為內史令、右領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he entered the capital as Director of the Palace Secretariat and General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he entered the capital as Director of the Palace Secretariat and General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋出鎮於蜀。

translations.literal: Soon after he went out to garrison Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he went out to garrison Shu.

sentences.zh: 秀有膽氣，容貌瑰偉，美有須髯，多武藝，甚為朝臣所憚。

translations.literal: Xiu had daring spirit; his appearance was magnificent, his beard handsome, and he was skilled in many martial arts—officials greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu had daring spirit; his appearance was magnificent, his beard handsome, and he was skilled in many martial arts—officials greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 帝每謂文獻皇后曰：「秀必以惡終。

translations.literal: The Emperor often said to Empress Wenxian: "Xiu will come to a bad end.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often said to Empress Wenxian: "Xiu will come to a bad end.

sentences.zh: 我在當無慮，至兄弟必反。

translations.literal: While I live there is no worry, but when it reaches his brothers he will rebel.
translations.idiomatic: While I live there is no worry, but when it reaches his brothers he will rebel.

sentences.zh: 」兵部侍郎元衡使於蜀，秀深結於衡，以左右為請。

translations.literal: " Vice Minister of War Yuan Heng was sent as envoy to Shu; Xiu formed a deep bond with Heng and requested attendants through him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Yuan Heng was sent as envoy to Shu; Xiu formed a deep bond with Heng and requested attendants through him.

sentences.zh: 衡既還京師，請益左右，帝不許。

translations.literal: When Heng returned to the capital he requested more attendants; the Emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: When Heng returned to the capital he requested more attendants; the Emperor did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 大將軍劉噲之討西爨，帝令上開府楊武通將兵繼進。

translations.literal: General Liu Huanzhi campaigned against the Western Cuan; the Emperor ordered Senior Opening Grandee Yang Wutong to lead troops in follow-up advance.
translations.idiomatic: General Liu Huanzhi campaigned against the Western Cuan; the Emperor ordered Senior Opening Grandee Yang Wutong to lead troops in follow-up advance.

sentences.zh: 秀使嬖人萬知先為武通行軍司馬，帝以秀任非其人，譴責之，因謂群臣曰：「壞我法者，必在子孫。

translations.literal: Xiu had his favorite Wan Zhixian serve as Rear Camp Marshal for Yang Wutong; the Emperor, holding that Xiu had appointed the wrong man, rebuked him, and said to the officials: "Those who ruin my laws will surely be among my descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu had his favorite Wan Zhixian serve as Rear Camp Marshal for Yang Wutong; the Emperor, holding that Xiu had appointed the wrong man, rebuked him, and said to the officials: "Those who ruin my laws will surely be among my descendants.

sentences.zh: 譬如猛獸，物不能害，反為毛間蟲所損食耳。

translations.literal: Like a fierce beast that nothing can harm, yet damaged by insects in its fur.
translations.idiomatic: Like a fierce beast that nothing can harm, yet damaged by insects in its fur.

sentences.zh: 」於是遂分秀所統。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xiu's command was divided.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xiu's command was divided.

sentences.zh: 秀漸奢侈，違犯制度，車馬被服擬于天子。

translations.literal: Xiu gradually grew extravagant, violated regulations, and his carriages, horses, and dress rivaled the Son of Heaven's.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu gradually grew extravagant, violated regulations, and his carriages, horses, and dress rivaled the Son of Heaven's.

sentences.zh: 及太子勇廢，秀甚不平。

translations.literal: When the crown prince Yong was deposed, Xiu was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince Yong was deposed, Xiu was greatly displeased.

sentences.zh: 皇太子恐秀終為後變，陰令楊素求其罪狀而譖之。

translations.literal: The crown prince feared Xiu would eventually become a future threat; he secretly had Yang Su seek out evidence of his crimes and slander him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince feared Xiu would eventually become a future threat; he secretly had Yang Su seek out evidence of his crimes and slander him.

sentences.zh: 仁壽二年，徵還京師，見不與語。

translations.literal: In the second year of Renshou he was summoned back to the capital; on audience the Emperor did not speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Renshou he was summoned back to the capital; on audience the Emperor did not speak with him.

sentences.zh: 明日，使使切讓之。

translations.literal: The next day he sent envoys to rebuke him sharply.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent envoys to rebuke him sharply.

sentences.zh: 皇太子及諸王流涕庭謝，帝曰：「頃者俊糜費財物，我以父道訓之。

translations.literal: The crown prince and the princes wept in the courtyard to apologize; the Emperor said: "Recently Jun wasted goods—I admonished him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and the princes wept in the courtyard to apologize; the Emperor said: "Recently Jun wasted goods—I admonished him as a father.

sentences.zh: 今秀蠹害生靈，當以君道繩之。

translations.literal: Now Xiu harms the people like a pest—I must restrain him as a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xiu harms the people like a pest—I must restrain him as a ruler.

sentences.zh: 」乃下以法。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he handed him over to the law.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he handed him over to the law.

sentences.zh: 開府慶整諫曰：「庶人勇既廢，秦王已薨，陛下兒子無多，何至如是！

translations.literal: Opening Grandee Qing Zheng remonstrated: "The commoner Yong is already deposed and the Prince of Qin is dead—Your Majesty has not many sons left; how can it come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Opening Grandee Qing Zheng remonstrated: "The commoner Yong is already deposed and the Prince of Qin is dead—Your Majesty has not many sons left; how can it come to this!

sentences.zh: 蜀王性甚耿介，今被責，恐不自全。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu is very upright by nature; now that he is rebuked, I fear he will not preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shu is very upright by nature; now that he is rebuked, I fear he will not preserve himself.

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，欲斷其舌。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was furious and wanted to cut out his tongue.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and wanted to cut out his tongue.

sentences.zh: 因謂群臣曰：「當斬秀于市以謝百姓。

translations.literal: He then said to the officials: "Xiu should be beheaded in the marketplace to answer to the people.
translations.idiomatic: He then said to the officials: "Xiu should be beheaded in the marketplace to answer to the people.

sentences.zh: 」乃令楊素、蘇威、牛弘、柳述、趙綽推之。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Yang Su, Su Wei, Niu Hong, Liu Shu, and Zhao Chuo to investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Yang Su, Su Wei, Niu Hong, Liu Shu, and Zhao Chuo to investigate him.

sentences.zh: 太子陰作偶人，書帝及漢王姓字，縛手釘心，令人埋之華山下，令楊素髮之。

translations.literal: The crown prince secretly made effigies bearing the Emperor's and the Prince of Han's names, bound their hands and nailed their hearts, had them buried beneath Mount Hua, and had Yang Su exhume them.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince secretly made effigies bearing the Emperor's and the Prince of Han's names, bound their hands and nailed their hearts, had them buried beneath Mount Hua, and had Yang Su exhume them.

sentences.zh: 又作檄文曰「逆臣賊子，專弄威柄，陛下唯守虛器，一無所知」，陳甲兵之盛，云「指期問罪」，置秀集中，因以聞奏。

translations.literal: He also composed a manifesto saying "Rebellious ministers and wicked sons monopolize power; Your Majesty merely holds an empty vessel and knows nothing," described the strength of armored troops, and wrote "We shall soon call them to account"; he placed it among Xiu's papers and thereby reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He also composed a manifesto saying "Rebellious ministers and wicked sons monopolize power; Your Majesty merely holds an empty vessel and knows nothing," described the strength of armored troops, and wrote "We shall soon call them to account"; he placed it among Xiu's papers and thereby reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「天下寧有是邪！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "How could such a thing exist in the world!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "How could such a thing exist in the world!"

sentences.zh: 」乃廢為庶人，幽之內侍省，不得與妻子相見，令給獠婢二人驅使之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was deposed as a commoner, imprisoned in the Palace Domestic Service, not permitted to see his wife and children, and given two Liao maidservants to drive him about.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was deposed as a commoner and imprisoned in the Palace Domestic Service. He was not permitted to see his wife and children, and was given two Liao maidservants to command him.

sentences.zh: 與連坐百餘人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred people were implicated with him.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred people were implicated along with him.

sentences.zh: 秀既幽逼，憤懣不知所為，乃上表陳己愆，請與其愛子爪子相見，並請賜一穴，今骸骨有所。

translations.literal: Xiu, being closely confined, was resentful and did not know what to do; he submitted a memorial confessing his faults, requesting to see his beloved son Zhuaizi, and also requesting a grave plot so his bones would have a resting place.
translations.idiomatic: Close confinement left Xiu resentful and at a loss. He submitted a memorial confessing his faults, asking to see his beloved son Zhuaizi and requesting a burial plot so his bones would have somewhere to rest.

sentences.zh: 帝乃下詔數其罪曰：「汝地居臣子，情兼家國，庸蜀險要，委以鎮之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then issued an edict enumerating his crimes, saying: "By your station you are both subject and son, your feeling embracing family and state; Yung and Shu are strategically vital—I entrusted you to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then issued an edict enumerating his crimes, saying: "By your station you are both subject and son, with obligations to family and state alike. Yung and Shu are strategically vital—I entrusted you to guard them.

sentences.zh: 汝乃幹紀亂常，懷惡樂禍，暿辟睨二宮，佇望災釁，容納不逞，結構異端。

translations.literal: Yet you violated law and disrupted order, harbored evil and rejoiced in disaster, cast sidelong glances at the two palaces, waited for calamity and omen, harbored the unbridled, and formed factions of heterodoxy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you violated law and disrupted order, harbored evil and rejoiced in disaster, cast sidelong glances at the two palaces, waited for calamity and misfortune, sheltered the unbridled, and formed factions of heresy.

sentences.zh: 我有不和，汝便覘候，望我不起，便有異心。

translations.literal: When I was indisposed, you spied and watched; when you hoped I would not rise, you harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: When I fell ill, you spied and watched; hoping I would not recover, you harbored rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 皇太子，汝兄也，次當建立，汝假託妖言，乃雲不終其位。

translations.literal: The crown prince is your elder brother—he is next to be established; you falsely relied on demonic talk, saying he would not complete his tenure.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is your elder brother and the rightful heir; yet you spread demonic rumors claiming he would not hold his position to the end.

sentences.zh: 妄稱鬼怪，又道不得入宮，自言骨相非人臣，德業堪承重器。

translations.literal: You falsely spoke of ghosts and demons, also saying you might not enter the palace, and declared that your bone structure was not that of a minister—that your virtue and merit could bear the heavy vessel.
translations.idiomatic: You spoke falsely of ghosts and demons, claimed you were forbidden to enter the palace, and declared that your bone structure marked you as no mere subject—that your virtue and merit qualified you to bear the imperial burden.

sentences.zh: 妄道清城出聖，欲己當之，詐稱益州龍見，托言吉兆。

translations.literal: You falsely said a sage would emerge from Qingcheng and wished to take that role yourself; you fraudulently claimed a dragon appeared in Yizhou, presenting it as an auspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: You falsely prophesied that a sage would emerge from Qingcheng and wished to claim that destiny yourself; you fraudulently claimed a dragon appeared in Yizhou and presented it as an auspicious omen.

sentences.zh: 重述木易之姓，更修成都之宮。

translations.literal: You again recited the surname 'Wood-Easy' and further renovated the palace at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: You again invoked the riddle of the surname Mu-Yi and further renovated the palace at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 妄說禾乃之名，以當八千之運。

translations.literal: You falsely spoke the name 'Grain-Nai,' matching it to the cycle of eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: You falsely invoked the riddle of the name He-Nai, matching it to the cycle of eight thousand years.

sentences.zh: 橫生京師妖異，以證父兄之災；

translations.literal: You fabricated prodigies and omens in the capital to prove disaster for father and brothers;
translations.idiomatic: You fabricated prodigies and omens in the capital to foretell disaster for your father and brothers;

sentences.zh: 妄造蜀地徵祥，以符已身之籙。

translations.literal: You falsely manufactured auspicious signs in Shu to match your own destined mandate.
translations.idiomatic: You falsely manufactured auspicious signs in Shu to match your own destined mandate of rule.

sentences.zh: 汝豈不欲得國家惡也？

translations.literal: Do you not wish the state ill?
translations.idiomatic: Do you not wish harm upon the state?

sentences.zh: 天下亂也？

translations.literal: The realm in chaos?
translations.idiomatic: The realm thrown into chaos?

sentences.zh: 輒造白玉之珽，又為白羽之箭，文物服飾，豈似有君？

translations.literal: You readily made a white-jade scepter and white-feathered arrows—in regalia, dress, and ornament, do these not resemble a ruler's?
translations.idiomatic: You had a white-jade scepter made and white-feathered arrows fashioned—in regalia, dress, and ornament, do these not befit a ruler?

sentences.zh: 鳩集左道，符書厭鎮，漢王與汝，親則弟也，乃畫其形像，題其姓名，縛手釘心，枷鎖杻械。

translations.literal: You gathered heterodox arts, talismanic writings, and curse-suppression charms; the Prince of Han is your younger brother by kin—you painted his likeness, inscribed his name, bound the hands and nailed the heart, and applied cangue, manacles, and fetters.
translations.idiomatic: You gathered heterodox arts, talismanic writings, and curse-suppression charms; the Prince of Han is your younger brother by kin—you painted his likeness, inscribed his name, bound his hands and nailed his heart, and applied cangue, manacles, and fetters.

sentences.zh: 仍雲請西嶽華山慈父聖母神兵九億萬騎，收楊諒魂神，閉在華山下，勿令散蕩。

translations.literal: You further said you prayed to the Compassionate Father and Holy Mother of Mount Hua of the Western Peak for nine hundred million divine troops to seize the soul of Yang Liang and confine it beneath Mount Hua, not letting it scatter.
translations.idiomatic: You further claimed to have prayed to the Compassionate Father and Holy Mother of Mount Hua of the Western Peak for nine hundred million divine troops to seize Yang Liang's soul and confine it beneath Mount Hua, not letting it scatter.

sentences.zh: 我之於汝，親則父也，復雲請西嶽華山慈父聖母，賜為開化楊堅夫妻，回心歡喜。

translations.literal: To you I am kin as father—yet you again said you prayed to the Compassionate Father and Holy Mother of Mount Hua of the Western Peak to grant you the married name Kaifua Yang Jian and wife, with joyful change of heart.
translations.idiomatic: To you I am kin as father—yet you again claimed to have prayed to the Compassionate Father and Holy Mother of Mount Hua of the Western Peak to grant you the married name Kaifua Yang Jian and wife, with joyful change of heart.
