sentences.zh: 又畫我形像，縛手撮頭，仍雲請西嶽神兵收楊堅魂神。

translations.literal: You also painted my likeness, bound the hands and clutched the head, and again said you prayed for Western Peak divine troops to seize the soul of Yang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: You also painted my likeness, bound the hands and clutched the head, and again claimed to have prayed for Western Peak divine troops to seize Yang Jian's soul.

sentences.zh: 如此形狀，我今不知楊諒、楊堅是汝何親也！

translations.literal: In such fashion—I now do not know what kin Yang Liang and Yang Jian are to you!
translations.idiomatic: In such fashion—I cannot tell what relation Yang Liang and Yang Jian bear to you!

sentences.zh: 包藏凶匿，圖謀不軌，逆臣之跡也。

translations.literal: Concealing evil and plotting rebellion—the mark of a traitor.
translations.idiomatic: Concealing evil and plotting rebellion—the mark of a traitorous minister.

sentences.zh: 希父之災，以為身幸，賊子之心也。

translations.literal: Hoping for your father's disaster as personal fortune—the heart of a wicked son.
translations.idiomatic: Hoping for your father's disaster as your own good fortune—the heart of a wicked son.

sentences.zh: 懷非分之望，肆毒心于兄，悖惡之行也。

translations.literal: Harbouring improper ambition and venting malice on your elder brother—conduct of perverse wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Harbouring improper ambition and venting malice upon your elder brother—conduct of perverse wickedness.

sentences.zh: 嫉妒于弟，無惡不為，無孔懷之情也。

translations.literal: Jealous of younger brothers, doing every evil, without bond of brotherly feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous of younger brothers, doing every evil, without the bond of brotherly feeling.

sentences.zh: 違犯制度，壞亂之極也。

translations.literal: Violating regulations—the height of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Violating regulations—the utmost of disorder.

sentences.zh: 多殺不辜，豺狼之暴也。

translations.literal: Killing many innocents—the savagery of wolves.
translations.idiomatic: Killing many innocents—the savagery of wolves and jackals.

sentences.zh: 剝削人庶，酷虐之甚也。

translations.literal: Extorting the people—the height of cruel tyranny.
translations.idiomatic: Extorting the common people—the height of cruel tyranny.

sentences.zh: 唯求財貨，市井之業也。

translations.literal: Seeking only wealth—the trade of the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking only wealth and goods—the trade of the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 專事妖邪，頑囂之性也。

translations.literal: Devoting yourself to evil spirits—the nature of the obstinate and arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Devoting yourself to evil spirits and sorcery—the nature of the obstinate and arrogant.

sentences.zh: 弗克負荷，不材之器也。

translations.literal: Unable to bear the burden—vessel of no talent.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear the burden—an untalented vessel.

sentences.zh: 凡此十者，滅天理，逆人倫，汝皆為之，不祥之甚也。

translations.literal: All these ten things destroy heavenly principle and violate human relations—you have done them all; the ill omen is extreme.
translations.idiomatic: All these ten things destroy heavenly principle and violate human relations—you have done them all; the ill omen could not be greater.

sentences.zh: 欲免患禍，長守富貴，其可得乎！

translations.literal: To escape calamity and long preserve wealth and nobility—how could that be possible!
translations.idiomatic: To escape disaster and long preserve wealth and nobility—how could that be possible!

sentences.zh: 」後聽與其子同處。

translations.literal: " Afterward he permitted Xiu to dwell with his son.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he permitted Xiu to dwell with his son.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，禁錮如初。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, confinement continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, his imprisonment continued as before.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之弑逆也，欲立秀為帝，群議不許。

translations.literal: At Yuwen Huaji's regicide, he wished to install Xiu as emperor; the group would not assent.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuwen Huaji's regicide, he wished to install Xiu as emperor, but the assembled officials would not assent.

sentences.zh: 於是害之，並其諸子。

translations.literal: Thereupon they killed him, together with all his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they killed him, together with all his sons.

sentences.zh: 諒自以居天下精兵處，以太子讒廢，居常怏怏，陰有異圖。

translations.literal: Liang, believing himself stationed where the empire's best troops were, and that the crown prince had deposed him through slander, was often discontented and secretly harbored designs.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, believing himself stationed where the empire's best troops were gathered, and that the crown prince had deposed him through slander, was often discontented and secretly harbored rebellious designs.

sentences.zh: 遂諷帝云：「突厥方強，太原即為重鎮，宜修武備。

translations.literal: He therefore hinted to the Emperor: "The Turks are growing strong; Taiyuan is a vital stronghold—it is fitting to strengthen military readiness.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore hinted to the Emperor: "The Turks are growing strong; Taiyuan is a vital stronghold—it is fitting to strengthen military readiness."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 於是大發工役，繕修器械，貯納於并州。

translations.literal: Thereupon corvée was massively mobilized, weapons repaired, and stores accumulated at Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon corvée labor was massively mobilized, weapons were repaired, and stores were accumulated at Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 招集亡命，左右私人，殆將數萬。

translations.literal: Outlaws were recruited and personal retainers gathered—nearly tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Outlaws were recruited and personal retainers gathered—nearly ten thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 王頍者，梁將王僧辯之子，少倜儻，有奇略，為諒諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Wang Pi was the son of Liang general Wang Sengbian—bold and talented in youth, with unusual stratagems—he served as Liang's advisory staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi was the son of Liang general Wang Sengbian—bold and talented in youth, with unusual stratagems—he served as Liang's advisory staff officer.

sentences.zh: 蕭摩訶者，陳氏舊將。

translations.literal: Xiao Mohe was a former Chen general.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mohe was a former general of Chen.

sentences.zh: 二人俱不得志，每鬱鬱思亂，並為諒親善。

translations.literal: Both were frustrated in their ambitions, often brooding on rebellion, and were both on intimate terms with Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Both were frustrated in their ambitions, often brooding on rebellion, and were both on intimate terms with Liang.

sentences.zh: 及蜀王以罪廢，諒愈不自安。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shu was deposed for his crimes, Liang grew even more ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Shu was deposed for his crimes, Liang grew even more ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 會文帝崩，使車騎屈突通征之，不赴，遂發兵反。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the Emperor sent Cavalry General Qu Tuo to summon him; he did not come and raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died, the new emperor sent Cavalry General Qu Tuo to summon him; he did not come and raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 總管司馬皇甫誕諫，諒怒，收系之。

translations.literal: Area Commander's aide Huangfu Dan remonstrated; Liang was angry and had him arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Area Commander's aide Huangfu Dan remonstrated; Liang was enraged and had him arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 王頍說諒曰：「王所部將吏家屬盡在關西，若用此等，即宜長驅深入，直據京都，所謂疾雷不及掩耳。

translations.literal: Wang Pi urged Liang: "Your generals and officers' families are all west of the Pass—if you use these men, you should drive deep at full speed and seize the capital directly—the proverb says thunder is too swift for one to cover one's ears.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi urged Liang: "Your generals and officers' families are all west of the Pass—if you use these men, you should drive deep at full speed and seize the capital directly—as the proverb says, thunder is too swift for one to cover one's ears.

sentences.zh: 若但欲割據舊齊之地，宜任東人。

translations.literal: If you only wish to carve out the old Qi territory, you should employ eastern men.
translations.idiomatic: If you only wish to carve out the old Qi territory, you should employ men from the east.

sentences.zh: 」諒不能專之。

translations.literal: " Liang could not commit to either alone.
translations.idiomatic: Liang could not commit to either plan alone.

sentences.zh: 乃兼用二策，唱言：「楊素反，將誅之。」

translations.literal: He therefore used both plans together, proclaiming: "Yang Su has rebelled—we shall execute him."
translations.idiomatic: He therefore used both plans together, proclaiming: "Yang Su has rebelled—we shall execute him."

sentences.zh: 總管府兵曹河東裴文安說諒曰：「井陘以西，是王掌據內，山東士馬，亦為我有，宜悉發之。

translations.literal: Area Commander's office military clerk Pei Wen'an of Hedong urged Liang: "West of Jingxing is territory you hold; Shandong's soldiers and horses are also ours—you should deploy them all.
translations.idiomatic: Area Commander's office military clerk Pei Wen'an of Hedong urged Liang: "West of Jingxing is territory you hold; Shandong's soldiers and horses are also ours—you should deploy them all.

sentences.zh: 分遣羸兵，屯守要路，仍令隨方略地；

translations.literal: Send weak troops in detachments to garrison key routes, still having them advance according to terrain;
translations.idiomatic: Send weak troops in detachments to garrison key routes, still having them advance according to terrain;

sentences.zh: 率其精銳，直入蒲津。

translations.literal: Lead your elite forces straight into Pujin.
translations.idiomatic: Lead your elite forces straight into Pujin.

sentences.zh: 文安請為前鋒，王以大軍繼後，風行電擊，頓於霸上，咸陽以東可指麾而定。

translations.literal: Wen'an asks to serve as vanguard; Your Highness follows with the main army—swift as wind and lightning you halt at Bashang; east of Xianyang can be secured at a wave of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Let Wen'an serve as vanguard while Your Highness follows with the main army—swift as wind and lightning you halt at Bashang; east of Xianyang can be secured at a wave of the hand.

sentences.zh: 京師震擾，兵不暇集，上下相疑，群情離駭，我即陳兵號令，誰敢不從！

translations.literal: The capital will be shaken; troops will not have time to assemble; superiors and subordinates will suspect each other; the multitude will scatter in alarm—we need only deploy troops and issue commands—who would dare disobey!
translations.idiomatic: The capital will be shaken; troops will not have time to assemble; superiors and subordinates will suspect each other; the multitude will scatter in alarm—we need only deploy troops and issue commands—who would dare disobey!

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，事可定矣。

translations.literal: Within ten days the matter can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the matter can be settled.

sentences.zh: 」諒大悅。

translations.literal: " Liang was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 於是遣所署大將軍余公理將兵出太谷，以趣河陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent his appointed Grand General Yu Gongli to lead troops out through Taigu toward Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sent his appointed Grand General Yu Gongli to lead troops out through Taigu toward Heyang.

sentences.zh: 大將軍綦良出滏口，以趣黎陽。

translations.literal: Grand General Qi Liang out through Fukou toward Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Qi Liang marched out through Fukou toward Liyang.

sentences.zh: 大將軍鄧建出井陘，以略燕、趙。

translations.literal: Grand General Deng Jian out through Jingxing to overrun Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Deng Jian marched out through Jingxing to overrun Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 柱國喬鍾馗出雁門。

translations.literal: Pillar of State Qiao Zhongkui out through Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar of State Qiao Zhongkui marched out through Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 署文安為柱國，紇單貴、王聃、大將軍茹茹天保、侯莫陳惠直指京師。

translations.literal: He appointed Wen'an Pillar of State; Gedan Gui, Wang Dan, Grand General Ruru Tianbao, and Hou Mo Chen Hui marched straight on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Wen'an Pillar of State; Gedan Gui, Wang Dan, Grand General Ruru Tianbao, and Hou Mo Chen Hui marched straight on the capital.

sentences.zh: 未至蒲津百餘里。

translations.literal: When still more than a hundred li from Pujin.
translations.idiomatic: When they were still more than a hundred li from Pujin.

sentences.zh: 諒忽改圖，令紇單貴斷河橋，守蒲州，而召文安。

translations.literal: Liang suddenly changed plans, ordered Gedan Gui to break the river bridge and hold Puzhou, and recalled Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liang suddenly changed plans, ordered Gedan Gui to break the river bridge and hold Puzhou, and recalled Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 文安至曰：「兵機詭速，本欲出其不意。

translations.literal: When Wen'an arrived he said: "Military opportunity relies on cunning speed—the intent was to catch them unawares.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen'an arrived he said: "Military opportunity relies on cunning speed—the intent was to catch them unawares.

sentences.zh: 王既不行，文安又返，使彼計成，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Your Highness neither advances nor I return—their plans succeed and the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness neither advances nor I return—their plans succeed and the great affair is lost.

sentences.zh: 」諒不對。

translations.literal: " Liang made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Liang made no reply.

sentences.zh: 於是從亂者十九州，乃以王聃為蒲州刺史，裴文安為晉州，薛粹為絳州，梁菩薩為潞州，韋道正為韓州，張伯英為澤州。

translations.literal: Thereupon nineteen prefectures joined the rebellion; he appointed Wang Dan Administrator of Puzhou, Pei Wen'an of Jinzhou, Xue Cui of Jiangzhou, Liang Pusa of Luzhou, Wei Daozheng of Hanzhou, and Zhang Boying of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon nineteen prefectures joined the rebellion; he appointed Wang Dan Administrator of Puzhou, Pei Wen'an of Jinzhou, Xue Cui of Jiangzhou, Liang Pusa of Luzhou, Wei Daozheng of Hanzhou, and Zhang Boying of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 遣偽署大將軍常倫進兵絳州，遇晉州司法仲孝俊之子，謂曰：「吾曉天文遁甲，今年起兵，得晉地者王。

translations.literal: He sent the falsely appointed Grand General Chang Lun to advance on Jiangzhou; he met the son of Jinzhou judicial officer Zhong Xiaojun and said: "I know astronomy and dunjia—whoever raises troops this year and gains Jin territory will be king.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the falsely appointed Grand General Chang Lun to advance on Jiangzhou; he met the son of Jinzhou judicial officer Zhong Xiaojun and said: "I know astronomy and dunjia—whoever raises troops this year and gains Jin territory will be king.

sentences.zh: 」孝俊聞之曰：「皇太子常為晉王，故曰晉地，非謂反徒也。

translations.literal: " Xiaojun heard this and said: "The crown prince was once Prince of Jin, hence Jin territory—it does not refer to rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojun heard this and said: "The crown prince was once Prince of Jin, hence Jin territory—it does not refer to rebels.

sentences.zh: 」時潞州有官羊生羔，二首相背，以為諒之咎徵。

translations.literal: " At that time in Luzhou an official sheep gave birth to a lamb with two heads facing opposite directions, taken as an omen of Liang's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: At that time in Luzhou an official sheep gave birth to a lamb with two heads facing opposite directions, taken as an omen of Liang's guilt.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣楊素率騎五千，襲王聃、紇單貴于蒲州，破之，於是率步騎四萬趣太原。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang sent Yang Su with five thousand cavalry to strike Wang Dan and Gedan Gui at Puzhou and defeat them; he then led forty thousand infantry and cavalry toward Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent Yang Su with five thousand cavalry to strike Wang Dan and Gedan Gui at Puzhou and defeat them; he then led forty thousand infantry and cavalry toward Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 諒使趙子開守高壁，楊素擊走之。

translations.literal: Liang had Zhao Zikai hold Gaobi; Yang Su attacked and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had Zhao Zikai hold Gaobi; Yang Su attacked and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 諒大懼，拒素於蒿澤。

translations.literal: Liang was greatly afraid and blocked Yang Su at Haomarsh.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was greatly afraid and blocked Yang Su at Haomarsh.

sentences.zh: 屬天大雨，諒欲旋師，王頍諫曰：「楊素懸軍，士馬疲弊，王以銳卒親戎擊之，其勢必舉。

translations.literal: Heavy rain fell; Liang wished to withdraw. Wang Pi remonstrated: "Yang Su's army is isolated—men and horses exhausted—if Your Highness personally leads elite troops to strike, victory is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain fell; Liang wished to withdraw. Wang Pi remonstrated: "Yang Su's army is isolated—men and horses exhausted—if Your Highness personally leads elite troops to strike, victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 今見敵而還，示人以怯，阻戰士之心，益西軍之氣，願必勿還。

translations.literal: To turn back upon sight of the enemy shows timidity to others, dampens the fighters' will, and boosts the western army's morale—I urge you not to return.
translations.idiomatic: To turn back upon sight of the enemy shows timidity to others, dampens the fighters' will, and boosts the western army's morale—I urge you not to return.

sentences.zh: 」諒不從，退守清源。

translations.literal: " Liang did not heed him and withdrew to defend Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang did not heed him and withdrew to defend Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 素進擊之，諒與官兵大戰，死者萬八千人。

translations.literal: Su pressed the attack; Liang fought a great battle with government troops—eighteen thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Su pressed the attack; Liang fought a great battle with government troops—eighteen thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 諒退保并州，楊素進擊之，諒乃降。

translations.literal: Liang retreated to hold Bingzhou; Yang Su pressed the attack and Liang surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Liang retreated to hold Bingzhou; Yang Su pressed the attack and Liang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 百僚奏諒罪當死，帝曰：「朕終鮮兄弟，情不忍言，欲屈法恕諒一死。

translations.literal: The hundred officials memorialized that Liang's crime merited death. The Emperor said: "I have few brothers to the end—my feelings will not permit me to speak of it; I wish to bend the law and spare Liang's life.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials memorialized that Liang's crime merited death. The Emperor said: "I have few brothers left—my feelings will not permit me to speak of it; I wish to bend the law and spare Liang's life.

sentences.zh: 」於是除名，絕其屬籍，竟以幽死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon his name was erased, his clan register severed, and in the end he died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon his name was erased, his clan register was severed, and in the end he died in confinement.

sentences.zh: 先是，并州謠言：「一張紙，兩張紙，客量小兒作天子。

translations.literal: Earlier, a ballad in Bingzhou ran: "One sheet of paper, two sheets of paper—the youngest son Ke will be Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a ballad in Bingzhou ran: "One sheet of paper, two sheets of paper—the youngest son Ke will be Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」時偽署官告身皆一紙，別授則二紙。

translations.literal: " At that time the falsely appointed official patent letters were all one sheet; separate appointments used two sheets.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the falsely appointed official patent letters were all one sheet; separate appointments used two sheets.

sentences.zh: 諒聞謠喜曰：「我幼字阿客，'量'與'諒'同音，吾於皇家最小。

translations.literal: Liang heard the ballad and rejoiced, saying: "My childhood name is A Ke—'liang' (measure) and 'liang' (my name) are homophones; I am the youngest in the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Liang heard the ballad and rejoiced, saying, "My childhood name is A Ke—the word for 'measure' and the word for my name sound alike; I am the youngest in the imperial house."

sentences.zh: 」以為應之。

translations.literal: " He believed it matched him.
translations.idiomatic: He believed it matched him.

sentences.zh: 子顥，因而禁錮。

translations.literal: His son Hao was accordingly imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hao was accordingly imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弑逆之際，遇害。

translations.literal: At Yuwen Huaji's regicide he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuwen Huaji's regicide he was killed.

sentences.zh: 煬帝三男：蕭皇后生元德太子昭、齊王暕。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang had three sons: Empress Xiao bore Crown Prince Yuande Zhao and Prince of Qi Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang had three sons: Empress Xiao bore Crown Prince Yuande Zhao and Prince of Qi Xiu.

sentences.zh: 蕭嬪生趙王杲。

translations.literal: Concubine Xiao bore Prince of Zhao Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Concubine Xiao bore Prince of Zhao Guo.

sentences.zh: 元德太子昭，煬帝長子也。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yuande Zhao was Emperor Yang's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yuande Zhao was Emperor Yang's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝以開皇三年四月庚午，夢神自天而降，雲是天神將生降。

translations.literal: Initially, on the gengwu day of the fourth month of the third year of Kaihuang, Emperor Wen dreamed a god descended from heaven, saying a heavenly spirit was about to be born.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, on the gengwu day of the fourth month of the third year of Kaihuang, Emperor Wen dreamed a god descended from heaven, saying a heavenly spirit was about to be born.

sentences.zh: 寤，召納言蘇威以告之。

translations.literal: Upon waking he summoned Chief Censor Su Wei and told him.
translations.idiomatic: Upon waking he summoned Chief Censor Su Wei and told him.

sentences.zh: 及聞蕭妃在并州有娠，迎置大興宮之客省。

translations.literal: When he heard Consort Xiao was pregnant at Bingzhou, he had her brought to the Guest Quarters of Daxing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Consort Xiao was pregnant at Bingzhou, he had her brought to the Guest Quarters of Daxing Palace.

sentences.zh: 明年正月戊辰而生昭，養于宮中，號大曹主。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, on the wuchen day, Zhao was born; he was raised in the palace and styled Lord Dacao.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, on the wuchen day, Zhao was born; he was raised in the palace and styled Lord Dacao.

sentences.zh: 三歲時，於玄武門弄石師子，文帝與文獻皇后至其所。

translations.literal: At age three, playing with a stone lion at Xuanyuan Gate, Emperor Wen and Empress Wenxian came to his place.
translations.idiomatic: At age three, while playing with a stone lion at Xuanyuan Gate, Emperor Wen and Empress Wenxian came to where he was.

sentences.zh: 文帝適患腰痛，舉手馮後，昭因避去，如此者再三。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen happened to suffer back pain and leaned on the empress for support; Zhao thereupon withdrew—this happened three times.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen happened to suffer back pain and leaned on the empress for support; Zhao thereupon withdrew—this happened three times.

sentences.zh: 文帝歎曰：「天生長者，誰復教乎！

translations.literal: Emperor Wen sighed: "Born with propriety—who could teach that!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sighed: "Born with propriety—who could teach that!"

sentences.zh: 」由是大奇之。

translations.literal: " From this he marveled at him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: From this he marveled at him greatly.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘗謂曰：「當為爾娶婦。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once said to him: "I shall take a wife for you."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once told him, "I shall find you a wife."

sentences.zh: 」應聲而泣。

translations.literal: At the words he immediately wept.
translations.idiomatic: At once he burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 文帝問其故，對曰：「漢王未婚時，恆在至尊所，一朝娶婦，便則出外。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen asked the reason. He replied: "When the Prince of Han was still unmarried, he always stayed at His Majesty's side; once he took a wife, he was sent away at once."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen asked why. He answered, "When the Prince of Han was still unmarried, he always remained at His Majesty's side; the moment he married, he was sent away."

sentences.zh: 懼將違離，是以啼耳。

translations.literal: I fear I shall be parted from you — that is why I weep.
translations.idiomatic: "I fear I shall be separated from you — that is why I weep."

sentences.zh: 」上歎其有至性，特鍾愛焉。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed at his utmost sincerity and favored him with special affection.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed at his exceptional filial devotion and came to cherish him with special affection.

sentences.zh: 年十二，立為河南王。

translations.literal: At age twelve he was established as Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of twelve he was enfeoffed as Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，徙為晉王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he was transferred to be Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Renshou era he was transferred and made Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 拜內史令，兼左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Commander-in-Chief of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Commander-in-Chief of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 轉雍州牧。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，便幸洛陽宮，昭留守京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he at once visited Luoyang Palace; Zhao remained to hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, he went at once to Luoyang Palace while Zhao remained behind to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 及大業元年，帝遣使者立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daye the emperor sent emissaries to establish him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daye the emperor sent envoys to install him as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 昭妃慈州刺史博陵崔弘升女。

translations.literal: Zhao's consort was the daughter of Cui Hongsheng of Boling, Governor of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's consort was the daughter of Cui Hongsheng of Boling, Governor of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 後秦王妃以蠱毒獲譴，昭奏曰：「惡逆者，乃新婦之姑，請離之。

translations.literal: Later the Princess of Qin was punished for witchcraft. Zhao memorialized: "The wicked rebel is my new wife's mother-in-law — I ask to divorce her."
translations.idiomatic: Later the Princess of Qin was punished for sorcery. Zhao submitted a memorial: "The guilty party is my new wife's mother-in-law — I ask permission to divorce her."

sentences.zh: 」乃娶滑國公京兆韋壽女為妃。

translations.literal: He then took as consort the daughter of Wei Shou of Jingzhao, Duke of Huaguo.
translations.idiomatic: He then married the daughter of Wei Shou of Jingzhao, Duke of Huaguo, as his consort.

sentences.zh: 昭有子三人：韋妃生恭皇帝，大劉良娣生燕王倓，小劉良娣生越王侗。

translations.literal: Zhao had three sons: Consort Wei bore Emperor Gong; the elder Lady Liu bore Prince of Yan Tan; the younger Lady Liu bore Prince of Yue Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had three sons: Consort Wei bore Emperor Gong; the elder Lady Liu bore Prince of Yan Tan; the younger Lady Liu bore Prince of Yue Tong.

sentences.zh: 倓字仁安，敏慧美咨容，煬帝于諸孫中特所鍾愛，常置左右。

translations.literal: Tan, styled Ren'an, was quick-witted and handsome in appearance; among all his grandsons Emperor Yang favored him especially and kept him always at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Tan, styled Ren'an, was quick-witted and handsome; of all his grandsons Emperor Yang favored him above the rest and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 性好讀書，尤重儒素，造次所及，有若成人。

translations.literal: By nature he loved reading and placed special value on Confucian plainness; even in casual moments his conduct was like that of a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading by nature and held Confucian simplicity in special esteem; even in unguarded moments his bearing was that of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 良娣早終，每忌日未嘗不流涕嗚咽，帝由是益奇之。

translations.literal: His lady companion died early; on each anniversary of her death he never failed to weep aloud, and the emperor marveled at him all the more for it.
translations.idiomatic: His lady companion died young; on each anniversary of her death he never failed to weep aloud, and the emperor came to admire him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弑逆之際，倓覺變，欲入奏，恐露其事，因與梁公蕭钜、千牛宇文晶等穿芳林門側水竇入。

translations.literal: At the moment of Yuwen Huaji's regicide Tan sensed the coup and wished to enter to report it; fearing the matter would be exposed, he and Duke of Liang Xiao Ju, Cabinet Guard Yuwen Jing, and others entered through a drainage culvert beside Fanglin Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji carried out his regicide, Tan sensed that something was wrong and wished to go in and report it; fearing discovery, he entered with Duke of Liang Xiao Ju, Cabinet Guard Yuwen Jing, and others through a drainage culvert beside Fanglin Gate.

sentences.zh: 至玄武門，詭奏曰：「臣卒中惡，命懸俄頃，請得面辭，死無所恨。

translations.literal: Reaching Xuanyuan Gate, he feigned a memorial: "Your subject has suddenly fallen gravely ill; my life hangs by a moment — I beg leave to take farewell in person, and I shall die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Xuanyuan Gate he submitted a false report: "Your subject has suddenly fallen gravely ill; my life hangs by a thread — I beg leave to take my farewell in person, and I shall die without regret."

sentences.zh: 」冀見帝，為司宮者所遏，竟不得聞。

translations.literal: He hoped to see the emperor, but was blocked by the palace attendants and never got through.
translations.idiomatic: He hoped to see the emperor, but was stopped by the palace attendants and never got his message through.

sentences.zh: 俄而難作，遇害，時年十六。

translations.literal: Soon the disaster erupted; he was killed. He was sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the catastrophe broke out and he was killed. He was sixteen years old.

sentences.zh: 越王侗，字仁謹，美姿容，性寬厚。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Tong, styled Renjin, had handsome features and a generous nature.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Tong, styled Renjin, was handsome in appearance and generous by nature.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，立為越王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye he was established as Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 帝每巡幸，侗常留守東都。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on tour, Tong usually remained to hold the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor traveled on tour, Tong usually remained behind to hold the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感反，與戶部尚書樊子蓋拒之。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, he joined Minister of Revenue Fan Zigai in resisting him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rose in rebellion, he joined Minister of Revenue Fan Zigai in resisting him.

sentences.zh: 事平，朝于高陽，拜高陽太守。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he attended court at Gaoyang and was appointed Administrator of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the affair was settled he attended court at Gaoyang and was appointed Administrator of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官留守東都。

translations.literal: Soon, in his existing capacity, he was again left to hold the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again left to hold the Eastern Capital in his existing capacity.

sentences.zh: 十三年，帝幸江都，復令侗與金紫光祿大夫段達、太府卿元文都、攝戶部尚書韋津、右武衛將軍皇甫無逸等總留台事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the emperor went to Jiangdu and again ordered Tong, together with Chamberlain for Attendant Affairs Duan Da, Grand Steward Yuan Wendu, Acting Minister of Revenue Wei Jin, and General of the Right Wuyi Guards Huangfu Wuyi, to oversee overall affairs of the capital in his absence.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the emperor went to Jiangdu and again ordered Tong, together with Chamberlain for Attendant Affairs Duan Da, Grand Steward Yuan Wendu, Acting Minister of Revenue Wei Jin, and General of the Right Wuyi Guards Huangfu Wuyi, to oversee all affairs of the capital in his absence.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之弑逆，文都等議尊立侗，大赦，改元曰皇泰。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, Wendu and the others deliberated raising Tong to the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Huangtai.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Wendu and the others deliberated raising Tong to the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Huangtai.

sentences.zh: 諡帝曰明，廟號世祖，追尊元德太子為孝成皇帝，廟號世宗，尊其母劉良娣為皇太后。

translations.literal: They posthumously titled the former emperor Ming with temple name Shizu; elevated Crown Prince Yuande to Emperor Xiaocheng with temple name Shizong; and honored his mother Lady Liu as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: They gave the former emperor the posthumous title Ming and temple name Shizu; elevated Crown Prince Yuande to Emperor Xiaocheng with temple name Shizong; and honored his mother Lady Liu as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 以段達為納言、右翊衛大將軍、攝禮部尚書，王世充為納言、左翊衛大將軍、攝吏部尚書，元文都為內史令、左驍衛大將軍，盧楚亦內史令，皇甫無逸為兵部尚書、右武衛大將軍，郭文懿為內史侍郎，趙長文為黃門侍郎，委以機務，為金書鐵券，藏之宮掖。

translations.literal: Duan Da was made Chief Censor, Commander-in-Chief of the Right Yiyi Guard, and Acting Minister of Rites; Wang Shichong Chief Censor, Commander-in-Chief of the Left Yiyi Guard, and Acting Minister of Personnel; Yuan Wendu Director of the Secretariat and Commander-in-Chief of the Left Xiao Guard; Lu Chu also Director of the Secretariat; Huangfu Wuyi Minister of War and Commander-in-Chief of the Right Wuyi Guard; Guo Wenyi Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Zhao Changwen Vice Director of the Yellow Gate — state affairs were entrusted to them, golden-letter iron bonds were made, and stored in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da was made Chief Censor, Commander-in-Chief of the Right Yiyi Guard, and Acting Minister of Rites; Wang Shichong Chief Censor, Commander-in-Chief of the Left Yiyi Guard, and Acting Minister of Personnel; Yuan Wendu Director of the Secretariat and Commander-in-Chief of the Left Xiao Guard; Lu Chu also Director of the Secretariat; Huangfu Wuyi Minister of War and Commander-in-Chief of the Right Wuyi Guard; Guo Wenyi Vice Director of the Secretariat; and Zhao Changwen Vice Director of the Yellow Gate. State affairs were entrusted to them, golden-letter iron bonds were issued, and stored within the palace.

sentences.zh: 于時洛陽稱段達等為「七貴」。

translations.literal: At the time Luoyang called Duan Da and the others the "Seven Nobles."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Luoyang referred to Duan Da and his colleagues as the "Seven Nobles."

sentences.zh: 未幾，宇文化及以秦王浩為天子，來次彭城，所經城邑，多從逆黨。

translations.literal: Before long Yuwen Huaji installed Prince of Qin Hao as emperor and came to halt at Pengcheng; of the cities and towns he passed through, many joined the rebel faction.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuwen Huaji set up Prince of Qin Hao as emperor and encamped at Pengcheng; many of the cities and towns along his route joined the rebel cause.

sentences.zh: 侗懼，遣使者蓋琮、馬公政招懷李密。

translations.literal: Tong was afraid and sent emissaries Gai Cong and Ma Gongzheng to win over Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Tong sent envoys Gai Cong and Ma Gongzheng to win Li Mi over.

sentences.zh: 密遂請降，侗大忻悅，禮其使甚厚。

translations.literal: Li Mi thereupon asked to surrender; Tong was greatly delighted and treated his emissaries with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi then offered to submit; Tong was overjoyed and treated his envoys with great honor.

sentences.zh: 即拜密為太尉、尚書令、魏國公，令拒化及。

translations.literal: He at once appointed Li Mi Grand Marshal, Director of the Secretariat, and Duke of Wei, and ordered him to resist Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately appointed Li Mi Grand Marshal, Director of the Secretariat, and Duke of Wei, and ordered him to resist Huaji.

sentences.zh: 仍下書曰：

translations.literal: He also issued an edict saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also issued an edict that read:

sentences.zh: 我大隋之有天下，於茲三十八載。

translations.literal: Our Great Sui has held the realm for thirty-eight years to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Our Great Sui has held the realm for thirty-eight years to this day.

sentences.zh: 高祖文皇帝聖略神功。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor Gaozu, Emperor Wen, possessed sage strategy and divine merit.
translations.idiomatic: Founding Emperor Gaozu, Emperor Wen, possessed sage strategy and divine merit.

sentences.zh: 載造區夏。

translations.literal: He established order throughout the Central Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: He brought order to the Central Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 世祖明皇帝則天法地，混一華戎。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor Ming measured heaven and patterned earth, unifying Chinese and barbarian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, temple name Shizu, took heaven as his model and earth as his law, uniting Chinese and barbarian alike.

sentences.zh: 東暨蟠木，西通細柳，前逾丹徼，後越幽都，日月之所臨，風雨之所至，圓首方足，稟氣食毛，莫不盡入提封，皆為臣妾。

translations.literal: East to Panmu, west to Xiliu, south beyond the red frontier, north past Youdu — wherever sun and moon shine and wind and rain reach, all who bear round heads and square feet, who draw breath and eat flesh, none failed to enter the imperial domain; all became subjects.
translations.idiomatic: East to Panmu, west to Xiliu, south beyond the red frontier, north past Youdu — wherever sun and moon shine and wind and rain reach, every living soul with round head and square feet, every creature that draws breath and eats flesh, all entered the imperial domain and became our subjects.

sentences.zh: 加以寶貺畢集，雲瑞咸臻，作樂制禮，移風易俗。

translations.literal: Moreover precious tributes gathered in full; auspicious clouds and omens all arrived; music was composed and ritual instituted; customs were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover precious tribute poured in from every quarter; auspicious clouds and omens appeared in abundance; music was composed, ritual was instituted, and customs were transformed.

sentences.zh: 智周寰海，萬物咸受其賜；

translations.literal: His wisdom encompassed the seas; all things alike received his bounty;
translations.idiomatic: His wisdom encompassed the four seas; all things alike received his bounty;

sentences.zh: 道濟天下，百姓用而不知。

translations.literal: His Way succored the realm; the common people benefited without knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: His Way succored the realm; the common people benefited without even knowing it.

sentences.zh: 世祖往因曆試，統臨南服，自居皇極，順茲望幸。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor, having previously undergone trials of rule and governed the southern domains, once he took the imperial seat, accorded with their wish for his presence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu, having previously been tested in provincial rule and having governed the southern domains, once he took the throne, wished to respond to their longing for his presence.

sentences.zh: 所以往歲省方，展禮肆觀，停鑾駐蹕，按駕清道，八屯如昔，七萃不移。

translations.literal: Hence in years past he toured the regions, displaying rites and receiving tribute; the imperial carriage halted and the retinue encamped; escorts cleared the road; the eight garrisons stood as before; the seven elite corps were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Hence in years past he toured the regions, displaying rites and receiving tribute; the imperial carriage halted and the retinue encamped; escorts cleared the roads; the eight garrisons stood as before and the seven elite corps remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 豈意釁起非常，逮於軒陛，災生不意，廷及冕旒。

translations.literal: Who could have thought rebellion would arise so abnormally, reaching the imperial hall; disaster would spring unlooked-for, extending to the imperial crown?
translations.idiomatic: Who could have imagined that rebellion would erupt so abnormally as to reach the imperial hall, or that disaster would strike without warning and touch the imperial crown itself?

sentences.zh: 奉諱之日，五情崩殞，攀號荼毒，不能自勝。

translations.literal: On the day we received the mournful news, the five emotions collapsed; we clung and wailed in agony beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day we received the mournful tidings, our hearts collapsed within us; we clung and wailed in unbearable grief.

sentences.zh: 且聞之自古，代有屯剝，賊臣逆子，何世無之。

translations.literal: Moreover we have heard that since antiquity every age has known adversity and decline; treacherous ministers and rebellious sons — what age has lacked them?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover we have heard that since antiquity every age has known hardship and decline; treacherous ministers and rebellious sons — what age has ever lacked them?

sentences.zh: 至如宇文化及，世傳庸品。

translations.literal: As for Yuwen Huaji, for generations his family has been known as common stock.
translations.idiomatic: As for Yuwen Huaji, his family has for generations been known as undistinguished stock.

sentences.zh: 其父述，往屬時來，早沾厚遇，賜以昏媾，置之公輔。

translations.literal: His father Shu, timely favored in the past, early received generous treatment — granted marriage ties and placed among chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shu, favored by fortune in earlier days, received generous treatment early on — granted marriage ties with the throne and placed among the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 位尊九命，祿重萬鐘，禮極人臣，榮冠世表，徒承海嶽之恩，未有涓塵之答。

translations.literal: His rank honored with the nine orders; his stipend weighed in myriad measures; ritual reached the utmost for a subject; glory topped all peers — yet he received favors vast as seas and mountains and repaid not a mote of dust.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was honored with the nine orders; his stipend was weighed in myriad measures; ritual for him reached the utmost permitted a subject; his glory topped all his peers — yet he received favors vast as seas and mountains and repaid not so much as a mote of dust.

sentences.zh: 化及以此下材，夙蒙顧眄，出入外內，奉望階墀。

translations.literal: Huaji, though of such base talent, long enjoyed the imperial gaze; he went in and out of the inner and outer courts, attending at the palace steps.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji, though of such base talent, long enjoyed the imperial favor; he passed in and out of the inner and outer courts and attended at the palace steps.

sentences.zh: 昔陪籓國，統領衛兵，及從升皇祚，陪列九卿。

translations.literal: Formerly he accompanied the prince in the domain and commanded the guard troops; when the sovereign ascended the throne he stood among the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly he accompanied the prince in his domain and commanded the guard troops; when the sovereign ascended the throne he took his place among the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 但本性凶狠，恣其貪穢，或交結惡黨，或侵掠商貨，事重刑簽，狀盈獄簡。

translations.literal: But his nature was fierce and cruel; he indulged greed and corruption — now consorting with evil factions, now plundering merchants' goods; charges merited heavy punishment and files overflowed the prison records.
translations.idiomatic: But his nature was fierce and cruel; he indulged greed and corruption — now consorting with evil factions, now plundering merchants' goods — until the charges merited heavy punishment and the prison records overflowed with his case files.

sentences.zh: 在上不遺簪履，恩加草芥，應至死辜，每蒙恕免。

translations.literal: The sovereign did not cast aside even humble retainers; grace extended to the meanest weed — crimes deserving death were repeatedly pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign did not cast aside even the humblest retainer; grace extended even to the meanest weed — crimes deserving death were repeatedly pardoned.

sentences.zh: 三經除解，尋復本職；

translations.literal: Three times he was dismissed from office, only to be restored to his former post shortly after;
translations.idiomatic: Three times he was dismissed from office, only to be restored to his former post shortly afterward;

sentences.zh: 再徙邊裔，仍即追還。

translations.literal: Twice he was banished to the frontier, yet immediately recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he was banished to the frontier, yet immediately recalled.

sentences.zh: 生成之恩，昊天罔極；

translations.literal: The grace of nurturing him was boundless as heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The grace of raising him was boundless as heaven itself;

sentences.zh: 獎擢之義，人事罕聞。

translations.literal: Such promotion and favor is rarely heard of among men.
translations.idiomatic: such promotion and favor is rarely heard of among men.

sentences.zh: 化及梟獍為心，禽獸不若，從毒興禍，傾覆行宮。

translations.literal: Huaji had the heart of an owl and a beast; not even animals would compare — he brewed poison to raise calamity and overthrew the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji had the heart of an owl and a beast — worse than any animal — brewing poison to raise calamity and overthrowing the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 諸王兄弟，一時殘酷，痛暴行路，世不忍言。

translations.literal: The princes and brothers were slaughtered together in one cruel moment; the horror on the roads — the age cannot bear to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and imperial brothers were slaughtered together in one cruel stroke; the horror on the roads is something the age cannot bear to speak of.

sentences.zh: 有窮之在夏時，犬戎之于周世，釁辱之極，亦未是過。

translations.literal: The outrage of Youqiong in the Xia and the Dog Rong in the Zhou — the extremity of insult hardly surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: The outrage of Youqiong in the Xia and the Dog Rong in the Zhou — the extremity of insult scarcely surpasses this.

sentences.zh: 朕所以刻骨崩心，飲膽嘗血，瞻天視地，無處自容。

translations.literal: Therefore we gnaw bone and shatter heart, drink gall and taste blood, look to heaven and earth, and find nowhere to hide our shame.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we gnaw our bones and shatter our hearts, drink gall and taste blood, look to heaven and earth, and find nowhere to hide our shame.

sentences.zh: 今王公卿士，庶尹百辟，咸以大寶鴻名，不可顛墜，元凶巨猾，須早夷殄，翼戴朕躬，嗣守寶位。

translations.literal: Now kings, dukes, ministers, and scholars, all officials and hundred lords, agree that the great mandate and glorious name must not fall; the arch criminal and great villain must be swiftly destroyed; they support us to succeed and guard the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Now kings, dukes, ministers, and scholars, all officials and lords of every rank, agree that the great mandate and glorious name must not fall; the arch criminal and great villain must be swiftly destroyed; they support us to succeed and guard the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 顧惟寡薄，志不逮此。

translations.literal: Reflecting on our own inadequacy, our will does not reach this far.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on our own inadequacy, our will does not reach so far.

sentences.zh: 今者出黼扆而仗旄鉞，釋衰麻而擐甲胄，銜冤誓眾，忍淚臨兵，指日遄征，以平大盜。

translations.literal: Now we leave the imperial screen to take up battle-axes, cast off mourning garb to don armor, bear grievance and vow to the host, hold back tears as we lead the army, and within days march swiftly to pacify the great rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Now we leave the imperial screen to take up battle-axes, cast off mourning garb to don armor, bear our grievance and vow ourselves to the host, hold back tears as we lead the army, and within days march swiftly to pacify the great rebel.

sentences.zh: 且化及偽立秦王之子，幽遏比於拘囚；

translations.literal: Moreover Huaji has falsely enthroned the Prince of Qin's son, confining him like a prisoner;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Huaji has falsely enthroned the Prince of Qin's son and confines him like a prisoner;

sentences.zh: 其身自稱霸相，專擅擬於九五。

translations.literal: He himself styles himself overlord and chancellor, arrogating to himself the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: He himself styles himself overlord and chancellor, arrogating to himself the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 履踐禁禦，據有宮關，昂首揚眉，初無慚色。

translations.literal: He treads the forbidden precincts and occupies the palace gates, holding his head high without a blush.
translations.idiomatic: He treads the forbidden precincts and occupies the palace gates, holding his head high without the slightest shame.

sentences.zh: 衣冠朝望，外懼凶威，志士誠臣，內懷憤怨。

translations.literal: Court officials and eminent men outwardly fear his brutal power; loyal hearts and true ministers inwardly burn with outrage.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials and eminent men outwardly fear his brutal power, while loyal hearts and true ministers inwardly burn with outrage.

sentences.zh: 以我義師，順彼天道，梟夷醜族，匪夕伊朝。

translations.literal: With our righteous army, following heaven's Way, we shall cut down and exterminate the foul clan — not overnight, but within the morning.
translations.idiomatic: With our righteous army, following heaven's Way, we shall cut down and exterminate the foul clan — not overnight, but within the morning.

sentences.zh: 太尉、尚書令魏公，丹誠內發，宏略外舉，率勤王之師，討違天之逆。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat, Duke of Wei — loyalty blazing within, grand strategy displayed without — leads the army that hastens to the sovereign's aid to punish rebellion against heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat, Duke of Wei — loyalty blazing within, grand strategy displayed without — leads the army that hastens to the sovereign's aid to punish rebellion against heaven.

sentences.zh: 果毅爭先，熊羆競進，金鼓振讋，若火焚毛，鋒刃從橫，如湯沃雪。

translations.literal: The resolute vie to lead; warriors compete like bears and panthers; drums and bells shake the timid like fire burning hair; blades cross as boiling water melts snow.
translations.idiomatic: The resolute vie to lead the charge; warriors compete like bears and panthers; drums and bells shake the timid like fire burning hair; blades cross as boiling water melts snow.

sentences.zh: 魏公志存匡濟，投袂前驅，朕親禦六軍，星言繼軌。

translations.literal: The Duke of Wei, his purpose set on restoring order, flings his sleeves and advances; we personally command the six armies and march at starlight to follow his track.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Wei, his purpose set on restoring order, flings his sleeves and advances at the fore; we personally command the six armies and march at starlight to follow in his track.

sentences.zh: 以此眾戰，以斯順舉，擘山可以動，射石可以入。

translations.literal: With such troops fighting, with such righteous cause — moving mountains is possible, piercing stone is achievable.
translations.idiomatic: With such troops fighting and such righteous cause, moving mountains is possible and piercing stone achievable.

sentences.zh: 況賊擁此人徒，皆有離德，京都侍衛，西憶鄉家，江左淳人，南思邦邑。

translations.literal: How much more when the rebels hold followers who all lack unity — capital guards longing west for home, simple folk of the Jiang region yearning south for their lands.
translations.idiomatic: How much more so when the rebels hold followers who all lack unity — capital guards longing westward for home, simple folk of the Jiang region yearning southward for their native lands.

sentences.zh: 比來表書駱驛，人信相尋。

translations.literal: Recently memorials and letters have arrived in continuous stream; messengers follow one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Recently memorials and letters have arrived in an unbroken stream, and messengers follow one upon another.

sentences.zh: 若王師一臨，舊章暫睹，自應解甲倒戈，冰銷棄散。

translations.literal: If the royal army appears once, and they glimpse the old order briefly, they should of themselves lay down arms and turn their blades — melting like ice, scattering like frost.
translations.idiomatic: If the royal army appears even once and they glimpse the old order again, they should of themselves lay down arms and turn their blades — melting like ice, scattering like frost.

sentences.zh: 且聞化及自恣，天奪其心，殺戮不辜，挫辱人士，莫不道路以目，號天跼地。

translations.literal: Moreover we hear Huaji indulges himself; heaven has withdrawn his mind — he slaughters the innocent and humiliates the gentry; none but walks the roads with eyes downcast, crying to heaven and stamping the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover we hear that Huaji indulges himself unrestrainedly; heaven has withdrawn his reason — he slaughters the innocent and humiliates the gentry; none but walks the roads with downcast eyes, crying to heaven and stamping the earth.

sentences.zh: 朕今復仇雪恥，梟轅者一人，拯溺救焚，所哀者士庶。

translations.literal: We now seek vengeance and wipe shame clean — the one we mean to execute at the gate is a single man; what we mean to rescue from drowning and fire is officials and common folk.
translations.idiomatic: We now seek vengeance and wipe away shame — the one we mean to execute at the gate is a single man; what we mean to rescue from drowning and fire are officials and common folk.

sentences.zh: 唯望天鑒孔殷，祐我宗社，億兆感義，俱會朕心。

translations.literal: We only hope heaven's mirror is vast and bright, protects our state and altars, and that the millions, moved by righteousness, unite with our heart.
translations.idiomatic: We only hope that heaven's mirror is vast and bright, that it protects our state and altars, and that the millions, moved by righteousness, unite with our heart.

sentences.zh: 梟戮元凶，策勳飲至，四海交泰，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: Slay the arch criminal, record merit and hold victory feast — the four seas at peace — that is our wish.
translations.idiomatic: Slay the arch criminal, record merit and hold the victory feast — let the four seas know peace — that is our wish.

sentences.zh: 兵衛軍機，並受魏公節度。

translations.literal: Military guard and statecraft all fall under the Duke of Wei's command.
translations.idiomatic: Military guard and state affairs alike fall under the Duke of Wei's command.

sentences.zh: 密見使者，大悅，北面拜伏，臣禮甚恭，遂東拒化及。

translations.literal: Li Mi received the emissaries with great joy, bowed prostrate facing north with utmost courtesy, and thereupon resisted Huaji from the east.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi received the envoys he was greatly pleased; he bowed prostrate facing north with the utmost courtesy and thereupon resisted Huaji from the east.

sentences.zh: 七貴頗不協。

translations.literal: The Seven Nobles were quite at odds with one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Seven Nobles were quite at odds with one another.

sentences.zh: 未幾，元文都、盧楚、郭文懿、趙長文等為世充所殺，皇甫無逸遁歸京師。

translations.literal: Before long Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, Guo Wenyi, Zhao Changwen, and others were killed by Wang Shichong; Huangfu Wuyi fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, Guo Wenyi, Zhao Changwen, and others were killed by Wang Shichong, while Huangfu Wuyi fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 世充詣侗所陳謝，辭情哀苦。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong came to Tong's residence to express regret, his words pitifully anguished.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong came to Tong's residence to express regret, his words pitifully anguished.

sentences.zh: 侗以為至誠，命之上殿，被髮為盟，誓無貳志。

translations.literal: Tong took it as sincere devotion, ordered him up to the hall, and with hair unbound they swore an oath of undivided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Tong took it as sincere devotion, summoned him to the hall, and with hair unbound they swore an oath of undivided loyalty.

sentences.zh: 自是侗無所關預。

translations.literal: From then on Tong had no part in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Tong had no part in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 及世充破李密，眾望益歸之，遂自為鄭王，總百揆，加九錫，備法物，侗不能禁。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong defeated Li Mi, popular hope turned to him all the more; he thereupon made himself King of Zheng, taking all authority, receiving the Nine Bestowals and full regalia — Tong could not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong defeated Li Mi, popular hope turned to him all the more; he thereupon made himself King of Zheng, seized all authority, received the Nine Bestowals and full regalia — and Tong could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 段達、雲定興等十人入見侗曰：「天命不常，鄭王功德甚盛，願陛下遵唐、虞之跡。

translations.literal: Duan Da, Yun Dingxing, and ten others entered to see Tong and said: "Heaven's mandate is not constant; the King of Zheng's merit is very great — we wish Your Majesty would follow the example of Tang and Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da, Yun Dingxing, and ten others came to see Tong and said, "Heaven's mandate is not constant; the King of Zheng's merit is very great — we wish Your Majesty would follow the example of Tang and Yu."

sentences.zh: 」侗怒曰：「天下者，高祖之天下，東都者，世祖之東都。

translations.literal: Tong angrily said: "The realm belongs to Gaozu; the Eastern Capital belongs to Shizu."
translations.idiomatic: Tong angrily replied, "The realm belongs to Gaozu; the Eastern Capital belongs to Shizu."

sentences.zh: 若隋德未衰，此言不可而發。

translations.literal: If Sui virtue has not declined, such words ought not be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: If Sui virtue has not yet declined, such words ought not even be spoken.

sentences.zh: 必天命有改，亦何論於禪讓！

translations.literal: Even if heaven's mandate must change, what talk is there of abdication!
translations.idiomatic: Even if heaven's mandate must change, what talk is there of abdication!

sentences.zh: 公等或先朝舊臣，或勤王立節，忽有斯言，朕亦何望！

translations.literal: You are either veterans of the former court or men who risked yourselves to raise the throne — to speak thus suddenly, what hope have I left!
translations.idiomatic: You are either veterans of the former court or men who risked yourselves to raise the throne — to speak thus suddenly, what hope have I left!

sentences.zh: 」神色凜然，侍衛者莫不流汗。

translations.literal: His bearing was stern and chilling; none of the attendants but broke into a sweat.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was stern and chilling; every attendant in the room broke into a sweat.

sentences.zh: 既而退朝，對良娣而泣。

translations.literal: Afterwards he withdrew from court and wept before his lady companion.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he withdrew from court and wept before his lady companion.

sentences.zh: 世充更使謂曰：「今海內未定，須得長君，待四方乂安，復子明辟。

translations.literal: Shichong again sent someone to say to him: "The realm is not yet settled within the four seas; we need a mature ruler. When all quarters are pacified, I shall restore the son to the enlightened throne.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong again sent an envoy to tell him, "The realm is not yet settled; we need a mature ruler. Once the four quarters are at peace, I shall restore you, the rightful heir, to the throne.

sentences.zh: 必若前盟，義不違負。

translations.literal: If it is truly as in our former covenant, in righteousness I shall not break faith.
translations.idiomatic: If our earlier pact holds, I will not break faith."

sentences.zh: 」侗不得已，遜位於世充，遂被幽於含涼殿。

translations.literal: Tong had no choice; he yielded the throne to Shichong and was thereupon confined in Hanliang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Tong had no choice. He abdicated in favor of Wang Shichong and was confined in Hanliang Hall.

sentences.zh: 世充僭偽號，封潞國公。

translations.literal: Shichong usurped a false imperial title and enfeoffed him as Duke of the State of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong seized a spurious imperial title and enfeoffed him as Duke of the State of Lu.

sentences.zh: 有宇文儒童、裴仁基等謀誅世充，復尊立侗。

translations.literal: Yuwen Rutong, Pei Renji, and others plotted to kill Shichong and restore Tong to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Rutong, Pei Renji, and others plotted to kill Wang Shichong and restore Tong to the throne.

sentences.zh: 事泄，並見害。

translations.literal: The plot leaked out, and all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, they were all executed.

sentences.zh: 世充兄世惲因勸世充害侗。

translations.literal: Shichong's elder brother Shiyun thereupon urged Shichong to kill Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong's elder brother Shiyun then urged him to kill Tong.

sentences.zh: 世充遣其侄行本齎鳩詣侗曰：「願皇帝飲此酒。

translations.literal: Shichong sent his nephew Xingben bearing poisoned wine to Tong, saying: "I wish that Your Majesty would drink this wine.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong sent his nephew Xingben with poisoned wine to Tong, saying, "I beg Your Majesty to drink this wine.

sentences.zh: 」侗知不免，請與母相見，不許。

translations.literal: Tong knew he could not escape; he asked to see his mother, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tong knew he could not escape. He asked to see his mother, but permission was refused.

sentences.zh: 遂布席焚香禮佛，祝曰：「從今以去，不生帝王尊貴家。

translations.literal: He thereupon spread a mat, burned incense, and bowed to the Buddha, praying: "From this day forward, may I never again be born into an imperial or noble house.
translations.idiomatic: He spread a mat, burned incense, and bowed before the Buddha, praying, "From this day forward, may I never again be born into an imperial or noble house.

sentences.zh: 」及仰藥，不能時絕，更以帛縊之。

translations.literal: When he drank the poison, death did not come quickly; they strangled him with silk as well.
translations.idiomatic: He drank the poison, but death did not come quickly, so they strangled him with silk as well.

sentences.zh: 世充偽諡曰恭皇帝。

translations.literal: Shichong gave him the posthumous title of Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong gave him the posthumous title Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 暕頗驕恣，昵近小人，所行多不法。

translations.literal: Jian was quite arrogant and willful, kept close company with petty men, and much of what he did was unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Jian was arrogant and willful, kept company with petty men, and much of what he did violated the law.

sentences.zh: 遣喬令則、劉虔安、裴該、皇甫諶、厙狄仲

translations.literal: He dispatched Qiao Lingze, Liu Qian'an, Pei Gai, Huangfu Chen, and Kudie Zhong
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Qiao Lingze, Liu Qian'an, Pei Gai, Huangfu Chen, and Kudie Zhong

sentences.zh: 錡、陳智偉等采求聲色狗馬。

translations.literal: Qi, Chen Zhiwei, and others to gather music, women, and horses for his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, Chen Zhiwei, and others to gather music, women, and horses for his pleasure.

sentences.zh: 令則等因此放縱，方人家有女者，輒矯暕命呼之，載入暕宅，因緣藏匿，恣行淫穢而後遣之。

translations.literal: Lingze and the rest therefore grew unrestrained: wherever a household had a daughter, they would forge Jian's orders to summon her, carry her into Jian's residence, hide her away on one pretext or another, indulge in debauchery, and only then send her off.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened, Lingze and the others grew unrestrained. Wherever a household had a daughter, they forged Jian's orders to summon her, brought her into his residence, concealed her on one pretext or another, abused her, and only then sent her away.

sentences.zh: 仲錡、智偉二人詣隴西，撾炙諸胡，責其名馬，得數匹以進於暕。

translations.literal: Zhong Qi and Zhiwei went to Longxi, beat and roasted various Hu tribesmen, and demanded their famous horses; they obtained several mounts and presented them to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Qi and Zhiwei went to Longxi, beat and tormented various Hu tribesmen, and demanded their famous horses. They obtained several mounts and presented them to Jian.

sentences.zh: 暕令還主，仲錡等詐言王賜，將歸家，暕不之知也。

translations.literal: Jian ordered that the horses be returned to their owners, but Zhong Qi and the others falsely claimed the prince had bestowed them and took them home — Jian did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Jian ordered the horses returned to their owners, but Zhong Qi and the others falsely claimed the prince had bestowed the horses and took them home. Jian knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 又樂平公主嘗奏帝，雲柳氏女美者，帝未有所答。

translations.literal: Moreover, Princess of Leping once reported to the Emperor that a daughter of the Liu clan was beautiful; the Emperor made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Leping once told the Emperor that a daughter of the Liu clan was beautiful, but the Emperor made no reply.

sentences.zh: 久之，主復以柳氏進暕，暕納之。

translations.literal: After a long while the princess again presented the Liu woman to Jian, and Jian took her in.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the princess again presented the Liu woman to Jian, and he took her in.

sentences.zh: 後帝問主柳氏女所在，主曰：「在齊王所。

translations.literal: Later the Emperor asked the princess where the Liu woman was, and the princess said: "She is at the Prince of Qi's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Emperor asked the princess where the Liu woman was. The princess replied, "She is at the Prince of Qi's residence.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 暕于東都營第，大門無故崩，應事栿中折，識者以為不祥。

translations.literal: While Jian was building a mansion in the Eastern Capital, the great gate collapsed for no apparent reason, and the ridge beams in the hall snapped in two; those who understood such things took it as an ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: While Jian was building a mansion in the Eastern Capital, the great gate collapsed without cause and the hall beams snapped in two. Those who read omens judged it inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 後從帝幸榆林，暕督後軍，步騎五萬，恆與帝相去數十里而舍。

translations.literal: Later, when he accompanied the Emperor on a visit to Yulin, Jian commanded the rear guard — fifty thousand infantry and cavalry — and always encamped several tens of li from the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, accompanying the Emperor to Yulin, Jian commanded the rear guard of fifty thousand infantry and cavalry and always encamped several tens of li from the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 會帝于汾陽宮大獵，詔暕以千騎入圍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor held a great hunt at Fenyang Palace, he ordered Jian to enter the hunting enclosure with a thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor held a great hunt at Fenyang Palace, he ordered Jian to enter the enclosure with a thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 暕大獲麋鹿以獻，而帝未有得也，怒從官，皆言為暕左右所遏，獸不得前。

translations.literal: Jian took many elk and deer and presented them, while the Emperor had taken none; enraged, he blamed his attendants, who all said Jian's followers had blocked the game and kept the beasts from coming forward.
translations.idiomatic: Jian took a great haul of elk and deer and presented them, while the Emperor had taken none. Enraged, he blamed his attendants, who all said Jian's followers had blocked the game and kept the beasts from advancing.

sentences.zh: 帝於是怒，求暕罪失。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon grew angry and sought out Jian's faults.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon grew angry and began searching out Jian's faults.

sentences.zh: 時制縣令無故不得出境，有伊闕令皇甫詡幸於暕，違禁將之汾陽宮；

translations.literal: At that time the rule was that magistrates might not leave their counties without cause; the magistrate of Yique, Huangfu Xu, who enjoyed Jian's favor, violated the prohibition and brought him to Fenyang Palace;
translations.idiomatic: At that time magistrates were forbidden to leave their counties without cause. Huangfu Xu, magistrate of Yique and a favorite of Jian's, violated the ban and brought him to Fenyang Palace;

sentences.zh: 又京兆人達奚通有妾王氏善歌，貴遊宴聚，多或要致，於是輾轉亦入王家。

translations.literal: moreover, a man of Jingzhao named Daxi Tong had a concubine, Lady Wang, skilled in song; at the banquets of the great and wealthy she was often summoned, and by stages she passed into the Wang household as well.
translations.idiomatic: moreover, a man of Jingzhao named Daxi Tong had a concubine, Lady Wang, skilled in song. At the banquets of the great and wealthy she was often summoned, and in time she passed into the Wang household as well.

sentences.zh: 御史韋德裕希旨劾暕。

translations.literal: Censor Wei Deyu, seeking to please the Emperor, impeached Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wei Deyu, seeking to please the Emperor, impeached Jian.

sentences.zh: 帝令甲士千餘，大索暕第，因窮其事。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent more than a thousand armored soldiers to search Jian's residence thoroughly and pursue the matter to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent more than a thousand armored soldiers to search Jian's residence thoroughly and pursue the matter to the end.

sentences.zh: 暕妃韋氏，戶部尚書沖之女也，早卒。

translations.literal: Jian's consort was Lady Wei, daughter of Minister of Revenue Chong; she died early.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's consort was Lady Wei, daughter of Minister of Revenue Chong; she had died early.

sentences.zh: 暕遂與妃姊元氏婦通，生一女。

translations.literal: Jian then had relations with his consort's elder sister, the wife of the Yuan clan, and she bore a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Jian then had relations with his consort's elder sister, a woman of the Yuan clan, and she bore a daughter.

sentences.zh: 外人皆不得知，陰引喬令則於第內酣宴，令則稱慶，脫暕帽以為歡。

translations.literal: Outsiders knew nothing of it. He secretly brought Qiao Lingze into his residence for a drunken feast; Lingze offered congratulations, removed Jian's cap, and made merry.
translations.idiomatic: Outsiders knew nothing of it. He secretly brought Qiao Lingze into his residence for a drunken feast. Lingze offered congratulations, removed Jian's cap, and made merry.

sentences.zh: 召相工遍視後庭，相工指妃姊曰：「此產子者當為皇后，貴不可言。

translations.literal: He summoned a physiognomist to inspect the entire rear court; the physiognomist pointed to the consort's elder sister and said: "She who bears a child shall become empress — her nobility cannot be expressed in words.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned a physiognomist to inspect the entire rear court. The physiognomist pointed to the consort's elder sister and said, "The woman who bears this child shall become empress. Her nobility cannot be expressed in words.

sentences.zh: 」時國無儲副，暕自謂次當得立。

translations.literal: At that time the state had no heir apparent, and Jian considered himself next in line for enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the state had no heir apparent, and Jian considered himself next in line for the throne.

sentences.zh: 又以元德太子有三子，內常不安，陰挾左道，為厭勝事。

translations.literal: He also brooded that Crown Prince Yuande had three sons and was inwardly ill at ease; he secretly employed heterodox arts to perform rites of magical suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He also brooded that Crown Prince Yuande had three sons and was inwardly ill at ease. He secretly employed heterodox arts to perform rites of magical suppression.

sentences.zh: 至是，皆發。

translations.literal: At this point it all came to light.
translations.idiomatic: At this point it all came to light.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，斬令則等數人，妃姊賜死，暕府僚皆斥之邊遠。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged. He executed Lingze and several others, ordered the consort's elder sister to take her own life, and banished all of Jian's staff to remote regions.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly enraged. He executed Lingze and several others, ordered the consort's elder sister to take her own life, and banished all of Jian's staff to remote regions.

sentences.zh: 時趙王杲猶在孩孺，帝謂侍臣曰：「朕唯有暕一子，不然者，當肆諸市朝，以明國憲也。」

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Zhao Gao was still a child; the Emperor said to his attendants: "I have only Jian as a son — otherwise he would be exposed in the marketplace to make clear the law of the state."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince of Zhao Gao was still a child. The Emperor told his attendants, "I have only Jian as a son — otherwise I would have him exposed in the marketplace to make clear the law of the state."

sentences.zh: 暕自是恩寵日衰，雖為京尹，不復關預時政。

translations.literal: From then on Jian's favor daily waned; though he served as Metropolitan Governor, he no longer took part in affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Jian's favor waned daily. Though he served as Metropolitan Governor, he no longer took part in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 帝恆令武賁郎將一人監其府事，暕有微失，輒奏之。

translations.literal: The Emperor always assigned one officer of the Martial Tiger Guard to oversee his household affairs; at Jian's slightest fault he would report it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor always assigned one officer of the Martial Tiger Guard to oversee his household affairs. At Jian's slightest fault the officer would report it.

sentences.zh: 帝亦慮暕生變，所給左右，皆以老弱備員而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor also feared Jian might rebel; those assigned to attend him were all old and weak men kept on as mere placeholders.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also feared Jian might rebel. Those assigned to attend him were all old and weak men kept on as mere placeholders.

sentences.zh: 暼柬每懷危懼，心不自安。

translations.literal: Jian constantly felt dread and could not be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Jian constantly felt dread and could not be at ease.

sentences.zh: 又帝在江都宮元會，暕具法服將朝，無故有血從裳中而下；

translations.literal: Moreover, when the Emperor was at Jiangdu Palace for the New Year's assembly, Jian put on his ceremonial robes to attend court, and for no reason blood flowed down from within his robe;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the Emperor was at Jiangdu Palace for the New Year's assembly, Jian put on his ceremonial robes to attend court, and for no reason blood flowed down from within his robe;

sentences.zh: 又坐齋中，見群鼠數十，至前而死，視皆無頭。

translations.literal: again, while seated in his study he saw several dozen rats come forward and die; when he looked, all were headless.
translations.idiomatic: again, while seated in his study he saw several dozen rats come forward and die. When he looked, all were headless.

sentences.zh: 暕甚惡之。

translations.literal: Jian was deeply revolted by this.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was deeply revolted by this.

sentences.zh: 俄而化及作亂，兵將犯蹕，帝聞之，顧蕭後曰：「得非阿孩也？

translations.literal: Before long Huaji raised rebellion and troops were about to threaten the imperial progress; when the Emperor heard of it he turned to Empress Xiao and said: "Could it be Ahai?
translations.idiomatic: Before long Huaji raised rebellion and troops were about to threaten the imperial progress. When the Emperor heard of it he turned to Empress Xiao and said, "Could it be Ahai?

sentences.zh: 」其見疏忌如此。

translations.literal: Such was the degree to which he was distrusted and suspected.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the degree to which he was distrusted and suspected.

sentences.zh: 化及復令人捕暕，時尚臥未起，賊進，暕驚曰：「是何人？

translations.literal: Huaji again sent men to seize Jian; he was still in bed and had not risen when the rebels entered. Jian startled and said: "Who are you?
translations.idiomatic: Huaji again sent men to seize Jian. He was still in bed and had not risen when the rebels entered. Jian startled awake and cried, "Who are you?

sentences.zh: 」莫有報者。

translations.literal: No one answered him.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered him.

sentences.zh: 暕猶謂帝令捕之，曰：「詔使且緩，兒不負國家！

translations.literal: Jian still thought the Emperor had ordered his arrest and said: "Imperial envoy, wait a moment — your son has not betrayed the state!
translations.idiomatic: Jian still thought the Emperor had ordered his arrest and said, "Imperial envoy, wait a moment — your son has not betrayed the state!

sentences.zh: 」賊曳至街，斬之，及其二子亦遇害。

translations.literal: The rebels dragged him into the street and beheaded him; his two sons were killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dragged him into the street and beheaded him. His two sons were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 暕竟不知殺者為誰。

translations.literal: Jian never learned who his killers were.
translations.idiomatic: Jian never learned who his killers were.

sentences.zh: 時年三十四。

translations.literal: He was thirty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-four years old.

sentences.zh: 有遺腹子湣，與蕭後同入突厥，處羅可汗號為隋王。

translations.literal: He had a posthumous son Min, who entered the Turks together with Empress Xiao; Kaghan Chuluo styled him King of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He had a posthumous son Min, who entered the Turks together with Empress Xiao. Kaghan Chuluo styled him King of Sui.

sentences.zh: 中國人沒入北蕃者，悉配之以為部落，以定襄城處之。

translations.literal: Chinese who had been taken captive in the northern frontier were all assigned to him to form a tribe, and they were settled at Dingxiang city.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese taken captive in the northern frontier were all assigned to him to form a tribe and settled at Dingxiang city.

sentences.zh: 及突厥滅，乃獲之。

translations.literal: When the Turks were destroyed, he was at last recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks were destroyed, he was at last recovered.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，位至尚衣奉御，永徽初，卒。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he rose to Palace Attendant for Imperial Wardrobe; in the early Yonghui era he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era he rose to Palace Attendant for Imperial Wardrobe. In the early Yonghui era he died.

sentences.zh: 趙王杲，小字季子。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Gao had the childhood name Jizi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Gao had the childhood name Jizi.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，以大業九年封趙王。

translations.literal: At age seven, in the ninth year of Daye, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: At age seven, in the ninth year of Daye, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 尋授光祿大夫，曆河南尹，行江都太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, served as Metropolitan Governor of Henan, and acted as Administrator of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, served as Metropolitan Governor of Henan, and acted as Administrator of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 杲聰令，美容儀，帝有所制詞賦，杲多能誦之。

translations.literal: Gao was clever and quick-witted, with handsome features; whenever the Emperor composed lyrics or rhapsodies, Gao could often recite them from memory.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was clever and quick-witted, with handsome features. Whenever the Emperor composed lyrics or rhapsodies, Gao could often recite them from memory.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，嘗見帝風動，不進膳，杲亦終日不食。

translations.literal: His nature was utterly filial: once when he saw the Emperor troubled in spirit and refusing his meal, Gao also ate nothing all day.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was utterly filial. Once when he saw the Emperor troubled in spirit and refusing his meal, Gao also ate nothing all day.

sentences.zh: 又蕭後嘗灸，杲先請試炷，後不許之。

translations.literal: Again, when Empress Xiao was about to undergo moxibustion, Gao first asked to test the moxa cones; the empress would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Again, when Empress Xiao was about to undergo moxibustion, Gao first asked to test the moxa cones. The empress would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 杲泣請曰：「後所服藥，皆蒙嘗之。

translations.literal: Gao wept and begged, saying: "Whenever the Empress took medicine, I always tasted it first.
translations.idiomatic: Gao wept and begged, saying, "Whenever the Empress took medicine, I always tasted it first.

sentences.zh: 今灸，願聽嘗炷。

translations.literal: Now with moxibustion, I beg to be allowed to taste the cones.
translations.idiomatic: Now with moxibustion, I beg to be allowed to test the cones.

sentences.zh: 」悲咽不已。

translations.literal: He sobbed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He sobbed without cease.

sentences.zh: 後為停灸，由是尤鍾愛。

translations.literal: The empress thereupon stopped the moxibustion, and from this he was especially cherished.
translations.idiomatic: The empress thereupon stopped the moxibustion, and from this he was especially cherished.

sentences.zh: 後遇化及反，杲在帝側，號慟不已。

translations.literal: Later, when Huaji rebelled, Gao was at the Emperor's side and wailed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Huaji rebelled, Gao was at the Emperor's side and wailed without cease.

sentences.zh: 裴虔通使斬之帝前而血湔御服。

translations.literal: Pei Qiantong had him beheaded before the Emperor, and his blood spattered the imperial robes.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Qiantong had him beheaded before the Emperor, and his blood spattered the imperial robes.

sentences.zh: 時年十二。

translations.literal: He was twelve years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was twelve years old.

sentences.zh: 論曰：周建懿親，漢開磐石，內以敦睦九族，外以輯寧億兆，深根固本，崇獎王室，安則有以同其樂，衰則有以恤其危，所由來久矣。

translations.literal: Commentary: The Zhou established worthy kinsmen; the Han opened the bedrock policy — inwardly to harmonize the nine clans, outwardly to pacify the countless masses; to root deeply and strengthen the foundation, to honor and reward the royal house — in prosperity to share its joys, in decline to relieve its perils: this has been so for a very long time.
