translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Zhou established worthy kinsmen; the Han instituted the bedrock policy — inwardly to harmonize the nine clans, outwardly to pacify the countless masses; to root deeply and strengthen the foundation, to honor and reward the royal house — in prosperity to share its joys, in decline to relieve its perils. This has been so for a very long time.

sentences.zh: 自魏、晉已下，多失厥中，不遵王度，各徇所私。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin downward, many lost the mean, failed to observe royal norms, and each pursued private ends.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin downward, many lost the mean, failed to observe royal norms, and each pursued private ends.

sentences.zh: 抑之則勢齊於匹夫，抗之則權侔于萬乘，矯枉過正，非一時也。

translations.literal: Restrain them and their power equaled that of commoners; resist them and their authority rivaled that of the Son of Heaven — overcorrecting the fault was not limited to one age.
translations.idiomatic: Restrain them and their power equaled that of commoners; resist them and their authority rivaled that of the Son of Heaven. Overcorrecting the fault was not limited to one age.

sentences.zh: 得失詳于前史，不復究而論焉。

translations.literal: Gains and losses are detailed in earlier histories; I shall not examine and discuss them again here.
translations.idiomatic: Gains and losses are detailed in earlier histories; I shall not examine and discuss them again here.

sentences.zh: 隋文昆弟之恩，素非篤睦，閨房之隙，又不相容。

translations.literal: Among Emperor Wen's brothers, affection was never deeply harmonious, and rifts within the inner quarters were likewise intolerable.
translations.idiomatic: Among Emperor Wen's brothers, affection was never deeply harmonious, and rifts within the inner quarters were likewise intolerable.

sentences.zh: 至於二世承基，茲弊愈甚。

translations.literal: When the second emperor inherited the foundation, this evil grew all the worse.
translations.idiomatic: When the second emperor inherited the foundation, this evil grew all the worse.

sentences.zh: 是以滕穆暴薨，人皆竊議，蔡王將沒，自以為幸。

translations.literal: Hence when Prince Teng Mu died suddenly, men whispered in private; when Prince of Cai was near death, he counted himself fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Hence when Prince Teng Mu died suddenly, men whispered in private; when Prince of Cai was near death, he counted himself fortunate.

sentences.zh: 唯衛王養於獻後，故任遇特隆，而諸子遷流莫知死所，悲夫！

translations.literal: Only Prince of Wei, raised by Empress Dowager Wenxian, enjoyed extraordinary favor and appointment — while the other sons were exiled and none knew where they died. Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Only Prince of Wei, raised by Empress Dowager Wenxian, enjoyed extraordinary favor and appointment — while the other sons were exiled and none knew where they died. Alas!

sentences.zh: 其錫以茅土，稱為磐石，特無甲兵之衛，居與皁吏為伍。

translations.literal: Though enfeoffed with fief and styled bedrock, they had no guard of armed troops and dwelt among petty clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Though enfeoffed with fief and styled bedrock, they had no guard of armed troops and dwelt among petty clerks.

sentences.zh: 外內無虞，顛危不暇，時逢多難，將何望哉！

translations.literal: Inside and outside there was no one to guard them; before collapse could be remedied, the times met with many hardships — what could be hoped for!
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside there was no one to guard them. Before collapse could be remedied, the times met with one hardship after another — what could be hoped for!

sentences.zh: 河間屬乃葭莩，地非寵逼，故高位厚秩，與時終始。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hejian belonged to a distant branch of the clan and stood in no position of threatening favor; therefore he held high rank and generous stipends from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hejian belonged to a distant branch of the clan and stood in no position of threatening favor; therefore he held high rank and generous stipends from first to last.

sentences.zh: 楊慶二三其德，志在苟生，變本宗如反掌，棄慈母若遺跡，及身而絕，固宜然矣。

translations.literal: Yang Qing wavered in his loyalty and sought only to survive; he changed his allegiance to the founding house as easily as turning his hand, and abandoned his devoted mother as if casting off old tracks — that he perished in his own lifetime was only fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing wavered in his loyalty and sought only to survive. He changed his allegiance to the founding house as easily as turning his hand and abandoned his devoted mother as if casting off old tracks. That he perished in his own lifetime was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 文帝五子，莫有終其天年。

translations.literal: Of Emperor Wen's five sons, not one lived out his natural span.
translations.idiomatic: Of Emperor Wen's five sons, not one lived out his natural span.

sentences.zh: 房陵資於骨肉之親，篤於君臣之義，經綸締構，契闊夷險，撫軍臨國，凡二十年。

translations.literal: Prince Yong of Fangling was rich in kinship of bone and blood and steadfast in the righteousness of lord and minister; he governed statecraft, bound the realm together, shared hardship and ease, commanded armies and ruled the state — in all, twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Fangling was rich in kinship of bone and blood and steadfast in the righteousness of lord and minister. He governed statecraft, bound the realm together, shared hardship and ease, commanded armies and ruled the state — in all, twenty years.

sentences.zh: 雖三善未稱，而視膳無闕。

translations.literal: Though the three excellences of filial conduct were not fully achieved, he never failed in attending to his father's meals.
translations.idiomatic: Though the three excellences of filial conduct were not fully achieved, he never failed in attending to his father's meals.

sentences.zh: 恩寵既變，讒言間之，顧復之慈，頓隔於人理；

translations.literal: Once favor changed and slander came between them, the tender care of a parent's love was suddenly cut off by human reason;
translations.idiomatic: Once favor changed and slander came between them, the tender care of a parent's love was suddenly cut off by human reason;

sentences.zh: 父子之道，遂滅于天性，隋室將亡之效，眾庶皆知之矣。

translations.literal: the way of father and son was extinguished in natural affection — the sign that the house of Sui would perish was known to the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: the way of father and son was extinguished in natural affection. The sign that the house of Sui would perish was known to the multitude.

sentences.zh: 《慎子》曰：「一兔走街，百人逐之；

translations.literal: Master Shen said: "When one rabbit runs through the market, a hundred men chase it;
translations.idiomatic: Master Shen said, "When one rabbit runs through the market, a hundred men chase it;

sentences.zh: 積兔於市，過者不顧。

translations.literal: pile rabbits in the market and passersby do not glance at them."
translations.idiomatic: pile rabbits in the market and passersby do not glance at them."

sentences.zh: 」豈其無欲哉？

translations.literal: Is it that they have no desire?
translations.idiomatic: Is it that they have no desire?

sentences.zh: 分定故也。

translations.literal: It is because shares are fixed.
translations.idiomatic: It is because shares are fixed.

sentences.zh: 房陵分定久矣，而帝一朝易之，開逆亂之源，長覬覦之望。

translations.literal: Prince Yong of Fangling's share had long been fixed, yet the Emperor changed it in a single morning — opening the source of rebellion and lengthening the reach of covetous eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Fangling's share had long been fixed, yet the Emperor changed it in a single morning — opening the source of rebellion and lengthening the reach of covetous eyes.

sentences.zh: 又維城肇建，崇其威重，恃寵而驕，厚自封植，進之既逾制，退之不以道，俊以憂卒，實此之由。

translations.literal: Again, when the rampart prince was first established his prestige was exalted; relying on favor he grew proud, and he enriched himself lavishly — advancing him beyond regulation, retiring him without proper conduct — Jun died of grief, and this was truly the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Again, when the rampart prince was first established his prestige was exalted. Relying on favor he grew proud and enriched himself lavishly. Advancing him beyond regulation and retiring him without proper conduct — Jun died of grief, and this was truly the cause.

sentences.zh: 俄屬天步方艱，讒人已勝，尺布鬥粟，莫肯相容。

translations.literal: Soon heaven's step grew difficult; slanderers had prevailed; an inch of cloth and a peck of grain — none would yield to the other.
translations.idiomatic: Soon heaven's step grew difficult; slanderers had prevailed. An inch of cloth and a peck of grain — none would yield to the other.

sentences.zh: 秀窺岷、蜀之阻，諒起晉陽之甲，成茲亂常之釁，蓋亦有以動之也。

translations.literal: Xiu eyed the barriers of Min and Shu; Liang raised arms at Jinyang — thus were these breaches of order provoked; there was cause that moved them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu eyed the barriers of Min and Shu; Liang raised arms at Jinyang. Thus were these breaches of order provoked; there was cause that moved them.

sentences.zh: 《棠棣》之詩徒賦，有庳之封無期，或幽囚於囹圄，或顛殞於鳩毒。

translations.literal: The ode "Wild Cherry" in the Book of Songs was sung in vain; enfeoffment at Youbi never came to pass — some were imprisoned in jail, some perished by poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: The ode "Wild Cherry" in the Book of Songs was sung in vain; enfeoffment at Youbi never came to pass. Some were imprisoned in jail, some perished by poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 本根既絕，枝葉畢翦，十有餘年，宗社淪陷。

translations.literal: Once the root was severed, every branch was cut away; within little more than ten years the ancestral temple fell.
translations.idiomatic: Once the root was severed, every branch was cut away. Within little more than ten years the ancestral temple fell.

sentences.zh: 自古廢嫡立庶，覆族傾宗者多矣，考其亂亡之禍，未若有隋之酷。

translations.literal: From antiquity, those who deposed the legitimate heir and enthroned a lesser son — bringing ruin on clan and kindred — have been many; examine the calamity of disorder and extinction, and none has been as cruel as Sui's.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, those who deposed the legitimate heir and enthroned a lesser son — bringing ruin on clan and kindred — have been many. Examine the calamity of disorder and extinction, and none has been as cruel as Sui's.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「殷鑒不遠，在夏後之世。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Yin's mirror is not far off—it lies in the age of the lord of Xia."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says, "Yin's mirror is not far off—it lies in the age of the lord of Xia."

sentences.zh: 」後之有國有家者，可不深戒哉！

translations.literal: " Let those who hereafter possess a state or a clan take this as a profound warning!
translations.idiomatic: " Let every ruler and every great house hereafter take this as a profound warning!

sentences.zh: 元德謹重，有君人之量，降年不永，哀哉！

translations.literal: Yuande was careful and grave, with the measure of a ruler, yet his years were cut short—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Yuande was careful and dignified, with the bearing of a true sovereign, yet Heaven granted him few years—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 齊王敏慧可稱，志不及遠，頗懷驕僭，故帝疏而忌之，內無父子之親，貌展君臣之敬。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi was clever and quick and worthy of praise, but his aims did not reach far; he harbored considerable pride and presumption. Therefore the Emperor kept him at a distance and was wary of him—within there was no father-son intimacy, outwardly only the show of minister and lord.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi was clever and accomplished, yet his vision was short and his pride ran deep. The Emperor therefore kept him at arm's length and feared him: inwardly there was no true father-son bond, outwardly only the ceremony of lord and minister.

sentences.zh: 身非積善，國有餘殃，至令趙及燕、越，皆不得死，悲夫！

translations.literal: His person had not accumulated goodness, and the state bore lingering calamity; in the end even the Princes of Zhao, Yan, and Yue could not die in peace—how tragic!
translations.idiomatic: He had not piled up virtue in his own person, and the dynasty bore the aftershocks; in the end even the Princes of Zhao, Yan, and Yue were denied a natural death—how tragic!
